UT: [Invariant] SrtpPolicy Disabled is the only variant valid when srtp feature is off — Mandatory and Optional must always be rejected
UT: [Invariant] GetAccountInfo is always Permitted during shutdown; ConfConnect and ConfDisconnect are always Rejected — the classification is immutable per variant
UT: [Invariant] ReconnectPolicy field accessors return construction-time values (base_delay, max_delay, jitter_ratio are immutable after construction)
testIntegration: IT: [Integration point] CodecAutoMode::apply to SipClient::configure_codecs — the auto-mode result feeds into the per-account codec configuration pipeline where pjsua_codec_set_priority FFI calls apply the priority map
IT: [Integration point] SrtpPolicy::validate to ClientConfig::validate — SRTP validation is invoked during ClientConfig::validate() to enforce feature-gating before transport initialization

IT: [Integration point] ShutdownCommandRouter::classify to CoreReactor::dispatch_command — the router output drives reactor behavior: Permit routes to execute_get_account_info, Reject routes to reject_command with error
IT: [Integration point] ReconnectPolicy to TransportManager::reconnect — the delay calculation feeds into transport-layer retry timer scheduling
testExceptions: Exception — CodecAutoMode::apply FFI call to pjsua_codec_set_priority: Reason: The actual FFI binding (pjsua_codec_set_priority) is not available until P2-4 when the FFI layer is built. The FFI side-effect call cannot test — it requires a working PJSIP installation and FFI bindings. However, the codec priority assignment logic (mapping codec_id to priority value) is fully testable without FFI. This is not a design defect — the pure function design intentionally separates computation from side effects so that the priority mapping is testable now and the FFI binding can be added later as a thin integration layer. Alternative verification: The apply function returns the priority map as a HashMap<String, u8> which is fully asserted in unit tests across all codec combinations.

Exception — ShutdownCommandRouter::classify integrating with CoreReactor: Reason: The dispatcher integration requires a running reactor with shutdown state machine, which makes end-to-end testing impossible to test in pure unit context. This is not a design defect — the pure function design of classify() allows exhaustive unit testing of all routing decisions independently of reactor state. The reactor integration is a thin dispatch wrapper. Alternative verification: The pure function classify() is covered exhaustively by unit tests (all RuntimeCommand variants x 2 shutdown states). Reactor dispatch integration is tested via existing dispatch_command tests in runtime/reactor.rs.

Exception — Transport reconnection integration with PJSIP transport layer: Reason: ReconnectPolicy produces delay values, but actual reconnection orchestration (socket creation, TLS handshake retry, timer scheduling) requires PJSIP transport lifecycle which is not testable until P2-4+. This is not a design defect — the computation of retry delays is independent of transport lifecycle, and the pure function design allows full testing of the delay algorithm now. Alternative verification: ReconnectPolicy::next_delay is fully validated as a pure function across all attempt/jitter combinations.
acceptanceCriteria: Happy path: A SipClient is created with default config (preferred_codecs empty). configure_codecs_auto_mode assigns Opus=255, PCMU=254, others=0. All SrtpPolicy::validate calls with feature enabled pass. During shutdown, GetAccountInfo is permitted and returns AccountInfoSnapshot. ConfConnect and ConfDisconnect are rejected with InvalidState.

Error case: SrtpPolicy::validate is called with Mandatory when srtp feature flag is disabled — returns Err(InvalidConfig). ShutdownCommandRouter::classify is called with ConfConnect during shutdown — returns Reject(InvalidState) with message containing 'shutting down'.

Edge case: preferred_codecs contains an explicitly-specified codec but is non-empty — CodecAutoMode::apply produces an empty priority map (auto mode bypassed). preferred_codecs is empty and enumerate_codecs returns an empty list — apply returns Ok(()) with empty map. ReconnectPolicy::next_delay with attempt=0 and base_delay=1s returns exactly 1s (no backoff yet). jitter_ratio=1.0 produces delay in [0, 2*computed] range.

tickets.invariants:
- 【Normal establishment】When preferred_codecs is empty, CodecAutoMode::apply assigns Opus=255, PCMU=254, and all other codecs=0. When preferred_codecs is non-empty, auto mode is bypassed (no priorities changed).
- 【Normal establishment】SrtpPolicy::validate returns Ok(()) when: Disabled (always valid) or Mandatory/Optional with srtp feature enabled.
- 【Normal establishment】During shutdown, ShutdownCommandRouter::classify returns Permit for GetAccountInfo and Reject(InvalidState) for media commands.
- 【On error】SrtpPolicy::validate must never panic or crash — it always returns Result<(), SipError> with InvalidConfig kind for feature violations.
- 【On error】If enumerate_codecs() fails, CodecAutoMode::apply must propagate the error without partial priority assignment.
- 【On error】ReconnectPolicy::new must reject invalid parameters (zero base_delay, out-of-range jitter_ratio) at construction time, never at next_delay call time.
- 【Internal state】ReconnectPolicy fields (base_delay, max_delay, jitter_ratio) are immutable after construction — no setter methods provided.
- 【Internal state】ShutdownCommandRouter has no mutable state — classify() is a pure function of (cmd, is_shutting_down).
- 【Boundary】Codec priority values are u8: Opus=255 (max valid priority), PCMU=254, others=0 (disabled). These exact values are invariants.
- 【Boundary】jitter_ratio must be in [0.0, 1.0] — values outside this range are rejected at construction.

tickets.investigation:
Investigation evidence gathered from RFC graph (N0041, N0042, N0044, N0040, N0043, N0015) and source code (src/config/m20_codec_auto_mode.rs, src/config/srtp_transport_reconnect.rs, src/error/m20_shutdown_routing.rs, src/config/codec_policy_fallback.rs, src/runtime/command.rs, src/error/error_design_siperror.rs, src/error/m20_runtime_command_error.rs, src/config.rs, src/lib.rs):

1. N0041 (Codec Auto Mode): Two-layer selection — preferred_codecs non-empty = explicit mode, empty = auto mode (Opus=255, PCMU=254). The configure_codecs() function in RFC uses pjsua_codec_set_priority FFI. Parent N0040 defines CodecSelectionPolicy (Ordered/PreferOpusFallbackPcmu) and NegotiatedCodec enum. The CallMediaPreferences struct is defined in N0040 parent but not yet implemented — P1-1 only implements the auto-mode computation, not the full CallMediaPreferences struct.

2. N0042 (SRTP & Transport Reconnection): SrtpPolicy enum (Disabled/Optional/Mandatory) with feature-gating via bool flag (not #[cfg] in function body). ReconnectPolicy with exponential backoff: base_delay * 2^attempt, clamped by max_delay, with jitter_ratio randomization. Transport protocol distinction: UDP stateless (no reconnect), TCP/TLS connection-oriented (reconnect needed). Parent N0015 defines TransportConfig enum with Udp/Tcp/Tls variants. The actual transport lifecycle (create, reconnect, destroy) is in N0015's domain and deferred to P2-4.

3. N0044 (Shutdown Routing): Three M20 RuntimeCommand variants: GetAccountInfo (permitted — read-only), ConfConnect (rejected — media mutation), ConfDisconnect (rejected — media mutation). Pure routing function with no reactor state dependence. Uses SipError::invalid_state("shutting down") from error_design_siperror. Parent N0043 defines the shutdown state machine (idempotent, cancels calls, unregisters, drains audio, destroys). The RuntimeCommand enum is already defined in src/runtime/command.rs (P0-6) with all three variants. The error converters (convert_conf_connect_error, convert_conf_disconnect_error, convert_get_account_info_error) are already implemented in src/error/m20_runtime_command_error.rs (P0-4).

4. Existing source state: All three target files are stubs (pub struct Config {}, pub enum Error {}) with [::STUB::] markers. The files have the Initial Design Artifact header. Module declarations exist in src/config.rs and src/error.rs with pub mod statements. No existing implementations to modify.

5. Key architecture decision: ShutdownCommandRouter is placed in src/error/m20_shutdown_routing.rs (error_policy module per the graph), not in runtime/. This keeps routing logic separate from reactor mechanics. The Reactor's dispatch_command calls classify() and acts on the ShutdownCommandAction result — this is the integration point tested in testIntegration.
tickets.boyScoutPlan:
Translatability improvements for P1-1 (applied to code touched by this ticket):

1. Function names as verb phrases: apply() for CodecAutoMode (applies auto-mode priorities), validate() for SrtpPolicy (validates policy against feature flag), classify() for ShutdownCommandRouter (classifies command during shutdown), next_delay() for ReconnectPolicy (computes next retry delay). All are imperative verbs describing the action.

2. Variable names as domain concepts: codec_id (not "id" or "codec"), preferred_codecs (not "pc" or "list"), jitter_ratio (not "j" or "r"), native_acc_id (matches existing RuntimeCommand field name), is_shutting_down (boolean flag with is_ prefix per coding standards).

3. One function, one responsibility: CodecAutoMode::apply only computes priority map (no FFI, no state mutation). SrtpPolicy::validate only validates (no side effects). ShutdownCommandRouter::classify only routes (no execution). ReconnectPolicy::next_delay only computes delay (no timer scheduling).

4. Named constants: OPUS_PRIORITY = 255, PCMU_PRIORITY = 254 extracted as constants rather than magic numbers. No hardcoded values in function bodies.

5. No error swallowing: All functions return Result<_, SipError> (not Result<_, ()>). Error messages include diagnostic context (codec_id for FFI errors, policy variant for validation errors, cmd variant for shutdown routing).

6. Existing code left cleaner: The three stub files currently have `pub struct Config {}` and `pub enum Error {}` with generic names and no real content. P1-1 replaces these with properly named types. No additional existing code is touched.

tickets.background:
N0046 defines tracing spans for all public operations and optional metrics feature. N0047 defines security (SecretString, Authorization redaction) and platform differences (Windows MSVC, macOS frameworks, Linux libs). N0050 defines optional cpal-input feature and complete usage examples for client init, account management, calling, audio tap, and AI TTS.

### Goal
Add tracing instrumentation to all public operations, implement SecretString for credential safety, define ClientCapabilities as part of the initialization protocol, document platform-specific build requirements, and provide comprehensive usage examples.

### Purpose
Observability ensures debuggability of production SIP calls; SecretString prevents accidental credential leaks via log output (investigating an incident should never expose passwords); ClientCapabilities enables consumers to adapt their feature usage to what the runtime supports; platform documentation reduces build friction across three target OSes.

### Motivation
Without tracing, diagnosing call failures in production is guesswork. Without SecretString, any error-format! or Debug-impl on AuthCredentials leaks the password to logs. Without ClientCapabilities, consumers cannot determine at runtime whether ICE, SRTP, or a specific codec is available. These gaps block the first production deployment of siprs.

### Constraints
Must work with existing SipClient facade (P0-3) and EventBus (P0-5). SecretString must be zeroize-compatible but optional (behind zeroize feature). All types must be serde-compatible (behind serde feature) for WebSocket serialization (P4-4). tracing spans must not change public API signatures. cpal-input is optional and non-default.

Implementation files: src/config/observability_metrics.rs, src/security/security_platform_diffs.rs

- [Implementation steps] (1) Wire observability_metrics module into config.rs tree (add `pub mod observability_metrics`). (2) Implement ClientCapabilities struct with all 20+ fields in observability_metrics.rs — derive Debug, Clone, Serialize. (3) Add ClientInitialized event variant to SipEventPayload that carries ClientCapabilities. (4) Wire security module into lib.rs tree (add `pub mod security`). (5) Implement SecretString newtype with Display/Debug redaction and Zeroize behind feature flag. (6) Replace password type in AuthCredentials (config.rs) with SecretString. (7) Add RawSipMessage::redact_authorization() method to event_model_payload_bus.rs. (8) Add #[tracing::instrument(skip(...))] on all public SipClient methods. (9) Implement MetricsRegistry behind #[cfg(feature = "metrics")]. (10) Write unit tests for all new types. (11) Add doc-examples behind spec-examples feature gate.

- [Risks] SecretString serde integration: password must be serializable/deserializable for persistence, but Display must never show it. Use #[serde(serialize_with = "...")] to preserve inner value for serialization while hiding via Display. Metrics registry thread-safety: dashmap provides lock-free concurrent access, but counter increment order matters for correctness in multi-task contexts. Use AtomicU64 per counter for lock-free increments.

- [Caveats] ClientCapabilities is a snapshot at init time — capabilities may change during runtime (e.g., transport reconnection). The RFC specifies it's emitted once in ClientInitialized. Consumers must not treat it as dynamic. SecretString with zeroize feature adds ~3KB to binary size. Feature gating via cfg-if keeps cost conditional.

- [Open items] RawSipMessage redact_authorization currently only supports SIP Authorization: header format. Should it also handle Proxy-Authorization: and WWW-Authenticate? RFC N0047 mentions "Authorization header" only. Deferring Proxy-Authorization to P2-6. Platform-specific build notes in security_platform_diffs.rs are documentation-only — actual build.rs cfg implementation is in P3-5.

- [Future improvements] Once cpal crate is added in P1-3 (P1-4), open_default_microphone_source() can be fully implemented. ClientCapabilities could be extended with runtime-query capability (e.g., query_pjsua_for_codecs()) once FFI bindings exist in P2-4.

## Translatability improvements (Boy Scout Rule)

### 1. src/config/observability_metrics.rs — Complete rewrite
**Current**: Empty stub with `pub struct Config {}` — no translatability (does nothing).
**Target**: Define `ClientCapabilities`, `MetricsRegistry`, `MetricsCounter`, `MetricsGauge` types with function names as verb phrases (`register_counter`, `increment_counter`, `initialize_metrics`), struct names as domain concepts (`ClientCapabilities`, `AudioDeviceCaps`, `SrtpImplementation`). One type per logical responsibility: ClientCapabilities is a capability matrix, MetricsRegistry is a counter/gauge store, AudioDeviceCaps describes device enumeration.

### 2. src/security/security_platform_diffs.rs — Complete rewrite
**Current**: `pub fn authorize() {}` with TODO comment — empty body, violates No-Justification Rule.
**Target**: Define `SecretString` newtype with `impl fmt::Display` (redacts), `impl Debug` (redacts), Conditional `impl Zeroize` (zeroizes on drop). Function names: `SecretString::new()`, `SecretString::as_str()` (unwraps for controlled access). Extract hardcoded "[REDACTED]" into a named constant `REDACTED_DISPLAY`.

### 3. src/api/event_model_payload_bus.rs — Add redact_authorization() to RawSipMessage
**Current**: RawSipMessage is a bare `pub data: Vec<u8>` wrapper — no methods, no type safety.
**Target**: Add `impl RawSipMessage { pub fn redact_authorization(&self) -> Self; }` — method name is a verb phrase describing the action. Return a new instance (immutable pattern) rather than mutating in place.

### 4. src/config.rs — Replace AuthCredentials.password String with SecretString
**Current**: `pub password: String` with STUB comment. Violates C048 invariant (SecretString for passwords).
**Target**: Change type to `SecretString` (via `zeroize`). The Authenticate flow reads as: "construct credentials with a password that is zeroed on drop; use the password only through controlled accessor; display never leaks value."

### 5. Extract hardcoded test feature strings into constants
**Current**: Feature names are referenced inline in tests (e.g., client.rs tests compare against string literals like "cpal-input").
**Target**: Define `const FEATURE_CPAL_INPUT: &str = "cpal-input"` in a `features` constants module for test reuse.

tickets.background:
### Goal
Create siprs-server as a separate crate from siprs with Axum-based HTTP/WS API, establish MIT/Apache 2.0 dual-licensing with GPL linking exception, implement JWT authentication middleware, and define Layer 5 API integration tests.

### Purpose
This ticket achieves the architectural separation of the SIP client library (siprs) from the HTTP/WebSocket API server (siprs-server). The split enables: (1) Tauri embedding without HTTP dependencies, (2) independent evolution of client and server crates, (3) clean dependency boundaries with siprs-server depending exclusively on siprs, never the inverse. JWT auth provides production-grade API security. Layer 5 tests ensure API correctness end-to-end.

### Motivation
Current state is a single crate with stub-only HTTP/WS types. External consumers (Tauri app, CLI tools, SDK clients) need a proper HTTP API. Without the split, all consumers would pay the cost of axum/tokio-tungstenite dependencies. Without JWT auth, the API can only listen on localhost — insecure for production. Layer 5 tests are needed before any REST/WS endpoint can be verified.

### Constraints
1) siprs must remain a pure library crate — zero HTTP/WS dependencies. 2) siprs-server must not create circular dependencies. 3) License must accommodate PJSIP's GPL v2 while keeping siprs MIT/Apache 2.0. 4) JWT must use SIP account credentials (not external OAuth) to maintain decentralized identity model. 5) No real PJSIP FFI calls in this ticket — all SIP operations use mock/stub.
scope: Crate split: siprs (pure SIP client library) + siprs-server (HTTP/WS API with Axum)
siprs-server Cargo.toml: depends on siprs (serde feature), axum, tokio-tungstenite, jsonwebtoken, rusqlite, sea-orm
siprs feature flags: default=[], serde, tls, srtp (no HTTP deps in siprs itself)
License goal: MIT/Apache 2.0 dual-license with GPL linking exception for PJSIP
Multi-instance: first SipClient::new() creates PjsuaBackend singleton, subsequent share it

acceptanceCriteria: siprs and siprs-server are separate crates with correct dependency direction
JWT auth works end-to-end: issue, validate, reject invalid tokens
Layer 5 tests pass for REST and WebSocket endpoints
License header is present in all source files

Happy path: User starts siprs-server with default config (localhost:3910, no auth). GET /api/v1/health returns 200. POST /api/v1/auth/token with valid SIP credentials returns JWT. Using that JWT, GET /api/v1/accounts returns 200 with account list. Full JWT round-trip passes.

Error case: User calls GET /api/v1/accounts without Authorization header -> 401 Unauthorized. User calls with expired/invalid JWT -> 401 Unauthorized. User starts with AuthMode::LocalhostOnly but binds to 0.0.0.0 -> startup error.
Edge case: JWT exp=0 is rejected as expired. Sequence numbers wrap from u64::MAX to 0. AuthFrameHeader padding bytes are zero. AuthConfig::validate() rejects Jwt mode without jwt_secret.

tickets.notes:
- [Implementation steps] Step 1: Create siprs-server crate directory structure (Cargo.toml, src/lib.rs, src/main.rs, tests/, migrations/). Step 2: Add siprs-server to root workspace Cargo.toml. Step 3: Move HTTP-related types (ServerConfig/AuthConfig/AuthMode) from siprs stubs to siprs-server, re-export from siprs. Step 4: Implement auth_jwt_middleware.rs (JwtValidator, Claims, AxumJWTAuthLayer, AxumJWTAuthMiddleware). Step 5: Implement standalone_server_config.rs (ServerConfig, AuthConfig, AuthMode, validate()). Step 6: Implement http_ws_protocol.rs (REST path constants, AudioFrameHeader, seq types). Step 7: Add license headers to all source files and create LICENSE exception text. Step 8: Declare Layer 5 test structure in test_apilayer5.rs.
- [Risks] Crate split may break existing imports if ServerConfig/AuthConfig paths change. Risk: moderate — current consumers are stubs. Migration: re-export from siprs:: so existing import paths still work. JWT crate (jsonwebtoken) API may differ between versions — pin to known-good version in Cargo.toml.
- [Caveats] AxumJWTAuthLayer interception of /health and /auth/token must be excluded explicitly via RouteLayered or skip predicate. WebSocket upgrade with JWT query param requires separate handling (RFC 6750 recommends header, but browser WebSocket API can only set headers via protocols/constructor).
- [Open items] Exact version pinning for axum, jsonwebtoken, tokio-tungstenite, rusqlite, sea-orm dependencies deferred to P4-3. Multi-instance PjsuaBackend singleton mechanism (OnceCell/OnceLock) design deferred to P2-4 (FFI integration). WebSocket audio binary frame handler implementation deferred to P4-4.
- [Future improvements] Introduce utoipa for OpenAPI doc generation from route handlers. Add AuthMode::TlsClientCert for mTLS authentication. Implement JWT refresh token flow. Add rate-limiting middleware.

tickets.invariants:
- [Normal establishment condition] 1) siprs crate has zero HTTP/WS dependencies (axum, tokio-tungstenite, jsonwebtoken, rusqlite, sea-orm are in siprs-server only). 2) siprs-server Cargo.toml declares siprs as a dependency. 3) Each .rs file across both crates carries the license header. 4) AuthConfig::default().mode == AuthMode::LocalhostOnly. 5) JWT Claims round-trip preserves username, domain, sub, exp, scope fields.
- [Invariant on error] 1) JWT validation failure (expired, wrong secret, malformed) never panics — always returns typed Err. 2) AuthConfig::validate() failure always returns detailed validation error message. 3) ServerConfig deserialization failure does not leave partial config in memory. 4) License header verification failure (build.rs check) produces compile-time error, never runtime panic.
- [Internal state invariant] 1) JwtValidator stores immutable secret key — once constructed, secret is never mutated. 2) AuthMode enum is exhaustive — no catch-all (_) match arms. 3) ServerConfig auth field is always validated before use via AuthConfig::validate(). 4) AudioFrameHeader is repr(C, packed) with exactly 24 bytes.
- [Boundary invariant] 1) JWT exp field at 0 = rejected as expired. 2) Sequence number at u64::MAX wraps to 0 via wrapping_add. 3) AudioFrameHeader::reserved field is [0u8; 4]. 4) AuthConfig::LocalhostOnly rejects bind addresses other than 127.0.0.1.
tickets.instrumentation:
- [Logging] JWT auth failures (expired, invalid signature, malformed token) logged via tracing::warn! with structured fields (reason, client_ip). Successful token issuance logged via tracing::info!. Axum middleware uses tracing::instrument for each request. ServerConfig validation failures logged via tracing::error!.
- [Metrics] Auth failure counter (auth_failures_total) keyed by failure reason. Token issuance counter (token_issued_total). Active WebSocket connections gauge (ws_connections_active). Crate split means metrics are defined in siprs-server, not siprs.
- [Error tracking] JwtError enum defines typed errors: Expired, InvalidSignature, Malformed, MissingHeader. All JWT errors map to HTTP 401 Unauthorized with structured JSON body {"error":"unauthorized","detail":"expired token"}. ServerConfig validation errors map to 500 InternalServerError at startup.
- [Health check] GET /api/v1/health returns 200 OK with {"status":"ok","version":"..."} without authentication. Health check route is excluded from JWT auth layer. siprs-server readiness depends on siprs SipClient initialization success.

contracts.precondition: Acceptance criteria must be enumerable as 12 items covering: build success, prebuilt detection, multi-account registration/unregister, transport creation, codec listing, DTMF send/receive, event subscribe, audio chunk access, API unification check, Send+Sync on SipClient. Input schema: each criterion is a boolean predicate verified via test assertion.
contracts.postcondition: lib.rs template compiles with all module declarations (client, config, account, call, transport, event, error, api, runtime, security, build, tests) and re-exports all public types. Output assertion: `pub use` for ServerConfig, AuthConfig, AuthMode, SipClient, ClientConfig, SipError, SipErrorKind, SecretString, EventBus, SipEvent, SipEventPayload, NativeEvent all resolve at compile time.
contracts.invariant: All 12 acceptance criteria must pass for ticket completion. Verified via `#[test]` assertions — a regression test suite must exist that exercises each criterion. New acceptance criteria cannot be added without corresponding test.

contracts.precondition: RFC design document must be complete — all graph nodes (N0002 through N0067) must have concrete implementation file assignments or explicit deferred status. Input schema: query RFC-ROOT-GRAPH.json and verify every node has an implementation file path or has `[::STUB::]` marker.

contracts.precondition: Server crate (siprs-server) must be separated from core (siprs). The crate boundary defines that siprs-server depends on siprs but not vice versa. Input schema: Cargo.toml of siprs-server must list `siprs = { path = ".." }` as dependency.
contracts.postcondition: Standalone server mode defined: ServerConfig struct with bind_addr (default 127.0.0.1:3910), db_path, config_file, allowed_origins, auth fields. AuthConfig with mode (LocalhostOnly/ApiKey/Jwt), jwt_secret Option, jwt_expiry_secs default 3600. Output assertion: ServerConfig implements Default + Send + Sync. AuthConfig::default().mode == AuthMode::LocalhostOnly.
contracts.invariant: AuthConfig defaults to LocalhostOnly. Verified via `assert_eq!(AuthConfig::default().mode, AuthMode::LocalhostOnly)`. If auth mode enum gets new variants, the match guard in `validate()` must be updated (verified via exhaustiveness check test).

contracts.precondition: Server mode (ServerConfig) must be defined with bind_addr and auth settings before HTTP/WS layer can bind to it. Input schema: build_router() accepts AppState { sip_client, db } and returns axum::Router. The router must include all 20 endpoints (18 REST + 2 WS).
contracts.postcondition: REST protocol specifies 18 endpoint constants (PATH_AUTH_TOKEN through PATH_SHUTDOWN) as `&str`. WebSocket protocol specifies 2 endpoint constants (PATH_WS, PATH_WS_AUDIO). AudioFrameHeader is repr(C,packed) 30-byte struct with sequence_number (u64), timestamp_ms (u64), frame_ms (u16), sample_rate (u16), channels (u8), bits_per_sample (u8), call_id (u32), reserved ([u8;4]). Output assertion: each path constant matches RFC spec. AudioFrameHeader size_of == 30.
contracts.invariant: Event-audio correlation via sequence numbers: both SipEvent.seq and AudioFrameHeader.sequence_number are u64. Verified via compile-time type assertion: `let _: u64 = event.seq; let _: u64 = header.sequence_number;`. Wrapping behavior defined: u64 wrapping_add.

contracts.precondition: API protocol paths must be defined before JWT middleware can be applied to them. Input schema: JWT middleware is applied as axum::Layer to a subset of routes (not /health, not /auth/token).
contracts.postcondition: JWT auth model specified: AuthMode::Jwt requires jwt_secret to be Some. AuthConfig.validate() returns ConfigError::JwtRequiresSecret if Jwt mode with no secret. Output assertion: validate() with Jwt + None secret returns Err. With Some(secret) returns Ok.
contracts.invariant: Default auth mode is LocalhostOnly (localhost-only listening). Verified via assert. If non-localhost address used with LocalhostOnly, validate() returns ConfigError::LocalhostRequiresLoopback.

contracts.precondition: Server mode defined with db_path before SQLite persistence can bind to it. Input schema: db_path in ServerConfig is used as DatabasePool::open() argument. PathBuf path must be valid for platform.
contracts.postcondition: SQLite schema specified: 4 tables (accounts, transport_configs, client_settings, tls_configs) with column types matching RFC S56. tickets.background:
## Goal
Define and implement the siprs-server crate specification: standalone server mode (ServerConfig, AuthConfig, AuthMode), HTTP/WS protocol layer (18 REST endpoints + 2 WebSocket paths + AudioFrameHeader binary protocol), SQLite persistence schema (4 tables via SeaORM + rusqlite bundled), semver/networking reference information (versioning policy, TLS cert info, DNS delegation), and lib.rs module/export declarations — all as specified by RFC nodes N0057, N0058, N0061, N0062, N0064, N0066, N0067.

## Purpose
This ticket transforms the RFC design for the server crate into concrete implementation artifacts: the config structs and protocol data structures that form the foundation of siprs-server. These types are the layer-5 (API layer) building blocks that downstream tickets (P4-3 route handlers, P4-4 WS handlers, P4-5 SQLite DAO) depend on. Without this ticket, no server-mode code can compile.

## Motivation
The siprs crate core (layer 1-4) is fully specified and partially implemented (P0/P1/P2-2 accomplished). The server mode is the next architectural layer needed for the zasso ecosystem to provide a network-accessible SIP API. Multiple downstream tickets (P4-series) are blocked on these type definitions. Additionally, the current source tree has `[::STUB::]` markers in sqlite_schema.rs and semver_sip_networking.rs that must be resolved.

## Constraints
- Crate uses rusqlite bundled feature (no system SQLite dependency). This must be reflected in Cargo.toml.
- SeaORM migration management must follow the Makefile convention from mycute project.
- AudioFrameHeader must use repr(C,packed) for ABI stability across Rust version upgrades (current size discovered: 30 bytes, not 24 as originally specified — spec correction needed).
- AuthMode enum has exactly 3 variants (LocalhostOnly, ApiKey, Jwt) — variant count invariant enforced by test.
- ServerConfig must at minimum derive Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize for config file loading.
- DEFAULT_SIPRS_PORT = 3910 — must match the zasso ecosystem port convention (RT_PORT = 3910).

acceptanceCriteria:
## Happy path — Standalone server configuration and protocol type definitions are complete:
1. ServerConfig, AuthConfig, AuthMode compile with Default, Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize, Send, Sync traits
2. All 20 API path constants (18 REST + 2 WS) compile as &str and match RFC S54
3. AudioFrameHeader is repr(C,packed) with size_of() == 30 bytes, implements Send + Sync
4. SQLite schema entities compile for all 4 tables (accounts, transport_configs, client_settings, tls_configs)
5. Semver policy constants and TLS info types compile in semver_sip_networking.rs
6. All 12 unit tests from testUnit pass, all 4 integration tests from testIntegration pass
7. Sequence number monotonicity verified across 1M iterations

## Error case — Configuration validation rejects invalid input:
1. AuthConfig::validate() returns ConfigError::LocalhostRequiresLoopback when LocalhostOnly + non-loopback address
2. AuthConfig::validate() returns ConfigError::JwtRequiresSecret when Jwt + missing jwt_secret
3. Invalid AudioFrameHeader field values store correctly (no panic) — struct is a passthrough format
4. Missing db_path causes DatabasePool::open() to return Err (not panic)
5. Build succeeds with `no-default-features` — SQLite dependency is optional behind feature flag

## Edge case — Boundary values handled correctly:
1. AudioFrameHeader with u64::MAX sequence_number and u64::MAX timestamp_ms round-trips correctly through bytes
2. Sequence number wraps at u64::MAX to 0 (wrapping_add), no panic or duplicate
3. AuthMode all 3 variants exhaustively matchable (compile-time guard via match)
4. ServerConfig with empty allowed_origins builds successfully (CORS disabled)
5. SQLite :memory: database path can be used for testing

tickets.notes:
## Implementation steps:
1. Add SQLite dependencies (rusqlite bundled, sea-orm sqlite) to Cargo.toml
2. Implement src/model/sqlite_schema.rs with SeaORM entities for 4 tables
3. Implement src/config/semver_sip_networking.rs with versioning policy constants and TLS info types
4. Add safe AudioFrameHeader::to_bytes() and ::from_bytes() methods in http_ws_protocol.rs
5. Expand test coverage in all affected files — match testUnit spec exactly
6. Fix lying comments in http_ws_protocol.rs tests (24-byte comment → 30-byte)
7. Verify re-exports in lib.rs and config.rs
8. Update CHANGELOG.md unreleased section

## Risks:
- AudioFrameHeader size discrepancy (RFC says 24, actual 30) could cause wire incompatibility if other implementations match RFC literally. Must document this clearly.
- sea-orm with sqlite may add significant compile time. Consider Feature flag gating SQLite-heavy features behind a `sqlite-storage` feature.
- The event_id vs seq field ambiguity in EventMeta/SipEvent could cause confusion in sequence number usage between P2-3 and P4-4.

## Caveats:
- The 30-byte AudioFrameHeader is the actual compiled size (verified by existing tests). The RFC documentation should be updated to match.
- rusqlite bundled feature statically links SQLite — increases binary size by ~1MB but eliminates system dependency.
- Makefile migration commands (gen-migration, migrate-up, etc.) are defined at the workspace level, not in this crate.

## Open items:
- Whether to declare `pub mod model;` in lib.rs or keep model as a private implementation module. Decision: make it private until the crate split (B1 boundary).
- Whether SeaORM migrations should live in siprs or siprs-server crate. Decision: migrations live with sqlite_schema.rs in siprs (types), executed in siprs-server.

## Future improvements:
- After crate split (B1), siprs-core removes SQLite dependency entirely; siprs-server owns the database layer.
- After 1.0 release, add cargo semver-checks CI step per C067 invariant.
- Consider zerocopy crate for safe AudioFrameHeader byte reinterpretation instead of manual to_bytes/from_bytes.

       - Function name: `to_bytes` (verb phrase: "convert header to wire-format bytes")
       - Function name: `from_bytes` (verb phrase: "construct header from wire-format bytes")

tickets.background:
N0011 defines the complete public API surface (crate root re-exports, SipClient, SipAccountHandle, OutgoingCallRequest). N0014 and N0015 define AccountConfig, TransportConfig with ICE/STUN/TURN specs. N0051 defines config validation rules (fail-fast). These form the user-facing configuration and API layer.

### Goal
Establish the complete, stable public API surface (SipClient, SipAccountHandle, AccountConfig, TransportConfig) for the siprs crate. All user-facing interactions with the SIP stack go through these types. Every public item is re-exported at crate root so application code writes siprs::SipClient not siprs::client::SipClient.

### Purpose
The public API is the contract between siprs and its consumers. Without a defined API surface, all internal refactoring breaks downstream code silently. By fixing the types, method signatures, validation rules, and re-exports in this ticket, we establish a stable foundation that downstream tickets (P3-2 FFI, P4-1 IDs, P5-1 Call lifecycle) can build on.

### Motivation
Existing code uses raw u64/String placeholders in RuntimeCommand and stub structs (account.rs, call.rs, transport.rs all have stub pattern). Before FFI bindings (P3-2) can be integrated, the typed API layer must exist so the FFI layer calls typed methods rather than manipulating raw pjsua handles. Additionally, the current src/config.rs ClientConfig is a simplified proxy-only config — the full N0013/N0014/N0015 configs must replace it.

### Constraints
(1) No PJSUA FFI dependency — all validation and API surface must work with MockBackend at Layer 2. (2) TLS variants are feature-gated behind #[cfg(feature = "tls")] — the public API must not expose TLS types when the feature is off. (3) SecretString via zeroize feature for password fields — memory zeroization is optional but the SecretString wrapper is mandatory. (4) Existing test in client.rs references old ClientConfig builder API with sip_proxy_host/sip_proxy_port — P3-1 must either update or deprecate these tests.

testExceptions: Exception: Feature-gated TLS variant compile-time presence — TransportConfig::Tls variant exists only when #[cfg(feature = "tls")] is active. This is a compile-time gate, not a runtime behavior, and is deterministic — the Rust compiler performs conditional compilation based on feature flags. However, a single test binary cannot test both presence and absence of a feature-gated variant because compilation is a one-shot process. This is NOT a design defect: the conditional compilation pattern is idiomatic Rust for optional features, and the variant's absence when the feature is disabled is guaranteed by the compiler, not a testing gap. Alternative verification: (1) CI matrix runs `cargo test --features tls` and `cargo test --no-default-features` separately, confirming compilation succeeds in both cases. (2) A `#[cfg(not(feature = "tls"))]` compile-fail test in a separate file or crate confirms TLS types are absent when feature is off. (3) Manual review of Cargo.toml #[cfg] attributes and feature definitions.

Translatability improvements for P3-1 scope:

1. **src/config/account_config_spec.rs**: Extract AccountConfig constructor as `AccountConfig::build()` builder pattern instead of direct field manipulation. Method names as verbs: `validate()`, `with_username()`, `with_domain()`. Extract OpusConfig magic numbers (bitrate range, ptime options) into named constants. Map validation rules to sentences: "username must not be empty", "at least one codec must be enabled".

2. **src/config/transport_ice_spec.rs**: Rename ICE config booleans as is/has prefixes: `is_enabled`, `has_aggressive_nomination`, `supports_trickle_ice`. Extract TlsConfig path fields as `PathBuf` rather than raw String. Make TransportConfig pattern match read as prose: `match transport { Udp { .. } => "use UDP", Tcp { .. } => "use TCP" }`.

3. **src/api/public_api_design.rs**: SipAccountHandle method names as verb phrases: `register().await`, `unregister().await`, `make_call(request).await`. OutgoingCallRequest fields as noun phrases: `target_uri`, `auth_override`, `preferred_transport`. Replace the existing `pub trait Service {}` placeholder with meaningful struct/impl.

4. **src/runtime/command.rs**: Replace String stubs with typed struct fields so that RuntimeCommand::AddAccount reads as "add account with AccountConfig" rather than "add account with opaque string". The from_runtime_command conversion currently uses Box::new closures — extract into named helper functions like `handle_add_account(backend, config)`.

5. **src/client.rs**: The existing SipClient::new() method uses a long chain of operations (validate, spawn, create, send). Extract into helper methods: `validate_config()`, `spawn_reactor()`, `initialize_reactor()` so new() reads as "validate, spawn, create event bus, initialize".

6. **src/account.rs, src/call.rs, src/transport.rs**: Replace stub structs (`pub id: u64`, `pub config: String`) with properly named fields and accessor methods. Use domain types: `AccountId` not `u64`, `OutgoingCallRequest` not `String`.

tickets.title: PJSIP FFI Layer, Runtime State & AudioMixer Architecture

contracts.precondition: Tokio async runtime must be initialized (tokio::runtime::Handle::current() succeeds). AudioWorkerTask must be spawned on Tokio blocking pool via tokio::task::spawn_blocking.
contracts.postcondition: AudioMixer struct created with lock-free queue boundary: crossbeam::ArrayQueue<Vec<i16>> out_queue separates AudioWorkerTask (async context) from RustMediaPort (PJSIP RT callback context). AudioWorkerTask runs process_frame loop in blocking pool.
contracts.invariant: No blocking operations (lock acquisition, dynamic memory allocation, syscall, .await) are permitted inside any function called from PJSIP RT callback thread (get_frame/put_frame). Only lock-free queue pop/push, memcpy, and zero-fill are allowed.
contracts.testPrecondition: testUnit validates: AudioMixer::new() creates struct with empty crossbeam::ArrayQueue. AudioWorkerTask::spawn succeeds when called from tokio::test context.
contracts.testPostcondition: testUnit validates: AudioWorkerTask::process_frame pushes mixed frame to out_queue. Mixer entry push operation does not panic.
contracts.testInvariant: testUnit validates: crossbeam::ArrayQueue push from std::thread does not deadlock or panic. memcpy within callback context verified via mock port struct.

contracts.precondition: AudioMixer must exist and be accessible via Arc<AudioMixer>. AudioWorkerTask must be spawned and running.
contracts.postcondition: AudioWorkerTask::process_frame iterates all sources in AudioMixer, calls AsyncAudioSource::next_chunk for each, applies gain/mute, mixes via i32 accumulation to saturating i16 clamp, pushes result to out_queue. Sources added/removed via AudioMixer are reflected at next frame boundary.
contracts.invariant: Sources are added and removed at frame boundaries. Source iteration uses snapshot of source_ids to avoid DashMap invalidation during iteration.
contracts.testPrecondition: testUnit validates: AudioMixer::add_source increments next_source_id and returns sequential IDs. Arc<AudioMixer> is Send + Sync.
contracts.testPostcondition: testUnit validates: AudioWorkerInner::process_frame with 2 MockAsyncAudioSources sums samples to mixed output buffer. Muted source skipped. Gain-adjusted source produces scaled output.
contracts.testInvariant: testUnit validates: AudioMixer::add_source during AudioWorkerTask iteration does not cause panic. 32 sources added sequentially all get correct IDs.

contracts.precondition: Audio mixer produces OUT frames; RT callback receives IN frames via separate lock-free queues.
contracts.postcondition: PairAligner with tolerance-based matching pairs IN and OUT frames by timestamp delta. Paired frames proceed to downstream processing. Missing partner beyond tolerance receives zero-padded data.
contracts.invariant: Zero-padding is applied when pair delta exceeds tolerance. Long-duration drift tracked as alignment_drift metric until threshold crossed.
contracts.testPrecondition: Deferred to P3-5/P5-2. P3-2 verifies only that mix_i16_frame output format (Vec<i16>) is compatible with downstream VecDeque<TimedFrame<Vec<i16>>> consumption.

contracts.testInvariant: testUnit validates: mix_i16_frame with unmatched source lengths zero-pads shorter sources, ensuring output length consistency.

contracts.precondition: Audio pipeline produces i16 PCM frames at AudioWorkerTask sample rate. Downstream consumer expects PJSUA conference bridge sample rate.
contracts.postcondition: ResamplePipeline using rubato FftFixedIn<f32> converts sample rate between internal rate and PJSUA bridge rate. Stereo output maps L=IN_mono, R=OUT_mono.

contracts.testInvariant: testUnit via boundary test: AudioMixer::mix_i16_frame output buffer length equals frame_samples() (160 for 20ms@8kHz).

contracts.postcondition: PJSIP FFI layer created with: (1) ffi::bindings module generated by bindgen build.rs with allowlist pattern, (2) PjOwnedStr safe wrapper for pj_str_t with Rust-owned Vec<u8> backing, (3) extern C callback functions enqueue NativeEvent, (4) runtime/ modules use only safe SipBackend trait.

tickets.background:
### Goal
Define and implement the foundational FFI layer for PJSUA integration, the AudioMixer with lock-free real-time boundary, and the typed runtime internal state (ClientState, AccountEntry, CallEntry). These three subsystems enable SipClient to drive real PJSIP calls with safe abstractions.
### Purpose
- FFI Layer (N0037): Isolate all unsafe PJSUA FFI calls behind a safe SipBackend trait, enabling testability via MockBackend and eventual backend switching.
- AudioMixer (N0033): Provide a safe, async-native audio mixing pipeline that respects PJSIP real-time thread constraints by using lock-free queues at the RT boundary.
- Runtime State (N0045): Define the type-safe source-of-truth state model that the reactor thread owns and query APIs snapshot via async RwLock, preventing deadlocks.
### Motivation
P0-6 established the AudioWorkerTask skeleton (AudioMixer, AsyncAudioSource, mock). P3-2 hardens this into production form: mix_i16_frame with overflow safety, MixerSourceEntry with gain/mute/EOF, and full crossbeam queue separation. The FFI layer is the gateway to real PJSUA interaction — without it all existing infrastructure remains mock-only. Typed ClientState is the prerequisite for state machine transitions (P6+).
### Constraints
- Bindgen must use allowlist patterns only (pjsua_*, pj_*, PJSUA_*, PJ_*) — no blanket generation.
- extern C callbacks must NEVER lock, allocate, or await — mechanical enqueue only.
- ClientState must use BTreeMap for deterministic iteration order, not HashMap.
- conf_port_id MUST NOT appear in CallEntry — PjsuaBackend exclusively owns resolution.
- Implementation order: ffi module -> SipBackend trait -> AudioMixer refinements -> ClientState types -> PjsuaBackend stub.
scope: AudioMixer: two-layer design (AudioWorkerTask Tokio async + RustMediaPort PJSIP RT callback)
AudioMixer struct: DashMap sources, atomic gain, next_id, lock-free queues (crossbeam::ArrayQueue)
MixerSourceEntry: Mutex<Box<dyn ErasedAudioSource>>, gain, muted, eof
mix_i16_frame: i32 accumulation, saturating i16 clamp
PJSIP FFI: bindgen allowlist (pjsua_*, pj_*, PJSUA_*, PJ_*), wrapper.h
PjOwnedStr: pj_str_t safe wrapper with Rust memory ownership
Callback bridge: extern C functions enqueue NativeEvent, no locks/alloc/async

SipBackend trait (pub(crate)): initialize, shutdown, create_transport, add_account, remove_account, set_registration, make_call, answer_call, hangup, conf_connect/disconnect, configure_codecs, send_dtmf, transfer_call
MockBackend for testing
ClientState: initialized, accounts BTreeMap, calls BTreeMap, transports, capabilities
AccountEntry: id, native_id, config, registration state
CallEntry: id, native_id, account_id, state, media runtime
Lock rules: read().await for queries (blocking_read prohibited), write().await for reactor updates
conf_port_id: PjsuaBackend internal, not exposed to Runtime/CallEntry
PjsuaBackend::resolve_conf_port: pjsua_call_get_info -> conf_slot

**Scope of changes:**
  - [Path=src/ffi/mod.rs] Action=add — New ffi module (bindings, pj_str, callback submodules).
  - [Path=src/ffi/bindings.rs] Action=add — Bindgen allowlist re-exports (pjsua_*, pj_*, PJSUA_*, PJ_*). Stub for cfg(not(feature=pjsua-native)).
  - [Path=src/ffi/pj_str.rs] Action=add — PjOwnedStr struct with Rust-owned Vec<u8> backing pj_str_t. Send+Sync.
  - [Path=src/ffi/callback.rs] Action=add — extern C fn on_incoming_call, on_reg_state, on_call_state, on_call_media_state enqueueing NativeEvent. No locks/alloc/async.
  - [Path=src/runtime/audio_worker.rs] Action=modify — Add MixerSourceEntry, mix_i16_frame(), AudioMixer out_queue/in_queue crossbeam::ArrayQueue, master_gain, next_id AtomicU64.
  - [Path=src/runtime/backend.rs] Action=refactor — Rename Backend to SipBackend trait. Align signatures with RFC: initialize(&ClientConfig)->ClientCapabilities, add_account(&AccountConfig), make_call(&OutgoingCallRequest). Add create_transport, configure_codecs, answer_call(code), transfer_call. Add PjsuaBackend stub.
  - [Path=src/runtime/state.rs] Action=modify — ClientState typed BTreeMap accounts/calls, transports Vec, capabilities. AccountEntry with native_id:pjsua_acc_id, config:AccountConfig, registration:RegistrationState. CallEntry typed. Compile-time conf_port_id assertion.
  - [Path=src/lib.rs] Action=modify — Uncomment pub mod ffi;
  - [Path=build.rs] Action=add — Bindgen build script with wrapper.h and allowlist.
  - [Path=wrapper.h] Action=add — #include <pjsua.h>, <pjmedia.h>.

**Out of scope:**
  - PairAligner (N0035) — timestamp alignment beyond AudioMixer boundary; ticket P3-5.
  - ResamplePipeline + rubato (N0036) — rubato crate integration; ticket P4-2.
  - RustMediaPort / pjmedia_port registration (N0049) — actual PJSUA media port functions; ticket P4-2.
  - Dual Client EventBus routing (N0038) — EventBus per SipClient; ticket P3-5/P5-2.
  - Production PjsuaBackend with real FFI calls — P3-2 defines trait + stub; real FFI in P4+.

**Affected areas:**
  - [runtime/reactor.rs] Impact=API surface — Backend type renamed to SipBackend in dispatch loop field.
  - [runtime/command.rs] Impact=API surface — DispatchCommand closures use &mut dyn SipBackend. RuntimeCommand backend dispatch signatures change.
  - [runtime/audio_worker.rs] Impact=Performance — New crossbeam queues add ~16KB static allocation per AudioMixer.
  - [audio_worker.rs AudioWorkerInner] Impact=Correctness — Inline mixing replaced by mix_i16_frame call. Regression risk mitigated by existing test suite.
  - [ffi/pj_str.rs] Impact=Memory — pj_str_t ptr now points to Rust-owned memory. All PJSUA callers must use as_raw() for each FFI call.
  - [runtime/state.rs] Impact=API — Caller code referencing old u64 id fields must use typed AccountId/CallId newtypes.
Response: Y — runtime/reactor.rs/batch rename. Y — re-run test suite to verify no regression in existing AudioWorkerTask behavior.

testExceptions: Exception: PJSIP RT callback get_frame/put_frame via RustMediaPort — Reason: cannot test because this requires physical PJSIP media port registration (pjsua_media_port_register, pjsua_conf_add_port) which is only available with actual PJSUA library linked (Layer 3+). Cannot be unit-tested because the extern C callback signature is called by PJSIP RT thread, not by test code. This is NOT a design defect — the architecture separates RT callback (unsafe extern C) from AudioWorkerTask (safe async) with a provable lock-free queue boundary, and the get_frame/put_frame implementation is a mechanical memcpy/zero-fill that is independently verifiable via Rust-native mock queue. Alternative verification: Layer 3 integration test with minimal pjsua_init + pjsua_media_port_register in isolated test binary (P4-2).

Exception: bindgen-generated FFI bindings (pjsua.h, pj_str_t, pjsua_call_get_info) — Reason: cannot test because bindgen build.rs generates Rust FFI declarations from system-installed PJSIP headers. These declarations are not authored by hand and their correctness depends on the installed PJSIP version. This is NOT a design defect — the bindgen output is a mechanical translation; structural correctness is verified at compile time and semantic correctness is tested via MockBackend. Alternative verification: compile-time test verifies ffi::pjsua_call_get_info has correct function signature via static assertion (size_of, align_of).

Exception: AudioMixer out_queue consumer (RT callback side pop) timing behavior — Reason: cannot test because the inter-thread latency between AudioWorkerTask push and PJSIP RT callback pop depends on OS scheduling, not on code correctness. This is NOT a design defect — the crossbeam::ArrayQueue provides bounded, lock-free, wait-free push/pop with predictable failure (full queue = drop), which is the correct behavior for real-time audio. Alternative verification: queue capacity behavior tested by filling queue to capacity in unit test; timing-independent queue semantics tested via concurrent push/pop from separate std::thread tasks.
acceptanceCriteria: Happy path: All unsafe PJSUA bindings isolated in ffi/ module — runtime/ modules compile with zero unsafe keywords. SipBackend trait covers all 13 PJSUA operations (initialize through transfer_call). MockBackend returns deterministic canned responses. AudioMixer::mix_i16_frame with 1-16+ sources produces clamped i16 output without overflow. ClientState snapshot exposes correct balance of accounts/calls via async read().await.

Error case: SipBackend trait method returning Err(SipError) propagates correctly through CoreReactor dispatch to RuntimeHandle submit caller. PjsuaBackend stub returns Err(SipError::unimplemented) for every operation. AudioMixer::remove_source on non-existent id returns Err. AudioMixer::mix_i16_frame with 0 sources produces zero-filled output. ClientStateSnapshot::read on empty state returns initialized=false without deadlocking.

Edge case: CallEntry construction with all fields explicitly set — compile fails if conf_port_id is attempted (intentional omission). AudioMixer with 32 concurrent sources — all IDs correctly assigned without gaps or collisions. PjOwnedStr with large (&str len > 4096) input — Vec<u8> allocation succeeds without panic.

tickets.notes:
- 【Implementation steps】Step 1: Create ffi/ module (mod.rs, bindings.rs, pj_str.rs, callback.rs) + build.rs + wrapper.h. Step 2: Rename Backend->SipBackend trait, update signatures, add new methods, add PjsuaBackend stub, extend MockBackend. Step 3: Add mix_i16_frame function + MixerSourceEntry to audio_worker.rs, add crossbeam queue fields to AudioMixer. Step 4: Update ClientState with typed BTreeMap fields, AccountEntry/CallEntry refinements, ClientCapabilities, TransportRuntimeState. Step 5: Wire ffi module into lib.rs. Step 6: Verify compilation + all existing tests still pass.
- 【Risks】Risk: Bindgen build.rs may fail if PJSIP headers not installed. Mitigation: ffi/bindings.rs has cfg(not(feature=pjsua-native)) stub. Risk: crossbeam::ArrayQueue capacity sizing. Mitigation: Configurable capacity with safe default (64 frames = ~1.28s audio @20ms frame). Risk: Backend trait rename causes compile errors in existing reactor code. Mitigation: Mechanical rename in single batch, verified by full test suite.
- 【Caveats】SipBackend trait is pub(crate), NOT pub — external consumers cannot implement it. PjsuaBackend stub returns Err(SipError::unimplemented()) for all methods. MockBackend provides reference implementation.
- 【Open items】Crossbeam queue integration into AudioWorkerTask::process_frame remains [::STUB::] waiting for RustMediaPort consumer (P4-2). NativeEvent types for callbacks (IncomingCall, CallState, RegState) are defined in P0-5 event module.
- 【Future improvements】Media Frame slab allocation pool for pre-allocated Vec reuse. SipBackend async trait if backend ops become async. PjsuaBackend singleton via OnceLock with trait object registration.

tickets.invariants:
- 【Normal establishment】AudioMixer lock-free queues (out_queue/in_queue) are initialized with positive capacity on creation. PjOwnedStr ptr/slen always reflects owned Vec<u8> content. ClientState is default-false initialized; accounts/calls/transports start empty.
- 【Invariant on error】ClientState remains internally consistent after any SipBackend error — partial account additions roll back fully. AudioMixer source iteration continues after a source returns next_chunk=0 (EOF). FFI callback errors enqueue NativeEvent with error payload, never panic.
- 【Internal state invariant】ClientState holds the single source of truth for accounts/calls/transports — never duplicated externally. AccountEntry.native_id maps 1:1 to pjsua_acc_id. CallEntry does NOT contain conf_port_id. AudioMixer.source_count never negative. conf_port_id resolved fresh on each call via PjsuaBackend::resolve_conf_port.
- 【Boundary invariant】mix_i16_frame output sample values always clamped to [i16::MIN, i16::MAX] via saturating i32->i16 conversion, never overflow. crossbeam::ArrayQueue capacity is the hard upper bound on queued frames — producer never blocks (drops on full). ffi/ module contains ALL unsafe code — zero unsafe in runtime/ or client.rs.

tickets.background:
N0061 defines the siprs-server main.rs entry point: SipClient initialization from config, DatabasePool initialization, saved account restoration from SQLite, and Axum server startup on configured bind address. Supports both standalone binary mode and Tauri-embedded library mode.

### Goal
Define the standalone server entry point (main.rs) and supporting types (ServerConfig, AppState, build_router) that initialize SipClient, DatabasePool, restore saved accounts from SQLite, and start an Axum HTTP/WS server on the configured bind address. The server provides at minimum a health check endpoint (GET /api/v1/health) and a shutdown endpoint (POST /api/v1/shutdown).

### Purpose
Enable external applications (external SIP clients, Tauri frontend, monitoring tools, CLI scripts) to control siprs via HTTP REST APIs and WebSocket event streams without linking to the siprs Rust library directly. The standalone server bridges the Rust SIP client implementation with any HTTP-capable consumer.

### Motivation
The RFC defines siprs as a crate with both library and server modes. Standalone server mode is required for the P2P network layer (server-side components), monitoring/observability tooling (health checks, metrics export), and future Tauri desktop integration where the server runs as an embedded sidecar. Without this entry point, all SIP operations would require direct Rust FFI, limiting integration options.

### Constraints
1. Must support two entry modes: standalone binary (with clap CLI arg parsing) and embedded library (programmatic ServerConfig, no CLI dependency). 2. Axum server must bind only after SipClient and DatabasePool are fully initialized and saved accounts restored — never expose an uninitialized state. 3. Health check must respond HTTP 200 before any accounts are added (readiness probe). 4. AuthConfig defaults to LocalhostOnly for security — server must not listen on external interfaces without explicit auth configuration. 5. No external crate split in P3-3 — server types live in siprs crate, behind a feature gate. siprs-server crate split is tracked in P4-3.
scope: main.rs: SipClient::new(config), DatabasePool::open, load saved accounts, build_router, axum::serve
ServerConfig binding address default: 127.0.0.1:3910
AuthConfig modes: LocalhostOnly (default), ApiKey, Jwt
Dual mode: standalone binary (cli feature + clap) and embedded library (lib.rs without cli)

**Scope of changes (describe each change comprehensively):**
  - [File/module path] src/api/standalone_server_config.rs
  - [Action: add/modify/remove/rename/refactor] modify (extend existing ServerConfig with from_args() method, add AppState struct, add build_router() function)
  - [What specifically changes] (1) Add ServerConfig::from_args() — CLI arg parsing via clap for --port, --bind-addr, --db-path, --config-file, --auth-mode, --jwt-secret, --jwt-expiry. (2) Add AppState struct with sip_client: Arc<SipClient> and db: Arc<DatabasePool> fields. (3) Add build_router() returning axum::Router with health check and shutdown routes.
  - [Before → After (behavior/signature)] Before: ServerConfig exists with direct construction only, no instance methods. After: ServerConfig::from_args() -> Result<ServerConfig, SipError> parses CLI args; AppState { sip_client: Arc<SipClient>, db: Arc<DatabasePool> } ; pub fn build_router(state: AppState) -> Router
  - [API contract change (if any)] New public API surfaces: AppState struct, build_router() function, ServerConfig::from_args() method. These become part of the crate public API (behind server feature gate).
  - [Data schema change (if any)] None — no new persistent data structures.
  - [Config/env change (if any)] CLI args added as environment variable overrides: SIPRS_PORT (--port), SIPRS_BIND_ADDR (--bind-addr), SIPRS_DB_PATH (--db-path), SIPRS_CONFIG_FILE (--config-file), SIPRS_AUTH_MODE (--auth-mode), SIPRS_JWT_SECRET (--jwt-secret)
  - [Dependency added/removed (if any)] clap = { version = "4", optional = true } behind 'cli' feature. axum = { version = "0.7", optional = true } behind 'server' feature. tower-http = { version = "0.5", features = ["cors"], optional = true } behind 'server' feature.

**Out of scope (items intentionally excluded, with justification):**
  - [Excluded item] Full REST API implementation (18 endpoints from RFC §54)
  - [Why excluded — separate ticket / future phase / not applicable] P4-3 handles all route handlers except health check and shutdown. P3-3 provides only minimal health+shutdown for verification that the server framework works.
  - [Excluded item] WebSocket endpoint implementation (ws:// and ws/audio)
  - [Why excluded — separate ticket / future phase / not applicable] WebSocket session management is tracked in P4-3. P3-3 reserves the WebSocket route paths but only wires health check.
  - [Excluded item] siprs-server crate split (separate Cargo.toml)
  - [Why excluded — separate ticket / future phase / not applicable] The crate split requires all route handlers and auth middleware to be implemented first. Tracked in P4-3.
  - [Excluded item] JWT token generation and verification middleware
  - [Why excluded — separate ticket / future phase / not applicable] JWT auth middleware is tracked in P4-2. P3-3 defines the AuthConfig types but the middleware layer is P4-2 scope.

**Affected areas (components/systems impacted, even without direct modification):**
  - [Affected component] Cargo.toml feature flags
  - [Nature of impact: performance / security / API surface / data format / …] API surface — new 'cli' and 'server' feature flags added to Cargo.toml. Default features do NOT include cli or server (library mode stays lightweight).
  - [Corresponding change needed Y/N + details] Y — lib.rs must conditionally compile the server-only modules behind feature gates.
  - [Affected component] config.rs re-exports
  - [Nature of impact: API surface] New ServerConfig methods exposed through public API.
  - [Corresponding change needed Y/N + details] Y — config.rs already re-exports ServerConfig/AuthConfig/AuthMode. New methods are auto-available through existing re-exports.
  - [Affected component] runtime/ module shutdown path
  - [Nature of impact: control flow] The shutdown route handler must submit RuntimeCommand::Shutdown to the reactor.
  - [Corresponding change needed Y/N + details] Y — shutdown handler needs access to the RuntimeHandle via AppState.

testExceptions:
- [Item] Full end-to-end server startup with real SipClient and DatabasePool (loading real PJSIP backend, connecting to SQLite DB)
   [Reason — NOT TESTABLE, NOT A DESIGN DEFECT] PJSIP FFI requires native library initialization (pj_init()) which cannot be sandboxed or mocked at this layer. The DatabasePool requires sqlite-storage feature which depends on rusqlite native build. Full stack integration is only possible in siprs-server crate. This is NOT a design defect — it is a consequence of FFI dependency isolation.
   [Alternative] MockBackend-based integration tests (P1-3/N0053) in P4-3 provide isolated server startup without PJSIP dependency.

- [Item] TCP port binding on a specific hardcoded port in unit tests
   [Reason — NOT TESTABLE, NOT A DESIGN DEFECT] Port availability is non-deterministic — port may be in use at test time, causing flaky CI failures. This is NOT a design defect — it is a fundamental property of TCP networking.
   [Alternative] (1) Bind to port 0, extract actual port from TcpListener, then make test requests. (2) Integration test in siprs-server crate uses CI-specific port allocation.

- [Item] Real HTTP client requests through the full Axum middleware stack (CORS, JWT auth) without PJSIP initialized
   [Reason — NOT TESTABLE, NOT A DESIGN DEFECT] The Axum middleware layer requires SipClient in AppState which depends on initialized PJSIP backend. Without PJSIP, the middleware chain beyond health check cannot be exercised. This is NOT a design defect — it is a natural dependency ordering.
   [Alternative] (1) Health check has NO auth requirement — testable via axum::test. (2) JWT middleware tests in P4-2. (3) Mock SipClient (P1-3 trait) for isolated middleware tests.
acceptanceCriteria: siprs-server binary starts and listens on configured address

(3) build_router() returns a Router with GET /api/v1/health route. (4) The health handler returns {"status":"ok"} HTTP 200 response via axum::test. (2) AuthConfig::validate() returns ConfigError::JwtRequiresSecret for Jwt mode without jwt_secret set. (4) ServerConfig::from_args() returns SipError for invalid --bind-addr format (not a valid IP:port).

(3) ServerConfig default db_path is ~/.siprs/data.db (home directory expansion is caller responsibility). (4) Empty allowed_origins vec produces permissive CORS. (5) AppState with Arc<SipClient> and Arc<DatabasePool> is Send + Sync.

Implementation file: src/api/standalone_server_config.rs

- [Implementation steps] Phase 1: Add 'cli' and 'server' feature flags to Cargo.toml with clap=4 (optional), axum=0.7 (optional), tower-http=0.5/cors (optional) dependencies. Phase 2: Extend standalone_server_config.rs — add ServerConfig::from_args() method using clap::Command/ArgMatches, add AppState struct, add build_router() function with health check (GET /api/v1/health) and shutdown (POST /api/v1/shutdown) endpoints. Phase 3: Add feature-gated condition in lib.rs or a new server_entry.rs module. Phase 4: Add comprehensive tests (unit tests for config parsing, integration test for health endpoint via axum::test). Phase 5: cargo fmt + cargo clippy.
- [Risks] (1) clap arg parsing with --port may conflict with existing arg parsers if this crate is used as a library — mitigated by gating behind 'cli' feature. (2) axum 0.7 API changes from 0.6 may affect Router construction — verify against locked version. (3) shutdown handler needs RuntimeHandle::submit(RuntimeCommand::Shutdown) — relies on RuntimeHandle not having moved/dropped.
- [Caveats] (1) ServerConfig::from_args() should use clap::Command::no_binary_name() for library-mode safety. (2) The health check handler is simple enough to implement without error types — just returns JSON with status:ok. (3) AppState server_start_time field is used for uptime calculation in health check.
- [Open items] (1) Whether to use clap::Parser derive or clap::Command builder API — prefer builder for library-mode compatibility. (2) Whether AppState needs a server_start_time: Instant field for health check uptime — yes, for observability. (3) DatabasePool::load_accounts() method signature not yet defined in P2-3 — may need trait-based indirection.
- [Future improvements] (1) Rate limiting layer on health endpoint (low priority — health is lightweight). (2) Graceful shutdown timeout configuration via ServerConfig. (3) systemd notify integration for socket-activated startup (Linux only).

tickets.invariants:
- 【Normal establishment】ServerConfig and AppState types must be constructible with valid defaults before server startup. build_router() must accept any valid AppState without panicking. Health check endpoint must respond HTTP 200 before any accounts are registered.
- 【Invariant on error】ConfigError must never panic in Display/From implementations. Server startup failure (invalid config, port in use, DB open failure) must produce a typed error, never an unwrap/panic. build_router() must not panic on any valid AppState input.
- 【Internal state invariant】ServerConfig default bind_addr must be 127.0.0.1:3910. DEFAULT_SIPRS_PORT must equal 3910. AuthConfig default mode must be LocalhostOnly. AppState fields are Arc-wrapped (never cloned deeply).

tickets.background:
- [Goal] Fully define the type system foundation for the siprs crate: newtype ID identifiers (AccountId, CallId, AudioSourceId) as NonZeroU64 with BiMap runtime-to-native mapping; complete SipEventPayload enum with 25+ variants spanning all event categories; RegistrationState machine with 7 states and 8 transition rules; CallState machine with 13 states and all transition paths.
- [Purpose] These types form the shared language across all siprs modules (API, event system, state machines, FFI bridge, audio processing). Without them, module boundaries use raw integers (u64, pjsua_acc_id, pjsua_call_id) leading to type confusion, parameter swap bugs, and opaque error messages. The BiMap specifically solves PJSUA id reuse — native IDs are recycled by PJSUA after session teardown, and public API consumers must never see recycled IDs.
- [Motivation] P0-5 (Event System) delivered SipEventPayload, EventBus, and basic CallState as a Minimum Viable Event System. However, P0-5 used placeholder AccountId(pub u64)/CallId(pub u64) with NonZeroU64 requirements stubbed out, only 6 CallState variants (vs 13 required by N0026), and no RegistrationState. These gaps must be resolved before downstream tickets (P3-1 Public API, P5-1 Call API) can depend on correct types.
- [Constraints] (1) model/ module is currently gated behind #[cfg(feature = "sqlite-storage")] — id_design_newtype.rs must be made unconditionally compilable. (2) BiMap must use existing dependencies (dashmap) — no new crate additions without justification. (3) SipEventPayload must remain #[non_exhaustive] — existing downstream consumers (P0-5 tests, EventBus, AccountEventReceiver) must continue to compile. (4) RegistrationState and CallState must be Copy+Clone — they are used in hot paths (per-event, per-call). (5) RFC 12 states for CallState are actually 13: Disconnected and Failed are separate terminal states.

tickets.invariants:
- [Normal condition] Newtype ID construction: AccountId::from_u64(x) succeeds iff x > 0, returns ZeroValue error iff x == 0. BiMap insert/lookup round-trip: insert(r, n) guarantees get_native(r) == Some(n) and get_runtime(n) == Some(r) until remove(r) is called. RegistrationState transitions: every transition follows exactly one of the 8 defined rules; no implicit transitions exist. CallState transitions: every transition follows the DAG defined in §18.1; all non-terminal states can reach Disconnected or Failed.
- [Error invariant] Zero-value ID construction (from_u64(0)) never succeeds — returns Err(SipErrorKind::ZeroValue). BiMap never loses data on concurrent access — dashmap interior mutability guarantees crash-consistency. Invalid state machine transitions never mutate internal state — Err is returned, state unchanged. RegistrationState::Failed and Expired do not prevent make_call() — this invariant is enforced by the absence of registration checks in the Call API.
- [Internal state invariant] BiMap internal state: for all (r, n) pairs, r is unique (RuntimeId is the primary key). NativeId n may be reused; the newest (r, n) pair wins on insert. RegistrationState machine: internal transition table enumerates exactly (7 states × 7 targets) = 49 boolean predicates, of which exactly 10 are true (the 8 rules plus 2 reflexive). CallState machine: transition table enumerates exactly (13 states × 13 targets) = 169 boolean predicates, covering all outgoing/incoming/hold/transfer paths.
- [Boundary invariant] AccountId/CallId/AudioSourceId NonZeroU64 domain: [1, u64::MAX]. BiMap capacity: unbounded (backed by dashmap). EventBus capacity impact: AccountId/CallId size is 8 bytes each, negligible on bus capacity. RegistrationState transitions: Failed→Registering retry must not cause infinite loop — controlled by ClientConfig::registration_retry_count (P3-1 scope). CallState: max_calls concurrent limit enforced by Call API (P3-1 scope), not by state machine itself.

tickets.background:
N0030 defines audio format types and AudioChunkPair. N0035 defines PairAligner for IN/OUT alignment. N0036 defines ResamplePipeline using rubato. N0040 defines codec policy with NegotiatedCodec and CodecSelectionPolicy.

### Goal
Define and implement the foundational audio data types (AudioFormat, AudioChunkPair), the IN/OUT alignment algorithm (PairAligner) for RTP-vs-mixer timebase reconciliation, the resampling pipeline (ResamplePipeline) with stereo IN/OUT mapping, and the codec negotiation/fallback policy (NegotiatedCodec, CodecSelectionPolicy). These four nodes form the audio processing layer that all higher-level audio features (AudioMixer, Media Bridge, Audio Subscribe) depend on.

### Purpose
Provide type-safe, testable audio primitives that decouple the inner audio pipeline from PJSUA's native format and codec model. Callers work with AudioFormat/AudioChunkPair regardless of the underlying FFI format; PairAligner absorbs the timing skew between RTP arrival (network jitter) and mixer scheduling (Tokio async); the resampler bridges sample rate gaps; the codec policy ensures only PCMU and Opus are active after initialization (C041 invariant).

### Motivation
P3-2 (AudioMixer) introduced mix_i16_frame and the mixer/source infrastructure but left the data representation layer abstract. Without AudioFormat/AudioChunkPair, callers must reason about raw Vec<i16> and sample rates manually — a fertile ground for off-by-one and format mismatch bugs. Without PairAligner, the RTP ingress timebase (realtime) and AudioWorkerTask timebase (Tokio async) diverge and cause audio artifacts. Without the codec policy, all PJSUA codecs remain enabled (including G.722, iLBC, etc.), violating the Opus-only/PCMU-fallback security and quality requirement (C041).

### Constraints
1. No PJSUA dependency in pure-data types (AudioFormat, AudioChunkPair, NegotiatedCodec) — they must be testable without an initialized PJSIP stack. 2. PairAligner must not block or allocate on the RT callback path — only VecDeque push/pop in AudioWorkerTask context. 3. ResamplePipeline uses rubato FftFixedIn as the single resampling backend — no fallback to linear interpolation. 4. Codec priority assignments follow the M20 spec: Opus=255, PCMU=254, all others=0 in auto mode. 5. The codec policy fallback file (codec_policy_fallback.rs) must remain consistent with the already-implemented m20_codec_auto_mode.rs.

acceptanceCriteria: 【Happy path】Construct AudioFormat with all valid field combinations (4 sample rates × 2 bit depths × 2 channel layouts × 4 frame_ms values = 64 valid combinations). Create AudioChunkPair with matching IN/OUT AudioChunk data. Push timed IN and OUT frames into PairAligner within tolerance — try_pair returns the paired (in, out) data. Configure ResamplePipeline for 48kHz→16kHz conversion — resample a known signal and verify correct output dimensions. CodecAutoMode::apply with PCMU/Opus/other codecs returns {PCMU=254, Opus=255, other=0}. NegotiatedCodec::Opus(OpusConfig) round-trips through AccountCodecPolicy storage.

【Error case】AudioFormat::new with frame_ms=0 or 70 (out of range) returns Err. AudioFormat::new with frame_ms=17 (not divisible by 10) returns Err. PairAligner::try_pair on both empty queues returns None. PairAligner drops the earlier frame when timestamp delta exceeds tolerance. ResamplePipeline::new with same in_rate==out_rate but unsupported combination returns Err. CodecAutoMode::apply with duplicate codec_ids returns Err(SipError).

【Edge case】AudioChunk::I16 with empty Vec<i16> is valid (len=0). AudioChunk::F32 with empty Vec<f32> is valid. AudioFormat frame_ms at minimum (10) and maximum (60) boundaries both construct successfully. PairAligner where only IN data arrives (no OUT data for extended period) produces zero-padded OUT with incrementing drift counter. interleave_in_out with in_mono shorter than out_mono truncates to the shorter length. Stereo interleave of empty inputs produces empty output vec.

Implementation files: src/model/audio_format_chunkpair.rs, src/config/codec_policy_fallback.rs, src/model/audio_aligner.rs (new), src/model/audio_resampler.rs (new)

- 【Implementation steps】1. Implement SampleRate/BitDepth/ChannelLayout enums in audio_format_chunkpair.rs → 2. Implement AudioFormat with validation → 3. Implement AudioChunk enum + AudioChunkPair struct → 4. Create audio_aligner.rs with PairAligner + TimedFrame → 5. Create audio_resampler.rs with interleave_in_out → 6. - 【Risks】PairAligner tolerance value selection (20ms default) may need tuning based on real network jitter measurements — use a configurable Duration. rubato crate API may change between versions — pin the version. Ensure AudioChunkPair timestamp field uses SystemTime (wall clock) not Instant (monotonic) for cross-module timestamp reconciliation.
- 【Caveats】AudioChunkPair's timestamp pairing invariant is enforced by the type design (single timestamp field for both IN and OUT), but callers must ensure they construct pairs with matching buffers. The interleave_in_out function truncates to the shorter input — callers must verify lengths match the expected frame size for the configured format.
- 【Open items】Whether to add rubato as an unconditional dependency or behind a feature gate (e.g., "resampler") is unresolved — current scope creates ResamplePipeline as a format-validation+interleave wrapper and defers the actual rubato call to P5-2. `first_seq`/`last_seq` fields in AudioChunkPair are placeholders for future RTP sequence number tracking — actual usage deferred to P5+.
- 【Future improvements】Pre-allocated buffer pools for Vec<i16> in PairAligner to reduce allocation pressure under high load. Configurable alignment loss threshold for MediaError generation. Dynamic sample rate detection from SDP negotiation. Additional codecs (G.722, iLBC) behind feature flags for enterprise PBX compatibility.

tickets.invariants:
- 【Normal establishment】AudioFormat fields must always have valid values: sample_rate in {Hz8000,Hz16000,Hz24000,Hz48000}, bit_depth in {I16,F32}, channel_layout in {Mono,StereoInOut}, frame_ms in {10,20,40,60} only. AudioChunkPair must always pair IN and OUT data under the same timestamp. PairAligner must only produce paired output when |ts_in - ts_out| <= tolerance. Codec auto mode must assign Opus=255 and PCMU=254 invariantly.
- 【Invariant on error】On any validation error (e.g., invalid frame_ms), the AudioFormat is not constructed — no partial or inconsistent AudioFormat instance is ever created. If PairAligner encounters a timeout during queue draining, it zero-pads rather than returning corrupt data. Aligner drift is reported as a counter metric, never as a hard error unless sustained loss exceeds a future configurable threshold.
- 【Internal state invariant】PairAligner in_q and out_q are VecDeque<TimedFrame<Vec<i16>>> that grow monotonically until try_pair is called — the queue depths reflect the cumulative IN/OUT imbalance. ResamplePipeline holds in_rate/out_rate AudioFormat references and is stateless between resample calls. CodecSelectionPolicy is a pure configuration enum with no mutable state.
- 【Boundary invariant】frame_ms=10 is the minimum valid frame duration (at 48kHz=480 samples), frame_ms=60 is the maximum (at 8kHz=480 samples). PairAligner tolerance must be > 0 (zero tolerance would prevent any matching; practically set to >=20ms to accommodate jitter). AudioChunk::I16 with empty Vec<i16> and AudioChunk::F32 with empty Vec<f32> are valid edge states. NegotiatedCodec has exactly 2 variants (Pcmu, Opus).
