This ticket implements the complete event system: EventBus with control/raw_sip broadcast channels (N0019), design decisions for loss-tolerant delivery with Lagged detection (N0020), NativeEvent to SipEventPayload conversion for all P0/P1/P2 priority events (N0021), CallState/CallMediaState mapping from pjsip_inv_state and media_status (N0022), RegistrationStateChanged via RuntimeCommand::GetAccountInfo pattern (N0023), DtmfSent two-phase design with timeout fallback (N0029), and Dual Client PJSIP callback routing with account_id-based EventBus dispatch (N0038).

## Goal
The P0-5 event system provides the complete bridge between PJSIP C callbacks and Rust async event consumers. It defines the SipEventPayload enum (all P0 variants: Registration/Call/DTMF; P1: Transport/ICE; P2: supplemental), the EventBus with split control/raw_sip broadcast channels, the NativeEvent-to-SipEventPayload conversion functions, and the Dual Client routing infrastructure. Every PJSIP callback-generated event is delivered to the correct SipClient's EventBus as a typed SipEvent struct.

## Purpose
SipClient consumers (UI layer, audio pipeline, logging) need observable, structured notifications about SIP state changes. Without this event system, application code would need to poll for state or interpret raw PJSIP callbacks directly. The EventBus provides a decoupled publish-subscribe pattern where:
- Reactor publishes SipEvents onto broadcast channels
- Multiple consumers independently subscribe and filter (via AccountEventReceiver)
- RawSIP messages are isolated on a separate bus to prevent control event loss

This is the primary async communication channel between the synchronous PJSIP thread (C callbacks) and the async Rust world (tokio tasks).

## Motivation
This is the foundational event infrastructure for the entire crate. All observable SIP behavior — registration status changes, call state transitions, DTMF events, media state changes — flows through this system. Every downstream feature (P2-2 error payloads, P2-4 audio pipeline, P4-1 registration state machine) depends on events being delivered. The current stub (src/client.rs uses mpsc::Receiver<()>) blocks all downstream development.

Without this ticket:
- No SipEventPayload type exists (all stubs)
- NativeEvent conversion is unimplemented
- SipClient returns dummy event receiver (cannot observe any SIP events)
- Dual Client mode (multiple SipClient instances) has no event routing

## Constraints
- Broadcast channel (lossy delivery): tokio::sync::broadcast is the only supported channel type. No reliable delivery, no per-subscriber retransmission. This is by design (N0020).
- PJSUA dependency: NativeEvent types mirror PJSIP callback signatures (pjsip_inv_state, pjsua_call_media_status). Any PJSIP version mismatch may require updating the mapping.
- Single Reactor constraint: global_runtime() must remain unchanged. Dual Client uses EventBus dispatch only — no second Reactor.
- All implementation targets are stub files (pub enum State {} / pub trait Service {}). This is net-new implementation, not refactoring of existing code.
- DtmfSent 500ms timeout: This is a fallback for when PJSIP does not fire a send-complete callback. The timeout may race with actual PJSIP callback delivery (firing both DtmfSent events) — consumer must handle duplicates.

### Goal (P7-2 re-implementation)
Close all five ABC inspection gaps in the P0-5 event system: (O-001) make RegistrationStateChanged actually publish RegistrationSucceeded/RegistrationFailed via the RuntimeCommand::GetAccountInfo → MockBackend::get_account_info() → registration_status_to_payload flow on the client EventBus; (O-002) implement the DtmfSent 500ms timeout fallback (spawn_dtmf_sent_timeout + DtmfConfig::sent_timeout_ms) with a tokio::time::pause() test; (O-003) implement production Reactor dispatch_event()/client_event_buses/default_event_bus and test the production code; (O-004) add SipClient::accounts()/call_state() authoritative query methods and prove events are observation-only; (O-005) assert the exact Lagged(n) count.
### Purpose (P7-2 re-implementation)
The prior implementation produced green tests that did not exercise the production publication/dispatch flows: RegistrationStateChanged never published an event, DtmfSent never fired as a timeout, dual-client routing existed only inside test bodies, the query API did not exist, and Lagged(n) was asserted loosely. The re-implementation makes every contract (C020-C024, C030, C039) verifiable against production code so a violation fails a test assertion.
### Motivation (P7-2 re-implementation)
The ABC Inspection Pipeline confirmed that the contracts' preconditions/postconditions/invariants were not translated into tests of production behavior — Evaluation A/B/C all failed for O-001..O-003. Downstream tickets (P2-2 error payloads, P2-4 audio pipeline, P4-1 registration state machine, P0-6 FFI bridge) depend on these events actually being delivered. Leaving the gaps means contract violations are undetectable, so the re-implementation must ship production code + tests together.
### Constraints (P7-2 re-implementation)
- Single Reactor constraint: global_runtime() unchanged — dual-client dispatch is EventBus-only (C039).
- DtmfSent timeout may race with the real PJSIP callback; consumers must tolerate duplicate DtmfSent events (N0029).
- tokio::time::pause() requires the `test-util` tokio feature — a Cargo.toml feature addition is mandatory for the O-002 deterministic timeout test (no runtime dependency change).
- No new crates; the production flow must be testable with MockBackend (no live PJSIP).
- CallMediaStateChanged currently hardcodes media_status=1 ([::STUB::] P4-2) — P7-2 keeps this stub but must not regress it.

tickets.invariants:
- [Normal condition] EventBus::publish() must never block — broadcast::Sender::send() is non-blocking by design. SipEventPayload must be Clone + Debug. EventBus must be Clone (all clones share same Sender). NativeEvent conversion must be total over defined P0 variants.
- [Error invariant] On Lagged(n), the receiver skips n messages and resumes from current position — no crash or state corruption. AccountEventReceiver must not panic on Lagged(n). DtmfSent timeout must not abort ongoing operations.
- [Internal state invariant] EventBus Sender is shared across all Clones. AccountEventReceiver holds its own broadcast Receiver. Reactor owns the EventBus Sender + client_event_buses map. client_event_buses is only mutated by SipClient initialization/shutdown, not by event dispatch.
- [Boundary invariant] EventBus default capacity 2048 must accommodate ~100 concurrent calls (~20 events/call). RawSIP channel capacity must be configured independently. DtmfSent timeout default 500ms must be less than typical PJSIP DTMF duration.
- [Normal condition] Reactor::dispatch_event() must route each event to exactly one destination: Some(account_id) matching a client_event_buses key → that bus only; Some(account_id) matching no key → default_event_bus; None (lifecycle) → default_event_bus + every registered client bus (C039). RegistrationStateChanged must publish exactly one RegistrationSucceeded/RegistrationFailed event per GetAccountInfo reply on both success and error paths (C024).
- [Error invariant] RegistrationStateChanged with backend.get_account_info() returning Err must still publish a failure event on the EventBus — no silent drop, no reactor state corruption (C024). DtmfSent timeout fallback must not abort any ongoing call operation — it only publishes DtmfSent{Err(Timeout)} (C030).
- [Internal state invariant] client_event_buses is owned by the Reactor and only mutated during SipClient initialization/shutdown (serialized via the reactor command queue) — dispatch_event() never observes a half-mutated map. DtmfConfig::sent_timeout_ms is read once at SendDtmf dispatch time; later config changes do not affect already-queued timers (C030). SipClient::accounts()/call_state() read the authoritative ClientState, not the event stream (C021).
- [Boundary invariant] Lagged(n) count equals the number of skipped messages (broadcast channel semantics) — asserted exactly, not matched with a wildcard (C020). EventBus default capacity 2048 must accommodate ~100 concurrent calls (~20 events/call); DtmfSent timeout default 500ms must be less than typical PJSIP DTMF duration; sent_timeout_ms is configurable via DtmfConfig::sent_timeout_ms (C030).

tickets.background:
[::INSPECTION_FLAGGED::]
This ticket has been flagged by the ABC Inspection Pipeline after completing the implementation lifecycle (make → plan → start → review → resolve). The actual source code was rigorously analyzed against three criteria:

  A — Contract Translation:   Are all Precondition/Postcondition/Invariant contracts accurately translated into test code?
  B — Violation Detection:    Can every contract violation be detected by an existing test assertion?
  C — Test Precision:         Are tests precise and unambiguous (no broad assertions, no missing edge cases)?

One or more ABC violations were confirmed. This ticket is hereby remanded for re-implementation. Every violation must be fully resolved, and every contract must be fulfilled in this final implementation round. Complete it this time.

## Goal
Define and implement the siprs-server crate specification: standalone server mode (ServerConfig, AuthConfig, AuthMode), HTTP/WS protocol layer (18 REST endpoints + 2 WebSocket paths + AudioFrameHeader binary protocol), SQLite persistence schema (4 tables via SeaORM + rusqlite bundled), semver/networking reference information (versioning policy, TLS cert info, DNS delegation), and lib.rs module/export declarations — all as specified by RFC nodes N0057, N0058, N0061, N0062, N0064, N0066, N0067.

## Purpose
This ticket transforms the RFC design for the server crate into concrete implementation artifacts: the config structs and protocol data structures that form the foundation of siprs-server. These types are the layer-5 (API layer) building blocks that downstream tickets (P4-3 route handlers, P4-4 WS handlers, P4-5 SQLite DAO) depend on. Without this ticket, no server-mode code can compile.

## Motivation
The siprs crate core (layer 1-4) is fully specified and partially implemented (P0/P1/P2-2 accomplished). The server mode is the next architectural layer needed for the zasso ecosystem to provide a network-accessible SIP API. Multiple downstream tickets (P4-series) are blocked on these type definitions. Additionally, the current source tree has `[::STUB::]` markers in sqlite_schema.rs and semver_sip_networking.rs that must be resolved.

## Constraints
- Crate uses rusqlite bundled feature (no system SQLite dependency). This must be reflected in Cargo.toml.
- SeaORM migration management must follow the Makefile convention from mycute project.
- AudioFrameHeader must use repr(C,packed) for ABI stability across Rust version upgrades (current size discovered: 30 bytes, not 24 as originally specified — spec correction needed).
- AuthMode enum has exactly 3 variants (LocalhostOnly, ApiKey, Jwt) — variant count invariant enforced by test.
- ServerConfig must at minimum derive Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize for config file loading.
- DEFAULT_SIPRS_PORT = 3910 — must match the zasso ecosystem port convention (RT_PORT = 3910).

### Goal

### Goal
Close all 8 ABC Inspection gaps in the P2-3 standalone-server implementation: (O-001) add a spec-verification test reading specs/P7-3.md asserting the 4 implementation target files; (O-002) test DatabasePool::open() invalid-path Err and init_schema()/query_tables() 4-table creation; (O-003) pin all 20 path constants to exact RFC S54 values; (O-004) test SequenceGenerator::next() over 1M iterations for monotonicity and uniqueness; (O-005) assert exact ConfigError variants (LocalhostRequiresLoopback, JwtRequiresSecret) instead of message substrings; (O-006) pin CREATE TABLE column types (username TEXT NOT NULL, password BLOB NOT NULL, domain TEXT NOT NULL); (O-007) assert CHANGELOG.md has an Unreleased section and CARGO_PKG_VERSION starts with "0."; (O-008) add an external integration test referencing siprs::{ServerConfig, AuthConfig, AuthMode} at crate root.

### Purpose
The prior implementation produced green tests that did not pin the exact wire/config contracts: path constants were only checked non-empty/unique, error kinds were asserted by message substring, DatabasePool's init_schema()/query_tables() were never exercised, SequenceGenerator monotonicity was tested with a hand-built Vec instead of 1M generator iterations, and no test verified the spec file or crate-root re-exports. The re-implementation makes every contract (C058, C059, C062, C063, C064, C065, C067, C068) verifiable against production code and the P7-3 spec so a violation fails a test assertion.

### Motivation
The ABC Inspection Pipeline confirmed the contracts' preconditions/postconditions/invariants were not translated into precise tests — Evaluation A/C failed for O-001..O-008. Downstream tickets (P4-3 route handlers, P4-4 WS handlers, P4-5 SQLite DAO) depend on these type definitions being correct and provable. Leaving the gaps means contract violations are undetectable, so the re-implementation must ship production types + precise tests together.

### Constraints
- Crate uses rusqlite bundled feature (no system SQLite dependency) — reflected in Cargo.toml.
- SeaORM migration management follows the Makefile convention from the mycute project.
- AudioFrameHeader uses repr(C,packed) for ABI stability; compiled size is 30 bytes, not the RFC's 24 — spec correction applied, tests pin 30.
- AuthMode has exactly 3 variants (LocalhostOnly, ApiKey, Jwt) — variant count invariant enforced by exhaustive-match test.
- ServerConfig must derive Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize, Send, Sync for config file loading.
- DEFAULT_SIPRS_PORT = 3910 must match the zasso ecosystem RT_PORT convention.
- ABC closure: every omission test must exercise production code or the P7-3 spec (no inline re-implementations, no message-substring assertions where exact-variant equality exists).

tickets.notes:
## Implementation steps:
1. Add SQLite dependencies (rusqlite bundled, sea-orm sqlite) to Cargo.toml
2. Implement src/model/sqlite_schema.rs with SeaORM entities for 4 tables
3. Implement src/config/semver_sip_networking.rs with versioning policy constants and TLS info types
4. Add safe AudioFrameHeader::to_bytes() and ::from_bytes() methods in http_ws_protocol.rs
5. Expand test coverage in all affected files — match testUnit spec exactly
6. Fix lying comments in http_ws_protocol.rs tests (24-byte comment → 30-byte)
7. Verify re-exports in lib.rs and config.rs
8. Update CHANGELOG.md unreleased section

## Risks:
- AudioFrameHeader size discrepancy (RFC says 24, actual 30) could cause wire incompatibility if other implementations match RFC literally. Must document this clearly.
- sea-orm with sqlite may add significant compile time. Consider Feature flag gating SQLite-heavy features behind a `sqlite-storage` feature.
- The event_id vs seq field ambiguity in EventMeta/SipEvent could cause confusion in sequence number usage between P2-3 and P4-4.

## Caveats:
- The 30-byte AudioFrameHeader is the actual compiled size (verified by existing tests). The RFC documentation should be updated to match.
- rusqlite bundled feature statically links SQLite — increases binary size by ~1MB but eliminates system dependency.
- Makefile migration commands (gen-migration, migrate-up, etc.) are defined at the workspace level, not in this crate.

## Open items:
- Whether to declare `pub mod model;` in lib.rs or keep model as a private implementation module. Decision: make it private until the crate split (B1 boundary).
- Whether SeaORM migrations should live in siprs or siprs-server crate. Decision: migrations live with sqlite_schema.rs in siprs (types), executed in siprs-server.

## Future improvements:
- After crate split (B1), siprs-core removes SQLite dependency entirely; siprs-server owns the database layer.
- After 1.0 release, add cargo semver-checks CI step per C067 invariant.
- Consider zerocopy crate for safe AudioFrameHeader byte reinterpretation instead of manual to_bytes/from_bytes.

tickets.title: Runtime Infrastructure — Command Serialization and AudioWorkerTask

contracts.precondition: Concurrency model established (P0-2): unbounded MPSC channel created, CoreReactor thread running, RuntimeHandle available
contracts.postcondition: RuntimeCommand enum defined with all 18 variants (the 12 pre-existing + P0-6 M20 ConfConnect/ConfDisconnect + 4 audio-source lifecycle AddAudioSource/RemoveAudioSource/SetAudioSourceGain/MuteAudioSource). Each variant carries a typed oneshot::Sender. DispatchCommand::from_runtime_command maps every variant to a backend execution closure or a dedicated reactor dispatch arm.
contracts.invariant: All PJSUA calls go through the MPSC channel — no direct FFI call outside the reactor thread. oneshot sender is resolved exactly once per command dispatch.

contracts.precondition: AudioMixer defined with: sources DashMap<u64, Arc<Mutex<Box<dyn AsyncAudioSource + Send>>>>, next_source_id AtomicU64, per-source gain map, per-source muted flags
contracts.postcondition: AudioWorkerTask struct defined with spawn() (creates a Tokio blocking task), shutdown() (terminates gracefully), and a frame processing loop. Source lifecycle API defined as RuntimeCommand variants and functional through the reactor-owned AudioMixer: add_audio_source (returns source_id), remove_audio_source (removes by id), set_audio_source_gain (updates clamped gain), mute_audio_source (toggles flag).
contracts.invariant: Sources added/removed at frame boundaries — AudioWorker processes pending lifecycle commands between process_frame iterations. source_id monotonically increases (wraps correctly at u64::MAX). Concurrent add/remove does not corrupt source iteration.

contracts.precondition: AsyncAudioSource trait defined: trait AsyncAudioSource: Send { async fn next_chunk(&mut self, buf: &mut [i16]) -> usize; }
contracts.postcondition: AudioMixer stores Box<dyn AsyncAudioSource + Send> per source_id. AudioWorker calls next_chunk on each source during process_frame and pushes the mixed frame to out_queue. MockAsyncAudioSource implements AsyncAudioSource for testing.
contracts.invariant: next_chunk returns 0 for an exhausted source without panicking. next_chunk fills the buffer partially (returns < buf.len()) for end-of-stream. Implementation is Send + Sync safe.

tickets.background:
[::INSPECTION_FLAGGED::]
This ticket has been flagged by the ABC Inspection Pipeline after completing the implementation lifecycle (make → plan → start → review → resolve). The actual source code was rigorously analyzed against three criteria:

  A — Contract Translation:   Are all Precondition/Postcondition/Invariant contracts accurately translated into test code?
  B — Violation Detection:    Can every contract violation be detected by an existing test assertion?
  C — Test Precision:         Are tests precise and unambiguous (no broad assertions, no missing edge cases)?

Six omissions were confirmed — O-001..O-006 (3 major, 3 minor). Every omission must be fully resolved, and every contract (C011, C035, C036) must be fulfilled in this final implementation round. Complete it this time.

### Goal
Close the ABC Inspection gaps and make the runtime infrastructure layer provably correct: (1) RuntimeCommand covers all 18 variants (incl. QueryState from P7-2, M20 ConfConnect/ConfDisconnect, and the 4 audio-source lifecycle commands), (2) RuntimeHandle exposes working audio-lifecycle submit methods that route through the reactor to a reactor-owned AudioMixer, (3) AudioWorkerTask's process_frame is test-verified end-to-end (next_chunk → gain/mute → mix → out_queue), and (4) MockBackend.conf_connect/conf_disconnect record observable side effects so the ConfConnect/ConfDisconnect dispatch path is provably wired.

### Purpose
The RuntimeCommand enum is the universal command interface that SipClient uses to drive the SIP stack. Every async public API call on SipClient eventually becomes a RuntimeCommand variant submitted via MPSC. The AudioWorkerTask enables per-call audio processing on dedicated Tokio blocking tasks, keeping audio computation off the reactor thread and the async runtime. Source lifecycle (add/remove/gain/mute) becomes a first-class RuntimeCommand capability.

### Motivation
P0-2 established the concurrency model with the base RuntimeCommand variants. P0-4 added the SipError type and M20 error converters. P0-5 added the EventBus and GetAccountInfo variant. P7-2 added QueryState. P0-6 extended the enum with M20 conference commands and the audio-source lifecycle. The ABC Inspection confirmed that although the implementation exists, the test suite does not detect regressions in the ConfConnect/ConfDisconnect dispatch path (O-001), the AudioWorker mix pipeline (O-002), or the audio-lifecycle reactor path (O-003). This re-implementation exists to close those detection gaps.

### Constraints
- Must not break existing RuntimeCommand API (backward-compatible extension).
- AudioMixer uses dashmap::DashMap (not std::sync::Mutex<HashMap>) for lock-free concurrent reads.
- AudioWorkerTask runs on Tokio blocking pool — no tokio::spawn on the reactor thread.
- No real PJSIP FFI calls in this ticket — all backend operations use MockBackend.
- AsyncAudioSource trait uses i16 (PCM S16LE), not f32 (migration is a future concern).
- The reactor must own the AudioMixer instance that audio-lifecycle commands mutate (single-writer rule on the reactor thread).
scope: **Scope of changes (describe each change comprehensively):**

- [src/runtime/command.rs] Action: modify — RuntimeCommand already has all 18 variants (12 pre-existing + 6 P0-6 additions); verify/keep them. Before → After: DispatchCommand::from_runtime_command no longer maps RemoveAudioSource/SetAudioSourceGain/MuteAudioSource to Execute closures returning hardcoded Err(BackendError("audio source lifecycle not yet connected (P0-7)")) (command.rs:349-383); instead they map to new dedicated DispatchCommand variants carrying typed oneshot replies.

- [src/runtime/command.rs] Action: add — new DispatchCommand variants: RemoveAudioSource { source_id: u64, reply: oneshot::Sender<Result<(), ReactorError>> }, SetAudioSourceGain { source_id: u64, gain: f32, reply: ... }, MuteAudioSource { source_id: u64, muted: bool, reply: ... }. API: each carries the mixer-mutation payload + reply. Update Debug/Display and from_runtime_command.

- [src/runtime/handle.rs] Action: add — 4 public async submit methods: submit_add_audio_source(source: Box<dyn AsyncAudioSource + Send>) -> Result<u64, ReactorError>, submit_remove_audio_source(source_id: u64) -> Result<(), ReactorError>, submit_set_audio_source_gain(source_id: u64, gain: f32) -> Result<(), ReactorError>, submit_mute_audio_source(source_id: u64, muted: bool) -> Result<(), ReactorError>. Before → After: the unreachable!("use submit_add_audio_source instead") branch (handle.rs:73-75) becomes a real dispatch; all four follow the submit → DispatchCommand → reactor → oneshot-reply pattern.

- [src/runtime/reactor.rs] Action: add — reactor owns an Arc<AudioMixer> (default-call mixer) alongside client_state. DispatchCommand::AddAudioSource arm (reactor.rs:111-123) calls mixer.add_source(source) and replies Ok(source_id). New arms for RemoveAudioSource/SetAudioSourceGain/MuteAudioSource call mixer.remove_source/set_gain/mute and reply Ok/Err. Before → After: the BackendError stub is replaced with real mixer routing.

- [src/runtime/backend.rs] Action: modify — MockBackend gains observable conf_connect/conf_disconnect side effects (e.g., pub conf_connect_calls: Vec<(i32, i32)> and conf_disconnect_calls: Vec<(i32, i32)> recording (source, sink)). **Out of scope (items intentionally excluded, with justification):**
- Real PJSIP FFI conference-port integration (pjsua_conf_connect / pjsua_conf_disconnect) — deferred to P2-4; requires FFI binding, this ticket uses MockBackend only.
- Audio resampling, stereo/pair alignment, dynamic frame_duration — deferred to P1+ (AudioMixer is mono 8kHz 20ms i16).
- CPAL/microphone capture and real hardware audio I/O — deferred to P1-4.
- Slab-based source allocation for >32 sources — deferred to P1+ (documented future optimization).
- f32 sample-type migration of AsyncAudioSource — deferred to a future round (i16 is the current contract).
**Affected areas (components/systems impacted, even without direct modification):**
- src/runtime/command.rs — DispatchCommand gains up to 3 variants; Display/Debug/from_runtime_command matches must stay exhaustive.

- src/runtime/reactor.rs — reactor loop gains mixer-backed dispatch arms; AddAudioSource stub replaced.
- src/runtime/backend.rs — MockBackend gains observable counters; SipBackend trait unchanged (no implementor breakage).
- src/runtime/audio_worker.rs — test hook for wrap invariant; no production logic change.

- [Implementation steps] 1) Add observable conf_connect/conf_disconnect invocation counters to MockBackend (backend.rs). 2) Add dedicated DispatchCommand variants RemoveAudioSource/SetAudioSourceGain/MuteAudioSource (command.rs) and update from_runtime_command/Debug/Display. 3) Add a reactor-owned Arc<AudioMixer>; wire the AddAudioSource arm to mixer.add_source and the three new arms to mixer ops (reactor.rs). 4) Add RuntimeHandle::submit_add_audio_source / submit_remove_audio_source / submit_set_audio_source_gain / submit_mute_audio_source (handle.rs). 5) Add a #[cfg(test)] next_source_id setter to AudioMixer (audio_worker.rs). 6) Add the O-001..O-006 unit + integration tests. 7) Run make test.

Should AddAudioSource resolve source_id internally or accept a caller-provided ID? Current decision: internal sequential allocation via AtomicU64.

tickets.invariants:
[Normal condition] RuntimeCommand has 18 distinct enum discriminants, each carrying a typed oneshot::Sender; reply channels are always created at construction and replaced by RuntimeHandle::submit()'s fresh channel (never reused). AudioMixer source_id starts at 0 and increments monotonically; per-source gain defaults to 1.0 and muted to false on add_source.
[Error invariant] oneshot::Sender is always resolved (send() called) in every code path of reactor dispatch — including the panic path, which replies Err(ReactorError::BackendError) before setting terminated. AudioMixer state is never partially modified: add_source fully inserts source+gain+mute or is a no-op; remove_source removes all three maps together.
[Internal state invariant] The reactor's AudioMixer is the single source of truth for the default-call audio sources; AudioWorkerTask holds its own Arc<AudioMixer> per call. RuntimeCommand reply channels are consumed exactly once by the reactor. process_frame snapshots source_ids before iteration so concurrent add/remove cannot corrupt iteration.
[Boundary invariant] u64 source_id wraps correctly from MAX to 0 (fetch_add wraps; the next available id after MAX is 0). Max 32 sources documented for slab optimization (future P1+). AudioWorker::process_frame must handle 0 sources (zero-filled silence) and 1 source (passthrough). gain clamped to [0.0, 2.0] on both bounds (negative clamps to 0.0, above 2.0 clamps to 2.0).

RuntimeCommand (src/runtime/command.rs:44-144) — all 18 variants present: Initialize, AddAccount, RemoveAccount, SetRegistration, MakeCall, Hangup, Hold, Unhold, SendDtmf, GetAccountInfo, QueryState, ConfConnect, ConfDisconnect, AddAudioSource, RemoveAudioSource, SetAudioSourceGain, MuteAudioSource, Shutdown. RemoveAudioSource/SetAudioSourceGain/MuteAudioSource map to Execute closures that return a hardcoded Err(BackendError("audio source lifecycle not yet connected (P0-7)")) (command.rs:349-383). These closures only receive &mut dyn SipBackend, so they cannot mutate a mixer — they must become dedicated reactor-loop dispatch arms.

3. RuntimeHandle (handle.rs:24-140) — submit() has unreachable!("use submit_add_audio_source instead") for AddAudioSource (handle.rs:73-75) but NO submit_add_audio_source method exists anywhere in the crate (O-003). The four audio-lifecycle submit methods must be added.

tickets.background:
[::INSPECTION_FLAGGED::]
This ticket has been flagged by the ABC Inspection Pipeline after completing the implementation lifecycle (make → plan → start → review → resolve). The actual source code was rigorously analyzed against three criteria:

  A — Contract Translation:   Are all Precondition/Postcondition/Invariant contracts accurately translated into test code?
  B — Violation Detection:    Can every contract violation be detected by an existing test assertion?
  C — Test Precision:         Are tests precise and unambiguous (no broad assertions, no missing edge cases)?

One or more ABC violations were confirmed (7 omissions: O-001..O-007). This ticket is hereby remanded for re-implementation. Every violation must be fully resolved, and every contract must be fulfilled in this final implementation round.

N0046 defines tracing spans for all public operations and the optional metrics feature. N0047 defines security (SecretString, Authorization redaction) and platform differences (Windows MSVC, macOS frameworks, Linux libs). N0050 defines the optional cpal-input feature and complete usage examples for client init, account management, calling, audio tap, and AI TTS.

### Goal
Add tracing instrumentation to all public operations, implement SecretString for credential safety, define ClientCapabilities as part of the initialization protocol, document platform-specific build requirements, provide comprehensive usage examples — and close all 7 ABC inspection gaps (O-001..O-007) confirmed in the prior implementation round.

### Purpose
Observability ensures debuggability of production SIP calls; SecretString prevents accidental credential leaks via log output (investigating an incident should never expose passwords); ClientCapabilities enables consumers to adapt their feature usage to what the runtime supports; platform documentation reduces build friction across three target OSes.

### Motivation
Without tracing, diagnosing call failures in production is guesswork. Without SecretString, any error-format! or Debug-impl on AuthCredentials leaks the password to logs. Without ClientCapabilities, consumers cannot determine at runtime whether ICE, SRTP, or a specific codec is available. The ABC inspection confirmed 7 testable behaviors that the prior implementation left untested or unimplemented: (O-001) no compile-time #[instrument] attribute-presence test; (O-002) SipClient::new never emits ClientInitialized; (O-003) metrics types not feature-gated; (O-004) no Drop zeroization for SecretString; (O-005) metrics zero-test covers only 4 of 8 defaults; (O-006) no include_str! platform-doc test; (O-007) open_default_microphone_source missing and spec-examples are empty stubs. These gaps block the first production deployment of siprs.

### Constraints
Must work with existing SipClient facade (P0-3) and EventBus (P0-5). SecretString must be zeroize-compatible but optional (behind zeroize feature). All types must be serde-compatible (behind serde feature) for WebSocket serialization (P4-4). tracing spans must not change public API signatures. cpal-input is optional and non-default. Metrics types must be structurally feature-gated (O-003). open_default_microphone_source defers real capture to the cpal crate (P8-4).

- All public SipClient and SipAccountHandle methods have #[tracing::instrument(skip(self, ...))] — enforced by the O-001 source-inspection test (removing any attribute fails red).
- SecretString Display is "[REDACTED]" and Debug is "SecretString([REDACTED])" — never leaks the inner password value; drop zeroizes the heap buffer under #[cfg(feature = "zeroize")] (O-004).
- ClientCapabilities constructable with all fields at safe defaults AND advertised via a ClientInitialized event emitted by SipClient::new() (O-002 — verified by integration test).

## Translatability improvements (Boy Scout Rule)

### 1. src/config/observability_metrics.rs — metrics feature-gating + test precision
**Current**: Metrics types compiled unconditionally; `metrics_types_not_available_without_feature` is an empty no-op (a lying test name). `metrics_registry_starts_at_zero` asserts only 4 of 8 metrics (under-specified).
**Target**: Add structural `#[cfg(feature = "metrics")]` on each metrics type so the source reads as "these types exist only under the metrics feature". Replace the no-op with `metrics_types_are_feature_gated` (source-inspection asserting the cfg attribute precedes each type). Extend `metrics_registry_starts_at_zero` to name all 8 metrics — the test then reads as a complete inventory.

### 2. src/security/security_platform_diffs.rs — drop-zeroization + doc enforcement
**Current**: `impl zeroize::Zeroize` exists but drop does not zeroize (a security gap the doc comment implies is covered: "the inner memory is zeroed on drop"). The doc comment lies.
**Target**: Add `#[cfg(feature = "zeroize")] impl Drop for SecretString` so the comment becomes true; add `secret_string_zeroized_on_drop` buffer-zero test; add `platform_docs_contain_os_notes` include_str! test so the OS-specific build notes are enforced rather than decorative.

### 3. src/client.rs — ClientInitialized emission + instrument enforcement
**Current**: `SipClient::new` returns a receiver but never publishes the initialization result; the `ClientInitialized` variant is dead code. `tracing_and_metrics_specified` asserts only that Cargo.toml contains the substring 'tracing' — it cannot detect removal of `#[instrument]`.
**Target**: Publish `ClientInitialized(ClientCapabilities::new())` after Initialize succeeds so the facade reads as "construct → initialize → advertise capabilities". Add `all_public_client_methods_are_instrumented` (source-inspection) so the tracing contract is provable, replacing the substring check as the primary guard.

### 4. src/api/asyncaudiosrc_adapter.rs — RFC §40 API contract
**Current**: The RFC-specified `open_default_microphone_source` does not exist; examples are empty `fn main() {}` stubs that demonstrate nothing.
**Target**: Add `open_default_microphone_source(format: AudioFormat) -> Result<Box<dyn AsyncAudioSource>, SipError>` behind `#[cfg(feature = "cpal-input")]` (typed STUB body pending cpal/P8-4) so the module reads as the audio-source entry point. Add `spec_examples_reference_public_api_types` so examples become documentation that references the real API.

### 5. Extract hardcoded feature strings into named constants
**Current**: Feature names are compared inline against string literals in tests (e.g., "cpal-input", "metrics") in client.rs and observability_metrics.rs.
**Target**: Define `const FEATURE_CPAL_INPUT: &str = "cpal-input"` and `const FEATURE_METRICS: &str = "metrics"` in a `features` constants module (or per-module consts) for test reuse — prevents drift if a feature is renamed.

tickets.background:
[::INSPECTION_FLAGGED::]
This ticket has been flagged by the ABC Inspection Pipeline after completing the implementation lifecycle (make → plan → start → review → resolve). The actual source code was rigorously analyzed against three criteria:

  A — Contract Translation:   Are all Precondition/Postcondition/Invariant contracts accurately translated into test code?
  B — Violation Detection:    Can every contract violation be detected by an existing test assertion?
  C — Test Precision:         Are tests precise and unambiguous (no broad assertions, no missing edge cases)?

Four ABC violations (O-001..O-004, all minor) were confirmed — all are test-coverage gaps, not implementation defects. This ticket is hereby remanded for re-implementation: every violation must be resolved by adding the missing tests in this final round. Complete it this time.

### Goal
Close the 4 ABC inspection gaps for the type-system foundation already delivered by P4-1: (O-001) enforce the C026 invariant "Registration independent of call ability" with a make_call signature / unit-variant test; (O-002) exhaustively verify the RegistrationState 7×7 transition table (exactly 10 true cells of 49); (O-003) exhaustively verify the CallState 13×13 transition table (exactly 20 true cells of 169) plus the currently-untested can_transition_to predicate and Held→Disconnecting edge; (O-004) enforce SipEventPayload's #[non_exhaustive] attribute with a separate-crate compile test.

### Purpose
The type definitions (AccountId, CallId, AudioSourceId NonZeroU64 newtypes + BiMap runtime-to-native mapping; 36-variant SipEventPayload; 7-state RegistrationState; 13-state CallState) form the shared language across all siprs modules. Without enforceable tests, the invariants they encode — zero-value rejection, native-ID-reuse semantics (newest wins), the "exactly-10-of-49" and "exactly-20-of-169" transition tables, registration/call separation, and #[non_exhaustive] — are only documented in comments and can silently rot: a removed #[non_exhaustive] or an added spurious transition would pass the current suite.

### Motivation
The ABC pipeline (criterion B — violation detection, C — test precision) confirmed the current tests cannot detect: an extra true cell in either state-machine transition table, removal of #[non_exhaustive] from SipEventPayload, or coupling of make_call to registration state. These are exactly the failure modes that would break downstream P3-1 (Account API) and P5-1 (Call API) at the type level. The 4 omissions must be resolved before downstream tickets build on these types.

SipEventPayload enum includes all 25+ variants including new categories (ICE, Transport, Account, Client, Error).

[Error case] AccountId::from_u64(0) returns Err(ZeroValue). CallState::transition(New→Active) returns Err(TransitionError). RegistrationState::transition(Idle→Disabled) returns Err(TransitionError). BiMap::get_native(unknown_id) returns None. SipEventPayload variant enum compiled with _ => {} wildcard (non_exhaustive check).

[Edge case] BiMap handles native ID reuse: insert(a1, n1), remove(a1), insert(a2, n1) — get_runtime(n1) returns a2. RegistrationState transition Expired→Registering (auto retry) followed by Failed (no network) then Registering again (retry). CallState transfer path Active→Transferring→Disconnecting (NOTIFY fail) verifies transfer failure branch. CallState Failed reached from Ringing (4xx), EarlyMedia (5xx), and Connecting (6xx) via 3 distinct paths.

[Happy path] All 4 ABC omissions (O-001..O-004) are closed AND the full original acceptance criteria hold: exhaustive 7×7 RegistrationState table passes (exactly 10 Ok edges, 39 Err); exhaustive 13×13 CallState table passes (exactly 20 Ok edges, 149 Err); CallState::can_transition_to tested for all 20 valid edges; Held→Disconnecting termination edge verified; tests/non_exhaustive.rs compiles as a separate crate matching SipEventPayload with a wildcard arm; make_call signature verified independent of RegistrationState.

[Error case] Violations are detected, not merely absent: adding a spurious true cell to either TRANSITIONS table fails the exhaustive test; removing #[non_exhaustive] from SipEventPayload fails the tests/non_exhaustive.rs build (exhaustive-match error); adding a RegistrationState parameter to make_call fails the O-001 source-inspection test.

[Edge case] Boundary transitions hold: Held→Disconnecting (termination while held) valid; Expired→Registering and Failed→Registering (retry) valid; Disconnected/Failed absorbing (no self-loop, is_terminal true); exactly 4 incoming edges reach Registering (Disabled, Idle, Expired, Failed).

tickets.invariants:
- [Normal condition] Newtype ID construction: AccountId/CallId/AudioSourceId::from_u64(x) succeeds iff x > 0, returns Err(IdError::ZeroValue) iff x == 0. BiMap insert/lookup round-trip: insert(r, n) guarantees get_native(r) == Some(n) and get_runtime(n) == Some(r) until remove(r). RegistrationState transitions: every transition follows exactly one of the 10 defined edges of the 7×7=49-cell table (O-002 exhaustive test enforces exactly 10 true cells). CallState transitions: every transition follows one of the 20 DAG edges of the 13×13=169-cell table (O-003); all non-terminal states can reach Disconnected or Failed.
- [Error invariant] Zero-value ID construction (from_u64(0)) never succeeds — returns Err(IdError::ZeroValue). BiMap never loses data on concurrent access — dashmap interior mutability guarantees crash-consistency. Invalid state-machine transitions never mutate internal state — Err is returned, state unchanged (enforced by the exhaustive negative matrices O-002/O-003). RegistrationState::Failed and Expired do not prevent make_call() — enforced by the O-001 source-inspection signature test.
- [Internal state invariant] BiMap internal state: for all (r, n) pairs, r is unique (RuntimeId is the primary key); NativeId n may be reused — the newest (r, n) pair wins on insert (bimap_handles_native_id_reuse). RegistrationState machine: internal transition table enumerates exactly (7×7)=49 boolean predicates, of which exactly 10 are true (the 10 RFC §17.1 edges). CallState machine: table enumerates exactly (13×13)=169 boolean predicates, of which exactly 20 are true, covering all outgoing/incoming/hold/transfer/termination paths. SipEventPayload is #[non_exhaustive] — enforced by the O-004 separate-crate compile test.
- [Boundary invariant] AccountId/CallId/AudioSourceId NonZeroU64 domain: [1, u64::MAX]. BiMap capacity: unbounded (backed by dashmap). RegistrationState retry: Failed→Registering and Expired→Registering must not cause an infinite loop — controlled by ClientConfig::registration_retry_count (P3-1 scope). CallState termination: Held→Disconnecting (termination while held) and Active→Disconnecting are both valid; Disconnected and Failed are absorbing (no self-loop, is_terminal true). CallState: max_calls concurrent limit enforced by Call API (P3-1/P5-1 scope), not by the state machine itself (transition() is pure — takes only from/to).

tickets.background:
- 【Goal】Define and implement the DTMF specification (DtmfMethod, DtmfReceivedInfo with the method:DtmfMethod field and contract-correct Option<u16>/Option<i8> field types), the AsyncAudioSource adapter types (ErasedAudioSource, SyncAudioSource, SyncSourceAdapter<T>), and the IncomingCall / REFER-transfer types (IncomingCall, IncomingCallConfig, ReferRequest.replaces, TransferInfo) per RFC nodes N0028 / N0032 / N0048. Close the 4 ABC inspection omissions (O-001..O-004) and resolve the TS-003 orphan-ticket crime in src/config/versioning_policy.rs so the ticket survives a full make → plan → start → review → resolve cycle this time.
- 【Purpose】Provide type-safe DTMF signalling primitives for SIP call control (send + receive with DtmfPolicy validation). Enable downstream crates to implement custom async audio sources for AudioMixer via the SyncAudioSource → SyncSourceAdapter bridge and the ErasedAudioSource dynamic-dispatch wrapper. Expose incoming call metadata (from_uri, to_uri, display_name, headers, offered_codecs, has_early_media) and REFER-based transfer capabilities (ReferRequest.replaces, TransferCompleted) to application code as typed SipEventPayload variants.
- 【Motivation】The ABC Inspection Pipeline remanded P8-4 with one critical omission (O-001: ReferRequest.replaces missing and zero tests construct ReferRequest/TransferInfo, so the C049 invariant and acceptance criteria are unenforced), one major (O-002: DtmfReceivedInfo.duration_ms widened to Option<u64> and volume_dbm0 to Option<i32> vs the contract Option<u16>/Option<i8>, and no None/0/MAX edge tests), and two minor (O-003: no SipEventPayload::DtmfSent construction test; O-004: no 65536-sample SyncAudioSource boundary test). The versioning_policy.rs STUB (TS-003) is an orphaned ticket reference that must be resolved this round. Every contract (C029/C030/C033/C049) must be translated into precise test assertions so that removing any contract behavior fails a test.
- 【Constraints】MSRV 1.95 — RPITIT is stable but the existing AsyncAudioSource uses #[async_trait] for Box<dyn> compatibility in AudioMixer; the ErasedAudioSource blanket impl provides the dynamic-dispatch path without refactoring existing implementors. Do NOT add new crate dependencies — all required derives (Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq) are std. Keep the canonical 4-variant DtmfMethod (Rfc2833, Rfc4733, Info, Inband) from account_config_spec.rs; leave the separate 2-variant DtmfMethod in m20_dtmfsent_twophase.rs intact to avoid breaking DtmfSentInfo consumers (unification is an open item, not a forced change). Maintain backward compatibility with existing DtmfReceivedInfo consumers (m20_native_event_conv.rs constructs with None/None, so field-type narrowing is compatible). ReferRequest gains the additive replaces: Option<String> field; all struct-literal construction sites must add it.
scope: Changes (path): src/api/event_model_payload_bus.rs (MODIFY) — narrow DtmfReceivedInfo.duration_ms to Option<u16> and volume_dbm0 to Option<i8>; add ReferRequest.replaces: Option<String>; add payload-construction and edge/boundary tests. src/api/asyncaudiosrc_adapter.rs (MODIFY) — add the 65536-sample SyncAudioSource/SyncSourceAdapter boundary test; update the open_default_microphone_source STUB marker. src/config/versioning_policy.rs (MODIFY) — implement VersionPolicy per N0006 §4.1 and remove the TS-003 STUB marker. src/state/m20_native_event_conv.rs (VERIFY) — DtmfReceivedInfo construction still compiles after type narrowing.

Changes (action): 1) Change DtmfReceivedInfo field types to the contract types. 2) Add ReferRequest.replaces field. 3) Add the missing event-payload construction tests and boundary tests. 4) Implement VersionPolicy (semver phase classification, CHANGELOG requirement, 1.0+ MAJOR/MINOR/PATCH semantics) with a #[cfg(test)] module. 5) Re-scope the microphone-source STUB to MUST RESOLVE with the cpal-dependency constraint reason.

Changes (detail): DtmfReceivedInfo { method: DtmfMethod, digit: char, duration_ms: Option<u16>, volume_dbm0: Option<i8> } (was Option<u64>/Option<i32>). ReferRequest { call_id: CallId, refer_to: String, referred_by: Option<String>, replaces: Option<String> }. VersionPolicy type in src/config/versioning_policy.rs implementing the N0006 §4.1 rules (0.x CHANGELOG-based breaking changes; 1.0+ MAJOR = breaking / MINOR = additive / PATCH = bugfix; security-fix PATCH exception). New tests: payload_dtmf_sent, payload_refer_received, payload_transfer_completed, dtmf_received_info_none_edge, dtmf_received_info_duration_boundary, dtmf_received_info_volume_boundary, refer_request_blind, refer_request_full, transfer_info_fields, sync_source_adapter_65536_buffer, version_policy_0x_and_10x.

Changes (before/after): BEFORE — DtmfReceivedInfo.duration_ms: Option<u64>, volume_dbm0: Option<i32>; ReferRequest { call_id, refer_to, referred_by }; versioning_policy.rs holds only a doc comment + STUB; no DtmfSent/ReferReceived/TransferCompleted payload tests. AFTER — duration_ms: Option<u16>, volume_dbm0: Option<i8>; ReferRequest gains replaces: Option<String>; VersionPolicy implemented with tests and the STUB marker removed; payload_* tests assert each event variant; the 65536-sample buffer boundary is covered.

Changes (API): DtmfReceivedInfo field types narrow (Option<u64> → Option<u16>, Option<i32> → Option<i8>) — a type-level change affecting struct-literal construction sites (only m20_native_event_conv.rs today, None-compatible). ReferRequest gains the additive replaces: Option<String> field. VersionPolicy is a new public type in the config domain. No changes to the AsyncAudioSource / ErasedAudioSource / SyncAudioSource / SyncSourceAdapter signatures (already present from P5-2/P0-6).
Changes (schema): None — pure Rust API types; no serialization, DB, or wire-format changes. DtmfConfig::sent_timeout_ms and IncomingCallConfig already exist (P7-2 / P5-2) and are untouched.

Changes (config): No AccountConfig or ClientConfig changes required for the P8-4 core scope. versioning_policy.rs is a standalone config-domain module (N0006) implemented independently of account/client config to avoid entanglement.

Changes (dep): No new crate dependencies. All derives (Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq) are std. VersionPolicy uses only std. The microphone source stays behind the cpal-input feature gate because adding the cpal crate is prohibited by the ticket constraint.

Non-change (item): PJSIP FFI callback wiring (on_dtmf_digit / on_incoming_call / on_refer) and the Reactor event dispatch — separate P5-3 ticket. RPITIT refactoring of the existing #[async_trait] AsyncAudioSource — deferred. Attended transfer end-to-end (REFER with Replaces targeting a live call) — depends on the multi-call state machine, P5-3+. Unification of the 2-variant DtmfMethod with the 4-variant canonical — open item, not forced.

Non-change (why): The P8-4 scope is the pure type definitions + test assertions that close the ABC gaps. FFI wiring needs a live PJSIP stack; RPITIT refactor risks the working AudioMixer integration; attended transfer needs multi-call semantics; DtmfMethod unification would break DtmfSentInfo consumers (P7-2 tests). Each is a separate, larger change better owned by a dedicated ticket.

Impact (component): src/api/event_model_payload_bus.rs — event payload structs (DtmfReceivedInfo, ReferRequest) + SipEventPayload variants. src/config/versioning_policy.rs — new VersionPolicy type (additive). src/api/asyncaudiosrc_adapter.rs — test-only change + STUB re-scope. src/state/m20_native_event_conv.rs — DtmfReceivedInfo construction (None-compatible). runtime/audio_worker consumers — ErasedAudioSource blanket impl adds an impl boundary with zero migration cost.

Impact (nature): API surface expansion (additive: replaces field, VersionPolicy) + field-type narrowing (minor breaking for DtmfReceivedInfo literal constructors). Existing Default implementations and None-construction paths remain compatible. No behavioral change to event dispatch.

Impact (response): Downstream crates constructing DtmfReceivedInfo must pass Option<u16>/Option<i8> values (u64/i32 literals beyond the range fail to compile — intended, enforces the boundary invariant). ReferRequest constructors must add replaces: Option<String>. VersionPolicy is additive with no consumer impact.

Reason: NOT TESTABLE at the P8-4 type level — the end-to-end flow depends on the live multi-call PJSIP state machine and call-lingering semantics, which cannot be exercised without a running PJSIP stack. This is NOT A DEFECT: ReferRequest.replaces (added in P8-4) fully models the attended-transfer payload and the type is unit-tested; only the integration wiring is deferred. Alternative verification: Layer-4 integration test with a live SIP server in a future P5-3 ticket.

- Item: Real microphone capture via open_default_microphone_source. Reason: NOT TESTABLE in P8-4 — the ticket Constraints prohibit adding the cpal crate dependency, which is required for device capture; the function stays behind the cpal-input feature and returns a typed error. This is NOT A DEFECT: the RFC §40 signature is verified by the C051 signature test and the feature gate is honest about the missing device backend. Alternative verification: C051 compile-time signature test; device capture deferred to a cpal-authorized future ticket.

- Item: PJSIP callback timing for on_dtmf_digit / on_incoming_call / on_refer. Reason: NOT TESTABLE without a live PJSIP v2.x stack — the exact callback signature and invocation context are runtime FFI-linked. This is NOT A DEFECT: the type definitions (DtmfReceivedInfo, IncomingCall, ReferRequest, TransferInfo) and the DtmfSent 500ms timeout fallback are fully unit-tested; only callback-to-event conversion is deferred to P5-3. Alternative verification: the spawn_dtmf_sent_timeout fallback is tested with tokio::time; Layer-3 integration with a Docker SIP server in a future ticket.
acceptanceCriteria: - [Happy path] DtmfReceivedInfo constructed with method=Rfc4733, digit='5', duration_ms=Some(100), volume_dbm0=Some(-15) round-trips all four fields; SipEventPayload::DtmfReceived matches. ReferRequest with replaces: Some("sip:carol@example.com") and TransferInfo with status_code=200 construct and match their SipEventPayload variants (ReferReceived / TransferCompleted). SyncSourceAdapter wraps a SyncAudioSource and AsyncAudioSource::next_chunk returns the correct sample count; the ErasedAudioSource blanket impl works for MockAsyncAudioSource. IncomingCall with from_uri / to_uri / headers / codecs / has_early_media constructs. VersionPolicy classifies a 1.0+ MAJOR breaking change correctly.

- [Error case] AccountConfig::validate with empty DtmfPolicy::send_methods or receive_methods returns Err(SipErrorKind::InvalidConfig). DtmfPolicy::is_send_allowed / is_receive_allowed return false for disallowed methods. SyncSourceAdapter with an exhausted inner source returns 0. IncomingCall with empty from_uri / to_uri does not panic on access or Debug formatting. spawn_dtmf_sent_timeout publishes DtmfSent{Err(Timeout)} after the deadline. VersionPolicy rejects an invalid change classification without panicking.

- [Edge case] DtmfReceivedInfo with duration_ms=None and volume_dbm0=None remains well-formed; duration_ms at u16::MAX and volume_dbm0 at i8::MIN / i8::MAX round-trip unchanged. IncomingCall with empty offered_codecs (pre-negotiation) and empty headers is accepted; has_early_media=false behaves identically to true. SyncAudioSource buffer sizes at both extremes (0 and 65536) are handled without overflow. ReferRequest blind transfer has replaces=None — the first-class blind-transfer path.

tickets.notes:
- 【Implementation steps】1. src/api/event_model_payload_bus.rs: narrow DtmfReceivedInfo.duration_ms → Option<u16> and volume_dbm0 → Option<i8>; add ReferRequest.replaces: Option<String>; refresh struct doc comments. 2. event_model_payload_bus tests: extend payload_dtmf_received with a volume_dbm0 assertion; add payload_dtmf_sent, payload_refer_received, payload_transfer_completed; add DtmfReceivedInfo None / 0 / u16::MAX / i8::MIN / i8::MAX edge+boundary tests; add ReferRequest blind + full construction and TransferInfo construction tests. 3. src/api/asyncaudiosrc_adapter.rs tests: add the 65536-sample SyncAudioSource / SyncSourceAdapter boundary test; re-scope the open_default_microphone_source STUB marker to MUST RESOLVE with the cpal constraint reason. 4. src/config/versioning_policy.rs: implement VersionPolicy per N0006 §4.1 with a #[cfg(test)] module; remove the TS-003 STUB marker. 5. src/state/m20_native_event_conv.rs: verify DtmfReceivedInfo construction still compiles after narrowing (None is type-agnostic). 6. Run `make check-be` and `make test` until green.
- 【Risks】Field-type narrowing (Option<u64> → Option<u16>, Option<i32> → Option<i8>) is a breaking change for any struct-literal consumer passing values beyond u16/i8 — audit all construction sites (only m20_native_event_conv.rs today, None-compatible). ReferRequest.replaces is additive but breaks struct-literal constructors that omit it — audit event_model_payload_bus consumers (zero external references today). The separate 2-variant DtmfMethod in m20_dtmfsent_twophase.rs remains a type-confusion risk; unification is preferred but deferred to avoid breaking DtmfSentInfo consumers (P7-2 tests depend on it).
- 【Caveats】DtmfConfig::sent_timeout_ms already exists in src/config.rs (P7-2 O-002 closure) — do NOT re-add it to account_config_spec.rs. The open_default_microphone_source STUB cannot be fully resolved without cpal (no-new-deps constraint) — the marker must be updated to MUST RESOLVE with the reason, not deleted. VersionPolicy (N0006 §4.1) is a distinct domain from the DTMF/audio/call scope — implement it as a standalone config type so it does not entangle account config.
- 【Open items】Unify the 2-variant DtmfMethod (m20_dtmfsent_twophase.rs) with the 4-variant canonical (account_config_spec.rs)? Option (a) use the canonical in DtmfSentInfo — breaks P7-2 tests; option (b) keep separate and add a From conversion. Deferred to avoid scope creep. Real microphone capture needs a cpal-authorized ticket. The RPITIT refactor of AsyncAudioSource (native async fn in trait) remains deferred; the ErasedAudioSource wrapper covers dynamic dispatch in the meantime.
- 【Future】P5-3 wires DtmfReceived / IncomingCall / ReferReceived / TransferCompleted events through PJSIP callbacks in the Reactor. Attended transfer (REFER with Replaces targeting a live call) becomes first-class once the multi-call state machine lands. VersionPolicy will drive release automation (CHANGELOG enforcement, semver classification checks) in a later tooling ticket.

tickets.invariants:
- 【Normal establishment】DtmfPolicy always has >= 1 send_method and >= 1 receive_method (enforced in AccountConfig::validate() returning SipErrorKind::InvalidConfig otherwise). DtmfReceivedInfo is always constructed with method + digit populated; duration_ms and volume_dbm0 are Option fields typed Option<u16>/Option<i8> that stay None when the remote endpoint reports no data. AsyncAudioSource::next_chunk and ErasedAudioSource::next_chunk return 0 when the source is exhausted and never panic. SyncSourceAdapter<T> delegates every call to the inner SyncAudioSource::next_chunk without adding logic.
- 【Invariant on error】DTMF method validation helpers (DtmfPolicy::is_send_allowed / is_receive_allowed) return bool and never panic; empty-policy rejection lives in AccountConfig::validate() and returns Err(SipErrorKind::InvalidConfig). SyncSourceAdapter with an exhausted inner source returns 0, never garbage. IncomingCall with empty from_uri/to_uri remains a valid, Debug-printable struct (no panic on field access). spawn_dtmf_sent_timeout always publishes DtmfSent{Err(Timeout)} after the deadline — the async completion event is emitted even when the PJSIP callback is absent.
- 【Internal state invariant】ErasedAudioSource blanket impl <T: AsyncAudioSource + Send> compiles for every concrete source type — no manual per-type impl required. SyncSourceAdapter<T> implements AsyncAudioSource + Send exactly when T: SyncAudioSource + Send. DtmfReceivedInfo / ReferRequest / TransferInfo / IncomingCall implement Clone + Debug (compile-time verified); DtmfMethod implements Clone + Copy + Debug + PartialEq + Eq. ReferRequest::replaces is Option<String> — the blind transfer (REFER without Replaces) is the first-class flow. DtmfConfig::sent_timeout_ms (src/config.rs) drives the DtmfSent fallback timer with DEFAULT_DTMF_SENT_TIMEOUT_MS == 500.
- 【Boundary invariant】duration_ms accepts the full [0, u16::MAX] range without truncation (field type Option<u16>). volume_dbm0 accepts the full [i8::MIN, i8::MAX] range (field type Option<i8>). SyncAudioSource buffer sizes at both extremes — 0 and 65536 samples — are handled without overflow or panic. IncomingCall offered_codecs and headers accept the empty vec (pre-negotiation state) as well as single/multi-element vecs. IncomingCallConfig reject_timeout_ms accepts 0 and custom values.
tickets.instrumentation:
- 【Logging】DTMF send/receive activity logged at debug level with call_id, method, and digit (log::debug!("dtmf received call={} method={:?} digit={}", ...)). VersionPolicy classification decisions logged at debug when a change is classified (0.x vs 1.0+ path). No new PII beyond the SIP URIs already carried in event payloads.
- 【Metrics】No new metrics in P8-4 (type-only scope). AudioMixer already observes source exhaustion (next_chunk == 0); the 65536-boundary test guards the buffer-fill path. A DtmfSent-timeout count can be derived downstream from the existing DtmfSent event stream (status == Err(Timeout)).
- 【Error tracking】All config validation errors propagate as Result via ? and surface as SipErrorKind::InvalidConfig (AccountConfig::validate). spawn_dtmf_sent_timeout publishes DtmfSent{Err(Timeout)} on the EventBus rather than logging-and-swallowing — errors reach subscribers. VersionPolicy rejects invalid classifications with a typed error, never panics.
- 【Health check】No health-check surface change. The compile-time trait-bound tests (Send, Clone, Debug) act as static health gates — a build failure signals a broken invariant. The C051 signature test gates the microphone-source signature behind the cpal-input feature.

tickets.boyScoutPlan:
Translatability improvement plan (Boy Scout Rule — leave code cleaner than found):
- Function names as verb phrases: DtmfPolicy::is_send_allowed / is_receive_allowed already read as verbs — keep. VersionPolicy methods must be verbs: classify_change(), requires_changelog(), current_phase() — never generic names like process() or check().
- Variable names as domain concepts: DtmfReceivedInfo fields already use SIP domain terms (method, digit, duration_ms, volume_dbm0). ReferRequest.replaces is the domain term for the Replaces header — no generic option. VersionPolicy must name the semver concepts (phase, change_kind, changelog) not raw strings.
- One function one responsibility: VersionPolicy::classify_change answers only "what kind of change" — CHANGELOG gating is a separate method requires_changelog(). Do not merge classification with release automation.
- Hardcoded values as named constants: DEFAULT_AUTO_REJECT_TIMEOUT_MS (incoming_call_refer.rs:36) and DEFAULT_DTMF_SENT_TIMEOUT_MS (m20_dtmfsent_twophase.rs:64) already exist — keep. Any new versioning thresholds become named constants in versioning_policy.rs.
- No error swallowing: AccountConfig::validate errors propagate via ?. spawn_dtmf_sent_timeout publishes errors on the EventBus instead of log-and-continue. VersionPolicy returns typed errors for invalid classifications.
- Proactive cleanups in touched files: update the stale [::STUB::] P0-1 reference in versioning_policy.rs (resolved by implementation); re-scope the microphone STUB to MUST RESOLVE with the cpal constraint reason instead of leaving a misleading P8-4 reference that would later read as a completed-ticket staleness crime; in event_model_payload_bus.rs, align the DtmfReceivedInfo doc comment with the narrowed Option<u16>/Option<i8> types and add the replaces field doc to ReferRequest.

tickets.title: Generate PJSIP bindings via bindgen behind the pjsua-native feature once PJSIP headers are available in the build environment, and uncomment the wrapper.h includes

contracts.precondition: Rust FFI required to call C PJSUA library functions. Concurrency model defines reactor thread for serialized command execution.
contracts.postcondition: PJSIP FFI layer created with: (1) ffi::bindings module generated by bindgen build.rs with allowlist pattern, (2) PjOwnedStr safe wrapper for pj_str_t with Rust-owned Vec<u8> backing, (3) extern C callback functions enqueue NativeEvent, (4) runtime/ modules use only safe SipBackend trait.
contracts.invariant: All unsafe code isolated to ffi/ module. No unsafe keyword in runtime/, client.rs, or config/. Compile-time lint enforces unsafe isolation.

contracts.precondition: PJSUA C library uses pj_pool_t for memory allocation. Callback parameters valid only within callback scope.
contracts.postcondition: pj_str_t always has Rust-owned backing (Vec<u8>). Native callback pointers not held beyond callback scope. pj_pool_t memory never embedded in Rust structs.
contracts.invariant: pj_str_t values outside FFI calls always point to Rust-owned memory. Original PJSUA ptr only used as source for immediate copy, never stored.

tickets.background: Source ticket P4-2 specified the audio format types, PairAligner, resampler and codec policy. During that implementation the build-time bindgen generation was left as stubs in build.rs and wrapper.h because PJSIP headers were not yet available in the build environment. This work item resolves those markers by generating PJSIP bindings via bindgen behind a new `pjsua-native` feature and uncommenting the wrapper.h includes once the headers are present.
scope: Changes (path): build.rs (MODIFY) — implement the bindgen build script: `pjsua-native` feature detection, PJSIP header-root resolution per RFC §28 search order, allowlist configuration, OUT_DIR emission
Changes (path): wrapper.h (MODIFY) — uncomment `#include <pjsua.h>`, `#include <pjmedia.h>`, `#include <pjmedia-codec/opus.h>` behind the feature
Changes (path): Cargo.toml (MODIFY) — add `pjsua-native` feature to [features]; add [build-dependencies] bindgen; add `pjsua-native` to lints.rust check-cfg (line 40)
Changes (path): src/ffi/bindings.rs (MODIFY) — gate the hand-written stub aliases behind `#[cfg(not(feature = "pjsua-native"))]` so bindgen output replaces them exactly when the feature is on
Changes (context): src/ffi/pj_str.rs — PjOwnedStr / pj_str_t Rust-owned backing (contract C057) stays the safe wrapper over generated bindings
Non-change (item): Replacing hand-coded PJSIP constants (P8-18) and wiring real FFI call sites (P8-20) are separate tickets that CONSUME the generated bindings
Non-change (why): The stub-resolution scope is the build pipeline only; constant replacement and FFI call wiring need the generated bindings to exist first and are tracked by P8-18/P8-20
Impact (component): build.rs, wrapper.h, Cargo.toml, src/ffi/bindings.rs. Enabling `pjsua-native` makes the crate build require a system PJSIP install (RFC §28 package lists)
Impact (nature): additive feature flag + build-script behavior. The default build (feature off) is unchanged and requires no external C library
Impact (response): downstream CI that enables `pjsua-native` must install PJSIP headers/libs per RFC §28.3-§28.4 or use the prebuilt/vendored path
Out of scope: PJSIP runtime callbacks, media handling, codec policy (P4-2 content) — unrelated to build-time binding generation
testUnit: UT: [Normal] C038-Post: build feature detection — a helper `pjsua_native_enabled()` reads CARGO_FEATURE_PJSUA_NATIVE and returns true/false; both branches assert
UT: [Normal] C038-Post: header-root resolution — resolve_header_root returns vendor/prebuilt/{triple}/include when present, else vendor/pjsip source path (pure path logic, no C toolchain needed)
UT: [Normal] C038-Post: allowlist membership — the bindgen allowlist array contains pjsua_call_get_info, pjsua_acc_id, pj_str_t, pjsua_call_info (compile-time/unit assertion on the const array)

UT: [Normal] C057: PjOwnedStr::new copies input bytes into Rust-owned Vec<u8> and produces a pj_str_t whose ptr points into that Vec — existing pj_str tests extended to assert ownership after the FFI module change
UT: [Error] C038: header-root missing with feature enabled — resolve_header_root returns Err carrying the RFC §28 dependency hint instead of panicking

UT: [Boundary] C038-Inv: stub fallback compile — with the feature off, src/ffi/bindings.rs stub aliases compile and pjsua_call_get_info returns PJ_SUCCESS for a non-null info (existing test kept green)
UT: [Invariant] C038-Inv: unsafe isolation — grep-based compile-time test asserts zero `unsafe` matches under src/runtime/, src/client.rs, src/config/ (excluding test code)
testIntegration: IT: [Build] Default build — `cargo build` (no features) succeeds on a machine without PJSIP installed; the stub-alias path is exercised
IT: [Build] Feature build — `cargo build --features pjsua-native` against a vendored/Docker PJSIP install runs bindgen and links pjsua_* symbols; verify OUT_DIR contains the generated bindings
IT: [Verification] Symbol exposure — with the feature on, `cargo doc`/compile-time use of pjsua_call_get_info and pjsua_call_info from the generated bindings type-checks (feeds P8-18/P8-20)
IT: [Failure] Missing headers — `cargo build --features pjsua-native` with an empty header root fails with the user-friendly message from the RFC §28 package list, and exits non-zero
testExceptions: - Item: Executing bindgen itself in a unit test. Reason: bindgen needs a real C toolchain and PJSIP headers, which the default CI build does not install; bindgen execution is exercised only by the integration/build job with `pjsua-native` enabled.

- Item: Link-level verification that pjsua_* symbols resolve. Reason: requires a live PJSUA shared/static library; unit tests cannot link against a C library that is absent from the default build environment.
- Item: Byte-for-byte comparison of generated bindings. Reason: bindgen output varies by clang/bindgen version; tests assert symbol presence and behavior, not exact generated text.

- Item: Full RFC §28 source-build fallback (CMake) in unit tests. Reason: building PJSIP from vendor/pjsip sources takes minutes and requires cmake + per-OS system packages; it is covered by a dedicated integration/build job, not by `make test`.
acceptanceCriteria: 【Happy path】Adding `pjsua-native` to the feature set with PJSIP headers available causes build.rs to run bindgen against wrapper.h and emit `pjsua_*` FFI declarations into OUT_DIR; `cargo build --features pjsua-native` succeeds and links.
【Happy path】build.rs resolves the PJSIP header root per RFC §28.1 search order (vendor/prebuilt/{target-triple}/include first, then vendor/pjsip source build) and passes wrapper.h to bindgen.
【Happy path】wrapper.h uncomments `#include <pjsua.h>`, `#include <pjmedia.h>`, and `#include <pjmedia-codec/opus.h>` when the `pjsua-native` feature is enabled.
【Happy path】The bindgen allowlist restricts generated declarations to the symbol subset siprs uses (pjsua_acc_id, pjsua_call_id, pj_str_t, pjsua_call_get_info, etc.), keeping compile times low.
【Error case】With the feature disabled (default), the crate compiles with no bindgen and no PJSIP installation using the stub aliases in src/ffi/bindings.rs — the default build must not fail.

【Error case】With the feature enabled but headers/libraries missing, build.rs fails with a user-friendly error that names the missing dependency and references the RFC §28 per-OS package list — not a raw clang/bindgen error.

【Edge case】The generated bindings and the stub aliases are mutually exclusive: exactly one compiles depending on the feature flag; `check-cfg` lists `pjsua-native` so `cargo check` emits no unexpected-cfg warning.
【Invariant】No `unsafe` appears outside the ffi/ module after the build change (C038); build.rs itself contains no unsafe.

tickets.notes:
- Stub markers resolved: build.rs:8 (covers build.rs:8,11), wrapper.h:6.
- Implementation steps: 1) add `pjsua-native = []` to Cargo.toml [features] and `pjsua-native` to lints.rust check-cfg (line 40); 2) add `[build-dependencies]` bindgen (pin a version, e.g. bindgen = "0.69"); 3) implement build.rs main() per RFC §28: detect the feature via CARGO_FEATURE_PJSUA_NATIVE, resolve the header root (vendor/prebuilt/{triple}/include → vendor/pjsip), run bindgen with the allowlist against wrapper.h, write to OUT_DIR; 4) uncomment the wrapper.h includes; 5) feature-gate src/ffi/bindings.rs stub aliases behind `#[cfg(not(feature = "pjsua-native"))]`.
- Related tickets: P3-2 (original FFI layer, contracts C038/C057), P8-18 (replace hand-coded PJSIP constants with bindgen output — consumes this ticket), P8-20 (wire real FFI call sites — consumes this ticket).
- Caveat: bindgen output varies by clang/bindgen version — the allowlist keeps the generated surface small and reviewable; pin the bindgen dependency in Cargo.toml. Verify with `make check-be` (default, stub path) and a feature-enabled build in a PJSIP-capable CI job.
tickets.invariants: 【C038】All unsafe code is isolated to the ffi/ module; no unsafe keyword appears in runtime/, client.rs, or config/ (compile-time enforced). 【C057】pj_str_t values outside FFI calls always point to Rust-owned memory (Vec<u8>); the original PJSUA pointer is used only as a source for immediate copy, never stored. 【Feature exclusivity】When `pjsua-native` is off, the crate builds with no external C library and no bindgen; when it is on, the bindgen-generated declarations replace the hand-written stubs exactly once — both are never compiled together. 【Build determinism】The bindgen allowlist is a fixed symbol set so generated output stays minimal and reviewable.
tickets.instrumentation:
- build.rs emits cargo:rerun-if-env-changed=CARGO_FEATURE_PJSUA_NATIVE and cargo:rerun-if-changed=wrapper.h so the script reruns when inputs change.
- build.rs prints which build path was taken (prebuilt / source-build / stub fallback) via println! so `cargo build -v` CI logs show the mode that produced the crate.
- When the feature is enabled but headers are missing, build.rs prints the RFC §28 package list to stderr with a `cargo:warning=` diagnostic so the failure reason is visible without a full build log.

The stub aliases in src/ffi/bindings.rs keep the crate compiling.' wrapper.h:6-10 — the three `#include` directives (`<pjsua.h>`, `<pjmedia.h>`, `<pjmedia-codec/opus.h>`) are commented out. Cargo.toml [features] (lines 15-37) declares no `pjsua-native` feature and there is no [build-dependencies] section, so `bindgen` is not available to build.rs; lints.rust check-cfg (line 40) lists only `cpal-input`. src/ffi/bindings.rs (lines 16-193) holds hand-written stub aliases (pjsua_acc_id, pjsua_call_id, pj_str_t, pjsua_call_info) and a stub pjsua_call_get_info (lines 124-133) that keep the crate compiling without a PJSIP install; the module header comment (lines 3-6) already promises bindgen output replaces it under `pjsua-native`. RFC §28.1-§28.4 specify the build.rs search order (prebuilt → source build → bindgen) and per-OS package requirements. A real implementation must: add the feature, add bindgen to [build-dependencies], implement header-root resolution + allowlist + OUT_DIR emission, uncomment wrapper.h, and feature-gate the stub aliases so bindgen output replaces them only when the feature is enabled.

tickets.background: Source ticket P1-3 specified the 4-layer test strategy, CI/CD pipeline, and panic policy. During that implementation the five example binaries were left as API-surface documentation stubs because the full CLI/PJSIP runtime was deferred — each example builds a ClientConfig, calls SipClient::new, and returns without performing its named operation. This work item resolves those markers by implementing the examples as runnable binaries with CLI args, real SipClient/PJSIP operations, and integration tests.
scope: Changes (path): examples/account_register.rs (MODIFY) — parse CLI args (host/port/username/domain/password), add an account, and register it per RFC §41.2
Changes (path): examples/audio_tap.rs (MODIFY) — parse CLI args, subscribe audio for a call, and stream AudioChunkPair frames per RFC §41.4
Changes (path): examples/client_init.rs (MODIFY) — parse CLI args and construct SipClient with transports/STUN per RFC §41.1
Changes (path): examples/make_call.rs (MODIFY) — parse CLI args (target URI), dial an OutgoingCallRequest, and wait for ring/connect events per RFC §41.3
Changes (path): examples/tts_source.rs (MODIFY) — parse CLI args, implement a real TtsStreamSource over mpsc, add it as an audio source, and set gain per RFC §41.5

Changes (path): Cargo.toml (MODIFY) — drop `autoexamples = false` and the `spec-examples` required-features gate once the referenced types exist; add the `cli` feature to the example builds if clap is used
Changes (path): tests/ (ADD) — Layer 5 integration tests that drive the example flows against MockBackend (contract C066)

Non-change (why): The example bodies depend on SipClient/account/call types that earlier tickets provide; the feature gate stays only until those exist

Impact (response): `make check-be` must still pass with the examples gated; integration tests run under `make test`

- Item: Real microphone capture in audio_tap. Reason: device capture requires the optional `cpal-input` feature (P8-7) and physical audio hardware; the example uses an injected source so it runs headless.

- Item: Verifying exact PJSIP call-state timing in make_call. Reason: ringing/connect timing depends on the live stack and network; integration tests assert event ordering with MockBackend, not wall-clock SIP behavior.
acceptanceCriteria: 【Happy path】Each of the five example binaries (account_register, audio_tap, client_init, make_call, tts_source) parses CLI args and runs against a real SipClient, performing its named operation instead of returning immediately.
【Happy path】account_register constructs an AccountConfig from CLI args and calls account.register(), exiting after registration completes or fails cleanly.
【Happy path】client_init constructs SipClient with transports/STUN per RFC §41.1 and reports the client capabilities.
【Happy path】make_call dials an OutgoingCallRequest to the CLI target URI and waits for OutgoingCallRinging / CallConnected / CallRejected events per RFC §41.3.
【Happy path】audio_tap subscribes to call audio via subscribe_audio and reads AudioChunkPair frames through AudioTapHandle::recv per RFC §41.4.
【Happy path】tts_source implements a TtsStreamSource (AsyncAudioSource over an mpsc receiver), adds it via add_audio_source, and sets gain per RFC §41.5.
【Error case】Each example exits non-zero with a user-facing error message when the SIP endpoint is unreachable, registration fails, or credentials are invalid — never panics.
【Edge case】Missing or invalid CLI args print a usage message to stderr and exit non-zero.
【Invariant】Every example main returns Result and propagates errors with `?`; no unwrap() in the example production paths (panic policy C056).
