tickets.background: Source ticket P3-2 specified AudioWorkerTask with a Tokio JoinHandle for the blocking-pool worker. The handle is stored as `Option<tokio::task::JoinHandle<()>>` (src/runtime/audio_worker.rs:279) and marked #[allow(dead_code)], so the worker's task lifecycle is not actively managed. This work item replaces the unused Option<JoinHandle> with a non-optional active JoinHandle and integrates shutdown so the handle is always awaited on shutdown.
scope: - src/runtime/audio_worker.rs - change `handle: Option<JoinHandle<()>>` to an active non-optional `JoinHandle<()>`; integrate shutdown to always await it
- src/runtime/mod.rs - verify re-export/compile
- Out of scope: FFI audio capture/playback (RustMediaPort) remains deferred until FFI audio integration is available; AudioMixer behavior unchanged.
- Impact: AudioWorkerTask always owns a live worker task; shutdown deterministically joins the worker.
testUnit: UT: [C034] AudioWorkerTask::spawn returns a worker whose handle field is non-optional (compile-time).
UT: [C035] spawn -> shutdown() completes and is_running() becomes false.
UT: [C035] spawn with a mock source -> process_frame produces frames -> shutdown stops production.
UT: [Error] Double shutdown returns promptly without panic.
UT: [Boundary] handle.is_finished() is false immediately after spawn (task still running).
UT: [C038] runtime/audio_worker.rs contains no unsafe keyword (grep test).
testIntegration: IT: [Lifecycle] Spawn N workers concurrently, each with its own mixer, add sources, and verify independent shutdown with no cross-contamination.
IT: [Shutdown] A worker whose task panics (via a panicking source) still resolves shutdown() without hanging.
testExceptions: FFI audio capture/playback (RustMediaPort get_frame/put_frame) is deferred to when FFI audio integration lands; the worker lifecycle is verified with MockAsyncAudioSource only.
acceptanceCriteria: 【Happy path】After spawn(), the worker holds a non-optional JoinHandle - no Option unwrap needed to observe the running task.
【Happy path】shutdown() sets the shutdown flag and awaits the JoinHandle; after shutdown returns, is_running() == false and the worker task has terminated.
【Happy path】A worker with active sources keeps producing mixed frames until shutdown, then stops cleanly.
【Error case】shutdown() called twice is idempotent - the second call does not panic and returns promptly.
【Edge case】If the worker task panics, shutdown() still resolves (the join returns Err which is logged, not panicked).
【Edge case】spawn() from a tokio runtime context always yields a running JoinHandle (handle.is_finished() == false immediately after spawn).
tickets.relatedTicketIds: P2-4 (depends on: AudioWorkerTask pattern), P3-1 (depends on: configure_codecs via backend), P6 (depends on: state machine transitions update ClientState)
tickets.notes:
- Stub file:line list - src/runtime/audio_worker.rs:277.
- Implementation steps: (1) change the field type to JoinHandle<()>; (2) store the handle directly in spawn(); (3) rewrite shutdown() to always await; (4) handle JoinError; (5) Red tests; (6) Green.
- Dependencies: existing spawn()/shutdown() tests (audio_worker.rs:699-722) must keep passing; FFI audio integration deferred.
- Related tickets: P8-25 (state accessors), P3-2 (AudioWorkerTask design), P8-7 (cpal device I/O).
tickets.invariants:
- AudioWorkerTask is spawned on the Tokio blocking pool via spawn_blocking and the JoinHandle is always present while the worker is alive (C034).
- The shutdown flag is set atomically; the worker loop exits on the next iteration after the flag is set; no new frames are pushed after shutdown (C035).
- No unsafe added; runtime/ remains unsafe-free (C038).
tickets.instrumentation:
- tracing::warn! if the joined task returns JoinError (worker panicked).
- tracing::info!(call_id, "audio worker stopped") at the end of shutdown().
tickets.investigation:
- src/runtime/audio_worker.rs:277-280 - the P8-26 stub sits above `#[allow(dead_code)] handle: Option<tokio::task::JoinHandle<()>>` (line 279). spawn() (lines 288-313) creates the handle via spawn_blocking and stores `handle: Some(handle)` (line 311). shutdown() (lines 316-321) takes the Option and awaits if Some - so the Option is partially used but still Option-typed and marked dead_code, leaving a 'no handle' state representable.
- AudioWorkerInner.run() (lines 342-347) loops on the shutdown_signal and sleeps frame_duration between process_frame calls.
- What a real implementation must provide: change the field to a non-optional `JoinHandle<()>`; store the raw handle from spawn_blocking; make shutdown() always await it; handle a JoinError gracefully (log, don't panic).
tickets.boyScoutPlan:
- Remove the now-inaccurate #[allow(dead_code)] and the Option wrapper.
- Document the invariant 'handle is always present while the worker is alive' on the struct.
- Log a warning if the join result is a JoinError (worker panicked).

tickets.title: Migrate to a Debug-friendly sender wrapper and derive Debug for RuntimeCommand

contracts.precondition: Runtime module structure matches RFC §6
contracts.postcondition: runtime/ module compiled and linked
contracts.invariant: Module boundary: runtime/ depends only on tokio + std

contracts.precondition: MPSC channel established between RuntimeHandle and CoreReactor
contracts.postcondition: All commands pass through unbounded MPSC channel in FIFO order
contracts.invariant: Reactor loop processes exactly one command per iteration with no reordering

contracts.precondition: RuntimeHandle is Send + Sync
contracts.postcondition: RuntimeHandle can be shared across tokio tasks and threads safely
contracts.invariant: RuntimeCommand enum and all its fields satisfy Send bounds

tickets.background: Source ticket P0-2 specified the RuntimeCommand enum with tokio oneshot reply channels. Because oneshot::Sender is not Debug, Debug was manually implemented (src/runtime/command.rs:148-174) to print only variant names. This work item migrates the reply channel to a Debug-friendly wrapper type so RuntimeCommand can derive Debug and produce richer debug output.
scope: - src/runtime/command.rs - introduce a Debug-friendly sender wrapper (e.g., ReplyChannel<T>), replace `tokio::sync::oneshot::Sender<...>` reply fields, and derive/verify Debug on RuntimeCommand
- src/runtime/reactor.rs - update construction/send sites to the wrapper type
- src/runtime/handle.rs - verify submit() sites compile against the wrapper
- Out of scope: changing oneshot reply semantics, FIFO ordering, or Send bounds.
- Impact: RuntimeCommand becomes fully Debug-derivable; debug output can include field summaries instead of just variant names.
testUnit: UT: [C012] RuntimeCommand implements Debug for every variant (compile-time: fn assert_debug<T: Debug>()).
UT: [C011] format!("{:?}", cmd) for a representative variant (Shutdown, AddAudioSource, MakeCall) does not panic and contains the variant name.
UT: [C012] The sender wrapper is Send (compile-time assert).
UT: [C011] Display output unchanged: format!("{}", RuntimeCommand::Shutdown) == "RuntimeCommand::Shutdown".
UT: [Normal] The wrapper round-trips a reply (send through the wrapper, receive on the oneshot) - exactly-once delivery.
UT: [Boundary] Debug output for a variant with a payload field (e.g., MakeCall with account_id) includes the field or a non-sensitive summary.
testIntegration: IT: [Dispatch] Submit a command through RuntimeHandle and receive the reply via the wrapper - identical to before the migration (existing P0-2 tests keep passing).
IT: [Logging] A debug log of a RuntimeCommand in the reactor loop renders without error.
testExceptions: oneshot::Sender itself cannot be made Debug without the wrapper; the migration is the wrapper. Raw sender identity is not exposed in Debug output by design.
acceptanceCriteria: 【Happy path】RuntimeCommand derives #[derive(Debug)] (or otherwise produces field-rich debug output) and compiles for every variant, including those carrying a reply channel.
【Happy path】The Debug-friendly sender wrapper implements Debug (e.g., prints "ReplyChannel" or a non-sensitive summary) and is used for all reply fields.
【Happy path】format!("{:?}", RuntimeCommand::Shutdown { reply }) prints the variant and does not panic.

【Happy path】AddAudioSource (which boxes a non-Debug AsyncAudioSource) also produces a working Debug representation (via a scoped manual Debug for that field or a second wrapper), so derivation is total.
【Error case】No behavior change: send_reply()/reactor dispatch still deliver exactly-once results through the wrapper.
【Edge case】The Display impl (format!("{}", cmd)) output is unchanged - it still prints "RuntimeCommand::Variant".
tickets.relatedTicketIds: P0-1 (depends on: P0 defines overall architecture that concurrency model realizes), P2 (depends on: P2 extends RuntimeCommand with M20 variants)
tickets.notes:
- Stub file:line list - src/runtime/command.rs:146.
- Implementation steps: (1) add the ReplyChannel wrapper with a Debug impl; (2) replace reply field types across RuntimeCommand and DispatchCommand; (3) update construction/send sites (reactor.rs, handle.rs, tests); (4) derive Debug on RuntimeCommand (and handle the boxed AsyncAudioSource field); (5) keep Display unchanged; (6) Red tests; (7) Green.
- Dependencies: reactor.rs and handle.rs consume the reply fields; existing P0-2 tests (command.rs:436-730) exercise construction and dispatch - they must be updated to the wrapper and kept green.
- Related tickets: P0-2 (original concurrency model), P2 (extends RuntimeCommand with M20 variants).
tickets.invariants:
- All commands pass through the MPSC channel in FIFO order; the wrapper must not alter dispatch semantics (C011).
- RuntimeCommand and all fields satisfy Send bounds; the wrapper must remain Send (C012).
- runtime/ module boundary is preserved (C010).
tickets.instrumentation: - No new logging required; the richer Debug output benefits existing reactor-loop tracing that formats RuntimeCommand.
tickets.investigation:
- src/runtime/command.rs:146 - the P8-27 stub sits above the manual `impl std::fmt::Debug for RuntimeCommand` (lines 148-174), which matches on variant names and prints only "RuntimeCommand::{Variant}", skipping all fields.
- Line 43 comment: "Debug is manual (not derived) because `Box<dyn AsyncAudioSource>` is not Debug." The enum (lines 44-144) has 18 variants; every reply field is `tokio::sync::oneshot::Sender<Result<...>>` (not Debug). AddAudioSource (lines 120-123) additionally boxes `dyn AsyncAudioSource` (not Debug). DispatchCommand (lines 217-269) has the same pattern and a manual Debug (lines 392-423).
- What a real implementation must provide: a Debug-friendly wrapper (e.g., `pub(crate) struct ReplyChannel<T>(oneshot::Sender<T>)` with a manual Debug impl), swap all reply fields to the wrapper, handle the non-Debug boxed source (scoped manual Debug for AddAudioSource or a second wrapper), then derive/confirm Debug on RuntimeCommand. send_reply() (lines 426-434) and the reactor must construct the wrapper.
tickets.boyScoutPlan:
- Replace the two near-identical manual match blocks (Debug lines 148-174 and Display lines 177-202) with derive + a single Display helper to avoid drift.
- Add a doc comment on the wrapper explaining why the manual Debug is required (oneshot::Sender not Debug) and that the raw sender is never printed.

tickets.title: Upgrade the Weak<JoinHandle> to Arc and expose it for FFI thread lifecycle inspection once pjsua is linked

contracts.precondition: Rust FFI required to call C PJSUA library functions. Concurrency model defines reactor thread for serialized command execution.
contracts.postcondition: PJSIP FFI layer created with: (1) ffi::bindings module generated by bindgen build.rs with allowlist pattern, (2) PjOwnedStr safe wrapper for pj_str_t with Rust-owned Vec<u8> backing, (3) extern C callback functions enqueue NativeEvent, (4) runtime/ modules use only safe SipBackend trait.
contracts.invariant: All unsafe code isolated to ffi/ module. No unsafe keyword in runtime/, client.rs, or config/. Compile-time lint enforces unsafe isolation.

contracts.precondition: Reactor thread owns single source-of-truth ClientState. Tokio runtime provides async RwLock for snapshot sharing.
contracts.postcondition: ClientState with initialized, accounts BTreeMap, calls BTreeMap, transports Vec, capabilities. AccountEntry with id, native_id, config, registration. CallEntry with id, native_id, account_id, state, media. conf_port_id NOT in CallEntry.
contracts.invariant: Read-only snapshots via read().await (never blocking_read()). Updates via write().await (reactor only).

tickets.background: Source ticket P3-2 (PJSIP FFI Layer, Runtime State & AudioMixer Architecture) specified the reactor-thread concurrency model and the Send+Sync RuntimeHandle, but left the join_handle field as an unused Weak<JoinHandle<()>>. This marker was left as a stub because CoreReactor::spawn returns the JoinHandle separately (reactor.rs:247) and nothing consumes the handle's stored weak reference. This work item resolves it by upgrading the field to Arc<JoinHandle<()>> and exposing a thread-lifecycle inspection accessor on RuntimeHandle for the FFI layer.
scope: - src/runtime/handle.rs:27-29 — replace the #[allow(dead_code)] Weak<JoinHandle<()>> field with Arc<JoinHandle<()>> and add a getter / is_thread_alive() inspection method
- src/runtime/handle.rs:34-44 — update RuntimeHandle::new signature to accept Arc<JoinHandle<()>>
- src/runtime/reactor.rs:63 — pass the spawned thread's join handle into RuntimeHandle::new instead of Weak::new()
- src/runtime/reactor.rs:247 — keep the caller-facing JoinHandle consistent with the Arc stored in the handle
- Out of scope: PJSUA C linkage / bindgen (P8-5); FFI callback registration (P8-21).
- Impact: RuntimeHandle public API; reactor spawn return contract; FFI thread-lifecycle observer can query reactor-thread liveness once PJSIP is linked.
testUnit: UT: [Normal] RuntimeHandle::new with an Arc<JoinHandle> stores the handle and the inspection accessor returns the identical Arc (Arc::ptr_eq).
UT: [Normal] runtime_handle_is_clonable (handle.rs:282) still passes with the Arc-typed field.
UT: [Boundary] inspection reports not-finished for a running reactor thread and finished after the thread is joined.
UT: [Error] construction with a valid Arc never fails; the field is non-optional, so no partial-state path exists.
testIntegration: IT: CoreReactor::spawn returns a RuntimeHandle whose exposed Arc<JoinHandle> refers to the same thread the caller joins; after join(), the handle's inspection method reports finished.
testExceptions: Actual OS-thread mid-life liveness depends on scheduling and cannot be asserted deterministically across platforms; unit tests verify the Arc wiring and thread-id equality, not liveness timings. FFI consumers of the exposed handle require the pjsua-native linkage (P8-5) that is not available in unit tests.
acceptanceCriteria: 【Happy path】RuntimeHandle stores the reactor thread's JoinHandle as Arc<JoinHandle<()>> and exposes an inspection accessor (e.g. thread_handle() -> &Arc<JoinHandle<()>> or is_thread_alive()).

【Happy path】CoreReactor::spawn (reactor.rs:56) passes the actual spawned thread's join handle into RuntimeHandle::new, and the stored Arc is the same thread the caller joins at reactor.rs:247 — verified by Arc::ptr_eq or std::thread::Thread::id equality.
【Happy path】RuntimeHandle remains Send + Sync and Clone after the change; the compile-time assert_send/assert_sync tests at handle.rs:272-277 stay green.
【Edge case】A cloned RuntimeHandle shares the same Arc<JoinHandle> — thread inspection from any clone reports the same underlying thread.
【Edge case】The #[allow(dead_code)] on the join_handle field is removed once the Arc is consumed by the inspection accessor.

tickets.notes: Stub site: src/runtime/handle.rs:27,29 (field + allow). Order: (1) change the field type to Arc<JoinHandle<()>>; (2) update new() and all call sites; (3) add the inspection accessor; (4) update tests. Callers of RuntimeHandle::new: reactor.rs:63 and the 7 test constructors in handle.rs. Keep the reactor thread std::thread-based per the type assertion at reactor.rs:586. Related: P3-2 (source), P8-5 (bindgen), P8-21 (callback registration).
tickets.invariants: RuntimeHandle remains Send + Sync (Arc<JoinHandle<()>> is Send+Sync because std::thread::JoinHandle<()> is Send+Sync). The reactor thread is still spawned via std::thread (never tokio::task::spawn), so the handle remains a std::thread::JoinHandle — the type assertion at reactor.rs:586 stays green. No unsafe code is introduced in runtime/handle.rs; unsafe remains confined to ffi/ (C038).

tickets.investigation: src/runtime/handle.rs:27-29 declares join_handle: Weak<JoinHandle<()>> guarded by #[allow(dead_code)]; the field is written in RuntimeHandle::new (handle.rs:34-44) and never read. src/runtime/reactor.rs:63 constructs the handle with std::sync::Weak::new(), and reactor.rs:247 returns the thread_join JoinHandle to the caller instead — so the stored weak reference can never upgrade (it is always None). tickets.title: Wire dispatch_event and process_native_event (with its extract_event_ids helper) into the reactor loop so NativeEvents delivered by the FFI callback bridge are processed

contracts.precondition: PJSIP FFI layer exists with callback bridge functions. SipBackend trait defined. Multiple SipClient instances may share PjsuaBackend singleton.
contracts.postcondition: Dual Client callback routing: single Reactor receives all NativeEvents. Reactor::dispatch_event resolves account_id and routes to correct SipClient EventBus.
contracts.invariant: Single Reactor pattern preserved. No event duplication across multiple clients.

contracts.precondition: Reactor thread owns single source-of-truth ClientState. Tokio runtime provides async RwLock for snapshot sharing.
contracts.postcondition: ClientState with initialized, accounts BTreeMap, calls BTreeMap, transports Vec, capabilities. AccountEntry with id, native_id, config, registration. CallEntry with id, native_id, account_id, state, media. conf_port_id NOT in CallEntry.
contracts.invariant: Read-only snapshots via read().await (never blocking_read()). Updates via write().await (reactor only).

tickets.background: Source ticket P3-2 specified the dual-client EventBus dispatch (C039) and the NativeEvent to SipEvent conversion pipeline, but left dispatch_event, process_native_event, and extract_event_ids as #[allow(dead_code)] free functions in reactor.rs with no call site. These were left as stubs because the FFI callback bridge (P8-21) that delivers NativeEvents to the reactor is not yet linked, so no event source feeds the loop. This work item resolves them by wiring the three helpers into the reactor loop so NativeEvents arriving from the callback bridge are converted and dispatched.
scope: - src/runtime/reactor.rs:260,294,335 — remove the #[allow(dead_code)] markers and wire dispatch_event / process_native_event / extract_event_ids into the reactor loop
- src/runtime/reactor.rs:80-244 — add a NativeEvent ingestion path (receiver) to the reactor loop and call process_native_event with the backend, client_event_buses, and default_event_bus
- src/runtime/reactor.rs:263-264,297-298 — have the reactor own/create the EventBus instances (currently only parameters, never instantiated in spawn)
- Out of scope: FFI callback-bridge enqueue (P8-21); NativeEvent conversion gaps (P8-20); mock/real backend split (P8-3).
- Impact: production event flow from PJSIP callbacks to SipClient EventBuses; removes the dead-code markers.
testUnit: UT: [Normal] a NativeEvent fed through the wired loop path reaches process_native_event and is published (mirrors process_native_event_call_state_changed_publishes at reactor.rs:526).
UT: [Normal] RegistrationStateChanged with status 200 publishes RegistrationSucceeded (existing test reactor.rs:472 stays green after wiring).
UT: [Error] backend Err publishes RegistrationFailed or Error (existing test reactor.rs:497 stays green).
UT: [Boundary] a P1/P2 event produces no publication (existing test reactor.rs:547 stays green).
UT: [Normal] dispatch_event routing isolation (reactor.rs:377,411,439) stays green.
testIntegration: IT: Spawn the reactor with a MockBackend, inject a NativeEvent through the new ingestion channel, subscribe a default EventBus, and assert the converted SipEvent arrives on the bus.
testExceptions: The real PJSUA callback bridge (P8-21) cannot run without pjsua linkage; integration tests inject NativeEvents directly through the reactor's ingestion channel using MockBackend. EventBus broadcast capacity (2048 at client.rs:100) makes delivery loss-tolerant, so exact-delivery counts are asserted only for single-subscriber control receivers in unit tests.
acceptanceCriteria: 【Happy path】The reactor loop receives a NativeEvent (from the callback-bridge channel) and calls process_native_event, which converts it to a SipEvent and routes it through dispatch_event to the correct client/default EventBus.
【Happy path】RegistrationStateChanged events query the backend via get_account_info and publish RegistrationSucceeded / RegistrationFailed / Error (reactor.rs:302-315) — no silent drop.

【Happy path】Non-registration P0 events (CallStateChanged, CallMediaStateChanged, DtmfDigit) flow through convert_native_event_to_payload plus extract_event_ids and publish with the correct account_id / call_id in EventMeta.
【Error case】Backend errors during event processing are published as SipEventPayload::Error (reactor.rs:306) and never crash the loop.
【Edge case】P1/P2 events (TransportStateChanged, NatDetected, etc.) are dropped without publication, as documented (reactor.rs:316-325).
【Edge case】The reactor owns at least a default_event_bus; client_event_buses maps account_id to the registered SipClient bus so no event is duplicated across clients (C039 invariant).
tickets.relatedTicketIds: P2-4 (depends on: AudioWorkerTask pattern), P3-1 (depends on: configure_codecs via backend), P6 (depends on: state machine transitions update ClientState)
tickets.notes: Stub sites: src/runtime/reactor.rs:260,294,335. Order: (1) create a NativeEvent ingestion channel and reactor-owned EventBus instances; (2) call process_native_event in the loop; (3) drop the dead-code markers; (4) add the integration test. Depends on the callback-bridge enqueue shape agreed in P8-21; until PJSIP is linked, tests inject NativeEvent directly. Related: P3-2 (source), P7-2 (dispatch tests), P8-21 (callback bridge), P8-20 (FFI call sites).
tickets.invariants: Single Reactor pattern preserved: all NativeEvents are processed on the one reactor thread and no event is duplicated across clients (C039). The reactor remains the single writer of ClientState (C046). No unsafe code is added to runtime/reactor.rs (C038). EventBus publish remains a loss-tolerant broadcast; the client.rs:100 default capacity (2048) is preserved.
tickets.instrumentation: tracing::info! per published SipEvent (event type, account_id, call_id); tracing::warn! for P1/P2 dropped events and for backend errors that publish Error payloads.
tickets.investigation: reactor.rs:260 marks dispatch_event with #[allow(dead_code)]; the function (262-282) implements account-based routing but is never called. process_native_event (295-327) implements the registration flow and the generic conversion but is also dead. extract_event_ids (336-355) is called only from process_native_event, so it too is dead. The reactor loop in spawn (80-244) handles only DispatchCommand variants; there is no NativeEvent receiver and no EventBus instance owned by the reactor — client.rs:100 creates an EventBus on the SipClient side but nothing connects it to dispatch_event. A real implementation must add a NativeEvent channel (the callback bridge's enqueue target, P8-21), have the reactor own a default_event_bus and a client_event_buses map, and call process_native_event from the loop for each received event, preserving the C039 no-duplication invariant.
tickets.boyScoutPlan: Remove the three #[allow(dead_code)] markers. Extract the repeated catch_unwind / panic-payload block (reactor.rs:85-114,153-183,185-222) into a helper so the loop reads as prose. Replace the trailing let _ = native_id; at reactor.rs:199 with a structured use or an explicit rename.

tickets.background: Source ticket P3-2 specified the call-state mapping where CallDirection (Outgoing/Incoming) discriminates CONNECTING into Trying vs Ringing, but left CallDirection and convert_call_state_with_previous with #[allow(dead_code)] and the on_incoming_call FFI callback (ffi/callback.rs:31) as a no-op that never records a direction. These were left as stubs because the FFI callback bridge (P8-21) that would deliver the incoming-call direction is not yet linked. This work item resolves them by wiring CallDirection into the on_incoming_call callback and calling convert_call_state_with_previous from Reactor call processing to discriminate Trying vs Ringing.
scope: - src/state/m20_callstate_mapping.rs:47-53 — remove #[allow(dead_code)] from CallDirection and consume it in the reactor path
- src/state/m20_callstate_mapping.rs:112-125 — remove #[allow(dead_code)], use the call_id parameter (drop the _ prefix), and make convert_call_state_with_previous the CONNECTING path
- src/ffi/callback.rs:31-37 — on_incoming_call must record the incoming call (enqueue a NativeEvent carrying the Incoming direction) instead of dropping its arguments
- src/runtime/reactor.rs — the reactor call-state processing must call convert_call_state_with_previous with the resolved CallDirection
- Out of scope: full callback registration via pjsua_config.cb (P8-21); bindgen bindings (P8-5).
- Impact: CONNECTING inbound calls now emit OutgoingCallRinging instead of always OutgoingCallTrying.
testUnit: UT: [Normal] convert_call_state_with_previous(CONNECTING, Incoming) returns OutgoingCallRinging (existing test at m20_callstate_mapping.rs:192 stays green).
UT: [Normal] convert_call_state_with_previous(CONNECTING, Outgoing) returns OutgoingCallTrying (existing test at :180 stays green).
UT: [Normal] on_incoming_call records an incoming call / enqueues a NativeEvent with direction Incoming.
UT: [Boundary] non-CONNECTING states delegate to convert_call_state (inv_state_confirmed test at :204 stays green).
UT: [Error] a call state with no resolvable direction falls back to convert_call_state's default (Trying).
testIntegration: IT: Feed an incoming-call NativeEvent through the reactor call processing and assert the published SipEvent is OutgoingCallRinging with the correct call_id.
testExceptions: The on_incoming_call FFI callback cannot be invoked from a unit test without a live PJSUA stack (pjsua-native feature, P8-5/P8-21); unit tests cover the direction-recording helper and the conversion function directly, and integration tests inject the NativeEvent.
acceptanceCriteria: 【Happy path】An incoming call at CONNECTING with CallDirection::Incoming produces SipEventPayload::OutgoingCallRinging via convert_call_state_with_previous.
【Happy path】An outgoing call at CONNECTING with CallDirection::Outgoing produces OutgoingCallTrying (unchanged behavior).
【Happy path】on_incoming_call (ffi/callback.rs:31) no longer drops its arguments — it records the incoming call so the reactor can resolve CallDirection::Incoming.
【Edge case】Non-CONNECTING states delegate to convert_call_state unchanged (m20_callstate_mapping.rs:123).
【Edge case】The #[allow(dead_code)] markers on CallDirection (line 48) and convert_call_state_with_previous (line 112) are removed once consumed.

tickets.title: Implement PhaseTimeout handling for per-call timeout tracking during shutdown

contracts.precondition: SipClient has been initialized (initialize() completed successfully); reactor is running and accepting commands
contracts.postcondition: ShutdownSpec orchestrates idempotent shutdown: (1) atomic is_shutdown_started swap prevents re-entry, (2) all active calls are BYE/CANCELed, (3) accounts unregistered, (4) audio worker drained, (5) backend.shutdown() called, (6) reactor loop exits
contracts.invariant: Shutdown is idempotent: first call executes full sequence and returns Ok(()); second and subsequent calls return Ok(()) immediately without executing the sequence again

contracts.precondition: ShutdownSpec.is_shutdown_started() returns true after first atomic swap
contracts.postcondition: ShutdownCommandRouter.classify() correctly routes commands during shutdown: GetAccountInfo → Permit, ConfConnect/ConfDisconnect → Reject(InvalidState), all others → Reject(InvalidState). Reactor applies this routing before command execution.
contracts.invariant: GetAccountInfo is always Permitted during shutdown (read-only state check). ConfConnect and ConfDisconnect are always Rejected during shutdown (media mutation is unsafe during teardown).

tickets.background: Source ticket P4-3 (Shutdown, Media Bridge, HTTP/WS Protocol & SQLite Schema) specified ShutdownSpec as an idempotent phase-ordered shutdown orchestrator with a per-phase timeout, but the timeout field is stored in the struct (shutdown_specification.rs:144-146) and never read, and ShutdownError::PhaseTimeout (lines 87-90) is never constructed. This marker was left as a stub because CancelCalls iterates calls with no deadline and no per-call timeout accounting. This work item resolves it by implementing PhaseTimeout handling for per-call timeout tracking during shutdown.
scope: - src/state/shutdown_specification.rs:144-146 — remove #[allow(dead_code)] and consume the timeout field
- src/state/shutdown_specification.rs:217-261 — execute_phase (especially CancelCalls) applies the per-phase timeout; a phase that exceeds it produces ShutdownError::PhaseTimeout
- src/state/shutdown_specification.rs:232-239 — per-call hangup deadline tracking (deadline per call and an overall phase deadline)
- src/state/shutdown_specification.rs:87-90 — ShutdownError::PhaseTimeout becomes reachable
- Out of scope: ShutdownCommandRouter command gating (P4-3/C045); audio drain coordination (P4-3/C050).
- Impact: shutdown CancelCalls no longer hangs indefinitely on a stuck backend; timeout errors are observable.
testUnit: UT: [Normal] a phase that completes within the timeout returns Ok (existing shutdown_sequence_executes_idempotently at shutdown_specification.rs:332 stays green).
UT: [Error] a backend hangup that blocks beyond the timeout yields ShutdownError::PhaseTimeout with the correct phase and timeout.
UT: [Boundary] timeout=Duration::ZERO with a non-completing phase returns PhaseTimeout without panic.
UT: [Boundary] the sequence continues after a PhaseTimeout and returns the first error (C044 continue-on-error).
testIntegration: IT: Drive ShutdownSpec with a MockBackend whose hangup blocks (or a timing-aware backend), and assert execute_sequence returns PhaseTimeout while is_shutdown_started() stays true and the remaining phases still run.
testExceptions: Deterministic wall-clock timing cannot be asserted in unit tests without sleeping; tests use a timeout-aware backend (or a MockBackend configured to report hangup as pending) and assert the PhaseTimeout error type and the continuation behavior rather than exact durations. tokio::time::timeout keeps the async tests fast.
acceptanceCriteria: 【Happy path】A phase that completes within the configured timeout returns Ok and records no timeout (existing shutdown tests stay green).

【Error case】A phase (e.g. CancelCalls) that exceeds the configured timeout produces ShutdownError::PhaseTimeout { phase, timeout } — and, per C044, subsequent phases still execute and the first error is returned.
【Edge case】The timeout is applied per phase boundary (per-call deadline plus an overall phase deadline), not as an unbounded per-call wait.
【Edge case】A zero or very small timeout does not panic — it degrades to an immediate PhaseTimeout for slow backends.
tickets.relatedTicketIds: P5-2 (depends on: FFI for media bridge), P4-3 (depends on: HTTP/WS protocol + SQLite), P2-3 (depends on: sequence number from event system)
tickets.notes: Stub site: src/state/shutdown_specification.rs:144. Order: (1) apply the timeout to phase execution (CancelCalls per-call and overall phase deadline); (2) construct ShutdownError::PhaseTimeout; (3) preserve continue-on-error and idempotency; (4) add timing tests. Related: P4-3 (source), P8-33 (Layer 5 tests consume shutdown), C044/C045 contracts.
tickets.invariants: Shutdown remains idempotent (C044): the timeout path never re-enters execute_sequence. PhaseTimeout errors never abort the remaining phases (C044: first error returned, later phases still run). The timeout field is always consumed — no dead code remains in ShutdownSpec.
tickets.instrumentation: tracing::warn! with phase + timeout when PhaseTimeout fires; tracing::info! with per-phase elapsed duration on completion.
tickets.investigation: shutdown_specification.rs:140-147 declares timeout: Duration with #[allow(dead_code)]; new(timeout) stores it (152-157) but nothing reads it. execute_phase (217-261) iterates call_ids and account_ids with unbounded backend.hangup / backend.set_registration calls (233-237, 241-245) — no deadline, so a stuck backend hangs shutdown forever. ShutdownError::PhaseTimeout (87-90) is defined and Display-formatted (101-108) but never constructed. execute_sequence (180-214) already accumulates first_error and continues after failures (200-208), which the timeout path must preserve. A real implementation must wrap phase execution with the configured timeout (per-phase and/or per-call deadline), construct PhaseTimeout on expiry, and keep the C044 idempotency and continue-on-error invariants.
tickets.boyScoutPlan: Remove the #[allow(dead_code)] and the dead timeout-field comment. Extract the per-phase execution body into a timed helper (e.g. run_phase_with_timeout) so execute_sequence reads as prose. Consider deriving Clone/PartialEq on ShutdownError for test assertions (it already derives Debug).

acceptanceCriteria: 【Happy path】AudioTapMode is defined with exactly the Realtime and Lossless variants; Default == AudioTapMode::Realtime (RFC §22.1).
【Happy path】AudioTapHandle wraps a tokio::sync::mpsc::Receiver<AudioChunkPair> and `recv()` returns Option<AudioChunkPair>, yielding None when the sender closes.

【Happy path】The subscribe_audio entry point exists with the RFC §22 signature: subscribe_audio(call_id: CallId, format: AudioFormat, capacity: usize, mode: AudioTapMode) -> Result<AudioTapHandle, SipError>.

【Happy path】In Realtime mode, when the channel is full the oldest pair is dropped and the newest pair is preferred (oldest-drop), reporting an AudioTapOverflow condition — the audio pipeline is not blocked.
【Happy path】In Lossless mode, when the channel is full the producer side applies backpressure (blocks instead of dropping) so no pair is lost.
【Error case】subscribe_audio for an unknown call_id returns Err(SipError::not_found(...)) and does not create a handle.
【Edge case】capacity == 0 is rejected with Err(SipError) since a zero-capacity channel cannot carry a pair.
【Invariant】AudioTapMode is Clone + Copy + Debug + PartialEq + Eq; AudioTapHandle is Send and not Clone (a single consumer per tap).

tickets.background:
[::INSPECTION_FLAGGED::]
This ticket has been flagged by the ABC Inspection Pipeline after completing the implementation lifecycle (make → plan → start → review → resolve). The actual source code was rigorously analyzed against three criteria:

  A — Contract Translation:   Are all Precondition/Postcondition/Invariant contracts accurately translated into test code?
  B — Violation Detection:    Can every contract violation be detected by an existing test assertion?
  C — Test Precision:         Are tests precise and unambiguous (no broad assertions, no missing edge cases)?

One or more ABC violations were confirmed. This ticket is hereby remanded for re-implementation. Every violation must be fully resolved, and every contract must be fulfilled in this final implementation round. Complete it this time.

This ticket implements the complete event system: EventBus with control/raw_sip broadcast channels (N0019), design decisions for loss-tolerant delivery with Lagged detection (N0020), NativeEvent to SipEventPayload conversion for all P0/P1/P2 priority events (N0021), CallState/CallMediaState mapping from pjsip_inv_state and media_status (N0022), RegistrationStateChanged via RuntimeCommand::GetAccountInfo pattern (N0023), DtmfSent two-phase design with timeout fallback (N0029), and Dual Client PJSIP callback routing with account_id-based EventBus dispatch (N0038).

## Goal
The P0-5 event system provides the complete bridge between PJSIP C callbacks and Rust async event consumers. It defines the SipEventPayload enum (all P0 variants: Registration/Call/DTMF; P1: Transport/ICE; P2: supplemental), the EventBus with split control/raw_sip broadcast channels, the NativeEvent-to-SipEventPayload conversion functions, and the Dual Client routing infrastructure. Every PJSIP callback-generated event is delivered to the correct SipClient's EventBus as a typed SipEvent struct.

## Purpose
SipClient consumers (UI layer, audio pipeline, logging) need observable, structured notifications about SIP state changes. Without this event system, application code would need to poll for state or interpret raw PJSIP callbacks directly. The EventBus provides a decoupled publish-subscribe pattern where:
- Reactor publishes SipEvents onto broadcast channels
- Multiple consumers independently subscribe and filter (via AccountEventReceiver)
- RawSIP messages are isolated on a separate bus to prevent control event loss

This is the primary async communication channel between the synchronous PJSIP thread (C callbacks) and the async Rust world (tokio tasks).

## Motivation
This is the foundational event infrastructure for the entire crate. All observable SIP behavior — registration status changes, call state transitions, DTMF events, media state changes — flows through this system. Every downstream feature (P2-2 error payloads, P2-4 audio pipeline, P4-1 registration state machine) depends on events being delivered. The current stub (src/client.rs uses mpsc::Receiver<()>) blocks all downstream development.

Without this ticket:
- No SipEventPayload type exists (all stubs)
- NativeEvent conversion is unimplemented
- SipClient returns dummy event receiver (cannot observe any SIP events)
- Dual Client mode (multiple SipClient instances) has no event routing

## Constraints
- Broadcast channel (lossy delivery): tokio::sync::broadcast is the only supported channel type. No reliable delivery, no per-subscriber retransmission. This is by design (N0020).
- PJSUA dependency: NativeEvent types mirror PJSIP callback signatures (pjsip_inv_state, pjsua_call_media_status). Any PJSIP version mismatch may require updating the mapping.
- Single Reactor constraint: global_runtime() must remain unchanged. Dual Client uses EventBus dispatch only — no second Reactor.
- All implementation targets are stub files (pub enum State {} / pub trait Service {}). This is net-new implementation, not refactoring of existing code.
- DtmfSent 500ms timeout: This is a fallback for when PJSIP does not fire a send-complete callback. The timeout may race with actual PJSIP callback delivery (firing both DtmfSent events) — consumer must handle duplicates.

### Goal (P7-2 re-implementation)
Close all five ABC inspection gaps in the P0-5 event system: (O-001) make RegistrationStateChanged actually publish RegistrationSucceeded/RegistrationFailed via the RuntimeCommand::GetAccountInfo → MockBackend::get_account_info() → registration_status_to_payload flow on the client EventBus; (O-002) implement the DtmfSent 500ms timeout fallback (spawn_dtmf_sent_timeout + DtmfConfig::sent_timeout_ms) with a tokio::time::pause() test; (O-003) implement production Reactor dispatch_event()/client_event_buses/default_event_bus and test the production code; (O-004) add SipClient::accounts()/call_state() authoritative query methods and prove events are observation-only; (O-005) assert the exact Lagged(n) count.
### Purpose (P7-2 re-implementation)
The prior implementation produced green tests that did not exercise the production publication/dispatch flows: RegistrationStateChanged never published an event, DtmfSent never fired as a timeout, dual-client routing existed only inside test bodies, the query API did not exist, and Lagged(n) was asserted loosely. The re-implementation makes every contract (C020-C024, C030, C039) verifiable against production code so a violation fails a test assertion.
### Motivation (P7-2 re-implementation)
The ABC Inspection Pipeline confirmed that the contracts' preconditions/postconditions/invariants were not translated into tests of production behavior — Evaluation A/B/C all failed for O-001..O-003. Downstream tickets (P2-2 error payloads, P2-4 audio pipeline, P4-1 registration state machine, P0-6 FFI bridge) depend on these events actually being delivered. Leaving the gaps means contract violations are undetectable, so the re-implementation must ship production code + tests together.
### Constraints (P7-2 re-implementation)
- Single Reactor constraint: global_runtime() unchanged — dual-client dispatch is EventBus-only (C039).
- DtmfSent timeout may race with the real PJSIP callback; consumers must tolerate duplicate DtmfSent events (N0029).
- tokio::time::pause() requires the `test-util` tokio feature — a Cargo.toml feature addition is mandatory for the O-002 deterministic timeout test (no runtime dependency change).
- No new crates; the production flow must be testable with MockBackend (no live PJSIP).
- CallMediaStateChanged currently hardcodes media_status=1 ([::STUB::] P4-2) — P7-2 keeps this stub but must not regress it.

testExceptions: Exception: NativeEvent::RegistrationStateChanged actual pjsua_acc_get_info() FFI call cannot be tested in unit environment — it requires a live pjsua library initialized with accounts. Reason: pjsua_acc_get_info() is a C FFI function that requires a running pjsua instance with registered accounts (not testable in pure Rust unit context). This is not an architectural defect — the MockBackend::get_account_info() alternative provides the same data shape for unit testing, and the real FFI call is covered by integration tests (P0-6+). Alternative: MockBackend::get_account_info() validates conversion logic without FFI.

Exception: Actual PJSIP callback invocation (on_reg_state2, on_call_state, on_dtmf_digit) cannot be unit-tested — these are C→Rust callbacks triggered by a live PJSIP stack. Reason: FFI callback registration and invocation (not testable without PjsuaBackend from P0-6). This is not an architectural defect — MockBackend simulated NativeEvent injection covers the conversion logic, and integration tests with PjsuaBackend (P0-6+) cover the full callback path. Alternative: MockBackend supplies NativeEvent directly for conversion tests.

Exception: Real-time DTMF timing variance cannot be precisely tested — actual PJSIP callback vs timeout race depends on system scheduling. Reason: The 500ms timeout is a wall-clock timer; actual PJSIP callback may arrive just before or after (not testable deterministically). This is not an architectural defect — tokio::time::pause() provides deterministic simulation for unit tests, and production behavior is verified by integration tests with real PJSIP. Alternative: tokio::time::pause() simulates deterministic timing.

Exception: Dual Client concurrency race condition (simultaneous NativeEvent arrives during client registration/deregistration) — not testable automatically without complex concurrency harness. Reason: Client registration/deregistration is a rare operation; race window is theoretically present but practically zero (not testable in automated unit environment). This is not an architectural defect — the dispatch function is deterministic, and registration/deregistration is serialized through the reactor command queue, eliminating the race in practice. Alternative: Manual stress test in QA phase; unit dispatch tests cover deterministic routing logic.

Exception: RegistrationStateChanged pjsua_acc_get_info() returning a timeout/error status from a live PJSIP stack cannot be simulated in a unit test. Reason: A live registration timeout depends on the SIP registrar's actual non-response, which requires a real network peer and is not testable in a deterministic unit environment. This is not an architectural defect — MockBackend::get_account_info() can be configured to return Err or any status code, exercising the production failure publication path deterministically. Alternative: MockBackend returns Err(ReactorError::BackendError) and the test asserts RegistrationFailed/Error is published on the EventBus.

[Happy path] A single SipClient is initialized, registers a SIP account, makes a call, and receives the call state transition events (OutgoingCallStarted -> OutgoingCallTrying -> CallConnected) on the AccountEventReceiver subscribed to that account_id. Each event has correct EventMeta (timestamp, event_id, account_id, call_id).

[Error case] A NativeEvent::RegistrationStateChanged fires for an account where pjsua_acc_get_info() fails (returns error). The EventBus delivers a RegistrationFailed event containing the SipError with details. The client is not left in an indeterminate state — the query API returns the correct registration state.

[Edge case] Two SipClient instances share the same PjsuaBackend (Dual Client mode). An incoming call event for account_id=A is published. Client A's AccountEventReceiver receives CallStateChanged; Client B's AccountEventReceiver (subscribed to account_id=B) must NOT receive the event. account_id=None lifecycle events (ClientInitialized, ClientShutdown) must be received by both clients.

A test with an Ok(403) snapshot asserting RegistrationFailed published via process_native_event is missing.

One or more ABC violations were confirmed. This ticket is hereby remanded for re-implementation. Every violation must be fully resolved, and every contract must be fulfilled in this final implementation round. Complete it this time.

## Goal
Define and implement the siprs-server crate specification: standalone server mode (ServerConfig, AuthConfig, AuthMode), HTTP/WS protocol layer (18 REST endpoints + 2 WebSocket paths + AudioFrameHeader binary protocol), SQLite persistence schema (4 tables via SeaORM + rusqlite bundled), semver/networking reference information (versioning policy, TLS cert info, DNS delegation), and lib.rs module/export declarations — all as specified by RFC nodes N0057, N0058, N0061, N0062, N0064, N0066, N0067.

## Purpose
This ticket transforms the RFC design for the server crate into concrete implementation artifacts: the config structs and protocol data structures that form the foundation of siprs-server. These types are the layer-5 (API layer) building blocks that downstream tickets (P4-3 route handlers, P4-4 WS handlers, P4-5 SQLite DAO) depend on. Without this ticket, no server-mode code can compile.

## Motivation
The siprs crate core (layer 1-4) is fully specified and partially implemented (P0/P1/P2-2 accomplished). The server mode is the next architectural layer needed for the zasso ecosystem to provide a network-accessible SIP API. Multiple downstream tickets (P4-series) are blocked on these type definitions. Additionally, the current source tree has `[::STUB::]` markers in sqlite_schema.rs and semver_sip_networking.rs that must be resolved.

## Constraints
- Crate uses rusqlite bundled feature (no system SQLite dependency). This must be reflected in Cargo.toml.
- SeaORM migration management must follow the Makefile convention from mycute project.
- AudioFrameHeader must use repr(C,packed) for ABI stability across Rust version upgrades (current size discovered: 30 bytes, not 24 as originally specified — spec correction needed).
- AuthMode enum has exactly 3 variants (LocalhostOnly, ApiKey, Jwt) — variant count invariant enforced by test.
- ServerConfig must at minimum derive Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize for config file loading.
- DEFAULT_SIPRS_PORT = 3910 — must match the zasso ecosystem port convention (RT_PORT = 3910).

## Implementation steps:
1. Add SQLite dependencies (rusqlite bundled, sea-orm sqlite) to Cargo.toml
2. Implement src/model/sqlite_schema.rs with SeaORM entities for 4 tables

## Risks:
- AudioFrameHeader size discrepancy (RFC says 24, actual 30) could cause wire incompatibility if other implementations match RFC literally. Must document this clearly.
- sea-orm with sqlite may add significant compile time. Consider Feature flag gating SQLite-heavy features behind a `sqlite-storage` feature.
- The event_id vs seq field ambiguity in EventMeta/SipEvent could cause confusion in sequence number usage between P2-3 and P4-4.

## Caveats:
- The 30-byte AudioFrameHeader is the actual compiled size (verified by existing tests). The RFC documentation should be updated to match.
- rusqlite bundled feature statically links SQLite — increases binary size by ~1MB but eliminates system dependency.
- Makefile migration commands (gen-migration, migrate-up, etc.) are defined at the workspace level, not in this crate.

## Open items:
- Whether to declare `pub mod model;` in lib.rs or keep model as a private implementation module. Decision: make it private until the crate split (B1 boundary).
- Whether SeaORM migrations should live in siprs or siprs-server crate. Decision: migrations live with sqlite_schema.rs in siprs (types), executed in siprs-server.

- After crate split (B1), siprs-core removes SQLite dependency entirely; siprs-server owns the database layer.
- After 1.0 release, add cargo semver-checks CI step per C067 invariant.
- Consider zerocopy crate for safe AudioFrameHeader byte reinterpretation instead of manual to_bytes/from_bytes.

N0061 defines the siprs-server main.rs entry point: SipClient initialization from config, DatabasePool initialization, saved account restoration from SQLite, and Axum server startup on configured bind address. Supports both standalone binary mode and Tauri-embedded library mode.

### Goal
Define the standalone server entry point (main.rs) and supporting types (ServerConfig, AppState, build_router) that initialize SipClient, DatabasePool, restore saved accounts from SQLite, and start an Axum HTTP/WS server on the configured bind address. The server provides at minimum a health check endpoint (GET /api/v1/health) and a shutdown endpoint (POST /api/v1/shutdown). Concretely: `ServerConfig::from_args()` (cli feature, clap) parses CLI args; `AppState { sip_client: Arc<SipClient>, db: Arc<DatabasePool>, server_start_time: Instant }` is the axum shared state; `build_router(state: AppState) -> axum::Router` registers the two endpoints behind the `server` feature; `run_server(config: ServerConfig) -> Result<(), SipError>` wires startup in RFC §53.1 order. The 5 ABC omissions (O-001 critical + O-002..O-005 minor) must be 100% resolved by new/updated tests in this round.

### Purpose
Enable external applications (external SIP clients, Tauri frontend, monitoring tools, CLI scripts) to control siprs via HTTP REST APIs and WebSocket event streams without linking to the siprs Rust library directly. The standalone server bridges the Rust SIP client implementation with any HTTP-capable consumer. The health endpoint gives monitoring/readiness probes a PJSIP-free liveness signal; the shutdown endpoint gives operators and the future Tauri sidecar a clean stop path. This ticket is the minimal verifiable server skeleton that unblocks P4-2 (auth middleware) and P4-3 (full REST/WS routes + crate split).

### Motivation
The RFC defines siprs as a crate with both library and server modes. Standalone server mode is required for the P2P network layer (server-side components), monitoring/observability tooling (health checks, metrics export), and future Tauri desktop integration where the server runs as an embedded sidecar. Without this entry point, all SIP operations would require direct Rust FFI, limiting integration options. This round is motivated by ABC Inspection: the prior P3-3 implementation shipped a compile-time-only router test (`test_build_router_returns_router_type` at src/api/standalone_server_config.rs:728) that never constructs AppState or executes the health handler, leaving the central observable behavior (health returns HTTP 200 before accounts are registered) unenforced. A behavioral axum::test must replace it.

### Constraints
1. Must support two entry modes: standalone binary (with clap CLI arg parsing, `cli` feature) and embedded library (programmatic ServerConfig, no CLI dependency — default features exclude `cli`).
2. Axum server must bind only after SipClient and DatabasePool are fully initialized and saved accounts restored — never expose an uninitialized state (RFC §53.1 startup order).
3. Health check must respond HTTP 200 before any accounts are added (readiness probe) — O-001 demands a behavioral axum::test proving this.
4. AuthConfig defaults to LocalhostOnly for security — server must not listen on external interfaces without explicit auth configuration (`AuthConfig::validate` rejects non-loopback in LocalhostOnly mode).
5. No external crate split in this ticket — server types live in the siprs crate, behind the `server`/`cli` feature gates. siprs-server crate split is tracked in P4-3.
6. All new tests must run under `make test` (Makefile exists) with the `server`/`cli`/`sqlite-storage` feature matrix; no PJSIP native init required (reactor uses MockBackend).

testExceptions:
- [Item] Full end-to-end server startup with a real PJSIP backend and a real SQLite file (SipClient against pj_init(), DatabasePool open, saved-account restoration, live serving).
   [Reason — NOT TESTABLE, NOT A DESIGN DEFECT] PJSIP FFI requires native library initialization (pj_init()) which cannot be sandboxed or mocked at this layer; DatabasePool requires the sqlite-storage feature and a writable SQLite file. Full-stack integration is only possible in the future siprs-server crate. This is NOT a design defect — it is FFI dependency isolation.
   [Alternative] MockBackend-based integration tests (P1-3/N0053) in P4-3 provide isolated server startup without PJSIP; this ticket's axum::test health/shutdown tests exercise the router with a real (MockBackend-backed) SipClient.

- [Item] Binding a specific hardcoded TCP port (e.g., 3910) in tests.
   [Reason — NOT TESTABLE, NOT A DESIGN DEFECT] Port availability is non-deterministic — the port may be in use at test time, causing flaky CI failures. This is NOT a design defect — it is a fundamental property of TCP networking.
   [Alternative] (1) Bind to port 0, extract the actual port from TcpListener::local_addr(), then make test requests. (2) siprs-server crate integration tests use CI-specific port allocation.

- [Item] Exercising the full Axum middleware chain (CORS + JWT auth) beyond the health/shutdown endpoints without PJSIP.
   [Reason — NOT TESTABLE, NOT A DESIGN DEFECT] The JWT auth middleware (P4-2) and full REST/WS handlers (P4-3) are not implemented in this ticket; the middleware chain beyond health/shutdown requires a PJSIP-backed SipClient for account operations. This is NOT a design defect — it is a natural dependency ordering (this ticket is the minimal server framework).
   [Alternative] (1) Health check has NO auth requirement — testable via axum::test in this ticket (resolves O-001). (2) JWT middleware tests land in P4-2. (3) Mock SipClient (P1-3 trait) isolates middleware tests.
acceptanceCriteria: - [Happy path] (1) ServerConfig::default() is valid — bind_addr=127.0.0.1:3910, db_path=~/.siprs/data.db, LocalhostOnly auth. (2) ServerConfig::from_args_with(["--port","3911"]) yields bind_addr.port()==3911. (3) build_router(AppState) returns an axum::Router with GET /api/v1/health AND POST /api/v1/shutdown registered. (4) Behavioral axum::test: GET /api/v1/health → HTTP 200 with JSON body containing {"status":"ok"} (O-001 critical — replaces the compile-time-only test). (5) ServerConfig serde roundtrip preserves all fields. (6) from_args_with([]) produces the clap defaults (LocalhostOnly, port 3910, db-path ~/.siprs/data.db).

- [Error case] (1) AuthConfig::validate() returns ConfigError::LocalhostRequiresLoopback for LocalhostOnly + non-loopback bind (0.0.0.0). (2) AuthConfig::validate() returns ConfigError::JwtRequiresSecret for Jwt mode without jwt_secret. (3) from_args_with returns Err(SipErrorKind::InvalidConfig) for: non-numeric port ("abc"), out-of-range port ("70000" — O-004), invalid --bind-addr format, missing --jwt-secret in jwt mode, and empty --db-path ("" — O-005, requires the from_args_with validation fix). (4) run_server returns a typed SipError (not panic) when startup fails.

- [Edge case] (1) Port 0 (OS auto-assign) accepted by AuthConfig::validate() in ApiKey and Jwt modes (O-004). (2) IPv6 loopback [::1]:3910 accepted by LocalhostOnly validation (O-003). (3) ServerConfig default db_path is the literal "~/.siprs/data.db" (home-directory expansion is the caller's responsibility). (4) Empty allowed_origins vec is valid → CorsLayer::permissive(). (5) AppState with Arc<SipClient> and (cfg sqlite-storage) Arc<DatabasePool> is Send + Sync + Clone.

Step 2: Add the O-001 behavioral test — inside `#[cfg(all(test, feature = "server"))] mod server_tests`, add `#[tokio::test] async fn test_health_check_returns_ok()` that builds AppState via a `fn build_test_app_state()` helper (SipClient::new with ClientConfig::builder().sip_proxy_host("sip.example.com").sip_proxy_port(5060).build(), Arc-wrap, Instant::now()), then `build_router(state).oneshot(Request::builder().uri("/api/v1/health").body(Body::empty())?)` asserting status 200 and body["status"]=="ok"; remove the stale `[::TEST_EXCEPTION::]` comment and the compile-time-only test_build_router_returns_router_type. Step 3: Add O-002 (jwt_secret.is_none() in the C062 default test), O-003 (`"[::1]:3910"` LocalhostOnly validate Ok), O-004 (port-0 validate Ok in ApiKey/Jwt + `--port 70000` Err). Step 4: Add a shutdown axum::test (POST /api/v1/shutdown → 200, {"status":"shutting_down"}). Step 5: Run `make test` (cargo test), `cargo clippy --all-features -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt`; verify feature matrix (default, +server, +cli, +server+sqlite-storage). Step 6: Update the `[::TICKET::]` annotations from P3-3 to P7-1 on touched lines and add @verifies C062 markers per project annotation protocol.
- [Risks] (1) axum::test oneshot with a real SipClient spawns a reactor OS thread (MockBackend) — the tokio::test current-thread runtime must not be starved; the reactor thread is independent so this is safe, but tests must not block on reactor commands that never reply. (2) ClientConfig::default() fails validate() (empty sip_proxy_host) — run_server currently returns Err(InvalidConfig) before binding; a decision is needed in the plan phase (add client_config to ServerConfig vs. build a valid default from config_file). Do NOT bake a failing test that pins this behavior without that decision. (3) The out-of-range port test (`--port 70000`) relies on u16 parse failure — stable across clap versions but verify the error message mentions the port. (4) AppState construction differs under sqlite-storage (extra `db` field) — the test helper must be cfg-gated or use a temp-file DatabasePool.
- [Caveats] (1) build_router wraps state in Arc internally — handlers receive State<Arc<AppState>>; the AppState passed in is moved, not borrowed. (2) CorsLayer::permissive() is applied unconditionally; auth middleware is P4-2 scope and not testable here. (3) server_start_time.elapsed() makes uptime_secs non-deterministic — the health test must assert status + "status":"ok" key, NOT the exact uptime value. (4) `~` in db_path is NOT expanded by siprs — the caller (binary entry) is responsible; tests assert the literal string.

(2) Whether to keep a slim type-assertion for build_router's signature after removing test_build_router_returns_router_type — recommend keeping an `fn _assert_type(router: axum::Router)` helper for the C063 precondition. (3) Whether the health check should also return HTTP 503 after shutdown begins (readiness vs liveness) — deferred to P4-3 observability. (4) DatabasePool::load_accounts() is undefined (P2-3/P4-3) — the startup restoration `[::STUB::]` at :374 remains tracked.

tickets.invariants:
- 【Normal establishment】ServerConfig and AppState types must be constructible with valid defaults before server startup. ServerConfig::default() must yield bind_addr=127.0.0.1:3910, db_path=~/.siprs/data.db, config_file=None, allowed_origins=[], auth=AuthConfig::default() — all valid without external I/O. build_router(app_state) must accept any valid AppState without panicking. Health check endpoint must respond HTTP 200 before any accounts are registered (readiness probe, O-001). from_args() with no overrides must produce the same valid default config.
- 【Invariant on error】ConfigError must never panic in Display/From implementations (thiserror-derived). Server startup failure (invalid config, port in use, DB open failure) must produce a typed SipError (SipErrorKind::InvalidConfig | NativeError), never an unwrap/panic. build_router() must not panic on any valid AppState input. from_args_with() must return Err(SipErrorKind::InvalidConfig) — never panic — for: non-numeric port, out-of-range port (70000), invalid bind-addr format, missing jwt-secret in jwt mode, and (after the O-005 fix) empty db-path. run_server() must propagate startup errors as typed SipError.
- 【Internal state invariant】ServerConfig default bind_addr must be 127.0.0.1:3910; DEFAULT_SIPRS_PORT must equal 3910 (src/api/standalone_server_config.rs:30). AuthConfig default mode must be LocalhostOnly; jwt_secret must be None (O-002); jwt_expiry_secs must equal DEFAULT_JWT_EXPIRY_SECS (3600). AppState fields are Arc-wrapped (sip_client: Arc<SipClient>, db: Arc<DatabasePool>) — never deep-cloned; server_start_time: Instant is set at construction. The single [::STUB::] (line 374, saved-account restoration) must remain tracked for P4-3 and must not be silently implemented in this ticket.
- 【Boundary invariant】Port range validation: 0-65535 (u16 type enforces upper bound; from_args must reject numeric overflow like 70000 — O-004). IPv4/IPv6 loopback detection must work for both 127.0.0.1 and ::1 via SocketAddr::ip().is_loopback() (O-003). Empty db_path must be rejected by from_args_with (O-005 — current code returns Ok(PathBuf::from("")) and needs a validation branch). Empty allowed_origins is valid (CorsLayer::permissive() allows all origins). Port 0 (OS auto-assign) must be accepted by AuthConfig::validate() in ApiKey and Jwt modes (O-004).

tickets.boyScoutPlan:
Translatability improvements planned for the code touched by P7-1 (src/api/standalone_server_config.rs and its tests):

1. **Remove the false `[::TEST_EXCEPTION::]` comment and replace the compile-time-only router test with a behavioral test (O-001).** The comment at :723-725 claims the health check response "requires SipClient initialization" and defers to P4-3 — this contradicts the ticket's own testExceptions (health is testable via axum::test). A lying comment is a bug; the replacement `test_health_check_returns_ok` makes the router's behavior executable and removes the stale justification.
2. **Replace `unwrap()` in the new tests with `Result<()>` propagation** per the Rust testing rule (tests return Result and use `?`). The O-003/O-004 tests must parse `"[::1]:3910".parse()` and `"0.0.0.0:0".parse()` with `?`, not `.unwrap()`. Existing test_auth_config_localhost_valid-style `.unwrap()` on a static literal is acceptable (unreachable panic), but new test code must use the Result pattern.

This also fixes O-005 cleanly.
4. **Rename the compile-time-only test** — `test_build_router_returns_router_type` becomes redundant once the behavioral test exists; it should be removed (or reduced to a type-assertion helper) so the test suite's intent reads accurately.
5. **Proactive improvements outside scope:** the existing test `test_app_state_send_sync` has a duplicated `assert_send::<AuthConfig>()` at :569 — remove the duplicate. `test_auth_config_default_localhost_only` (:439) should also assert jwt_secret.is_none() (O-002) so the C062 invariant is enforced in one place. The `run_server` ClientConfig::default() issue (empty sip_proxy_host) is flagged in notes for the plan phase; if fixed here, the fix must extract a `fn build_client_config(config: &ServerConfig) -> Result<ClientConfig, SipError>` helper rather than inlining a builder chain.

tickets.title: Runtime Infrastructure — Command Serialization and AudioWorkerTask

contracts.precondition: Concurrency model established (P0-2): unbounded MPSC channel created, CoreReactor thread running, RuntimeHandle available
contracts.postcondition: RuntimeCommand enum defined with all 18 variants (the 12 pre-existing + P0-6 M20 ConfConnect/ConfDisconnect + 4 audio-source lifecycle AddAudioSource/RemoveAudioSource/SetAudioSourceGain/MuteAudioSource). Each variant carries a typed oneshot::Sender. DispatchCommand::from_runtime_command maps every variant to a backend execution closure or a dedicated reactor dispatch arm.
contracts.invariant: All PJSUA calls go through the MPSC channel — no direct FFI call outside the reactor thread. oneshot sender is resolved exactly once per command dispatch.

contracts.precondition: AudioMixer defined with: sources DashMap<u64, Arc<Mutex<Box<dyn AsyncAudioSource + Send>>>>, next_source_id AtomicU64, per-source gain map, per-source muted flags
contracts.postcondition: AudioWorkerTask struct defined with spawn() (creates a Tokio blocking task), shutdown() (terminates gracefully), and a frame processing loop. Source lifecycle API defined as RuntimeCommand variants and functional through the reactor-owned AudioMixer: add_audio_source (returns source_id), remove_audio_source (removes by id), set_audio_source_gain (updates clamped gain), mute_audio_source (toggles flag).
contracts.invariant: Sources added/removed at frame boundaries — AudioWorker processes pending lifecycle commands between process_frame iterations. source_id monotonically increases (wraps correctly at u64::MAX). Concurrent add/remove does not corrupt source iteration.

contracts.precondition: AsyncAudioSource trait defined: trait AsyncAudioSource: Send { async fn next_chunk(&mut self, buf: &mut [i16]) -> usize; }
contracts.postcondition: AudioMixer stores Box<dyn AsyncAudioSource + Send> per source_id. AudioWorker calls next_chunk on each source during process_frame and pushes the mixed frame to out_queue. MockAsyncAudioSource implements AsyncAudioSource for testing.
contracts.invariant: next_chunk returns 0 for an exhausted source without panicking. next_chunk fills the buffer partially (returns < buf.len()) for end-of-stream. Implementation is Send + Sync safe.

tickets.background:
[::INSPECTION_FLAGGED::]
This ticket has been flagged by the ABC Inspection Pipeline after completing the implementation lifecycle (make → plan → start → review → resolve). The actual source code was rigorously analyzed against three criteria:

  A — Contract Translation:   Are all Precondition/Postcondition/Invariant contracts accurately translated into test code?
  B — Violation Detection:    Can every contract violation be detected by an existing test assertion?
  C — Test Precision:         Are tests precise and unambiguous (no broad assertions, no missing edge cases)?

Six omissions were confirmed — O-001..O-006 (3 major, 3 minor). Every omission must be fully resolved, and every contract (C011, C035, C036) must be fulfilled in this final implementation round. Complete it this time.

### Goal
Close the ABC Inspection gaps and make the runtime infrastructure layer provably correct: (1) RuntimeCommand covers all 18 variants (incl. QueryState from P7-2, M20 ConfConnect/ConfDisconnect, and the 4 audio-source lifecycle commands), (2) RuntimeHandle exposes working audio-lifecycle submit methods that route through the reactor to a reactor-owned AudioMixer, (3) AudioWorkerTask's process_frame is test-verified end-to-end (next_chunk → gain/mute → mix → out_queue), and (4) MockBackend.conf_connect/conf_disconnect record observable side effects so the ConfConnect/ConfDisconnect dispatch path is provably wired.

### Purpose
The RuntimeCommand enum is the universal command interface that SipClient uses to drive the SIP stack. Every async public API call on SipClient eventually becomes a RuntimeCommand variant submitted via MPSC. The AudioWorkerTask enables per-call audio processing on dedicated Tokio blocking tasks, keeping audio computation off the reactor thread and the async runtime. Source lifecycle (add/remove/gain/mute) becomes a first-class RuntimeCommand capability.

### Motivation
P0-2 established the concurrency model with the base RuntimeCommand variants. P0-4 added the SipError type and M20 error converters. P0-5 added the EventBus and GetAccountInfo variant. P7-2 added QueryState. P0-6 extended the enum with M20 conference commands and the audio-source lifecycle. The ABC Inspection confirmed that although the implementation exists, the test suite does not detect regressions in the ConfConnect/ConfDisconnect dispatch path (O-001), the AudioWorker mix pipeline (O-002), or the audio-lifecycle reactor path (O-003). This re-implementation exists to close those detection gaps.

### Constraints
- Must not break existing RuntimeCommand API (backward-compatible extension).
- AudioMixer uses dashmap::DashMap (not std::sync::Mutex<HashMap>) for lock-free concurrent reads.
- AudioWorkerTask runs on Tokio blocking pool — no tokio::spawn on the reactor thread.
- No real PJSIP FFI calls in this ticket — all backend operations use MockBackend.
- AsyncAudioSource trait uses i16 (PCM S16LE), not f32 (migration is a future concern).
- The reactor must own the AudioMixer instance that audio-lifecycle commands mutate (single-writer rule on the reactor thread).
scope: **Scope of changes (describe each change comprehensively):**

- [src/runtime/command.rs] Action: modify — RuntimeCommand already has all 18 variants (12 pre-existing + 6 P0-6 additions); verify/keep them. Before → After: DispatchCommand::from_runtime_command no longer maps RemoveAudioSource/SetAudioSourceGain/MuteAudioSource to Execute closures returning hardcoded Err(BackendError("audio source lifecycle not yet connected (P0-7)")) (command.rs:349-383); instead they map to new dedicated DispatchCommand variants carrying typed oneshot replies.

- [src/runtime/command.rs] Action: add — new DispatchCommand variants: RemoveAudioSource { source_id: u64, reply: oneshot::Sender<Result<(), ReactorError>> }, SetAudioSourceGain { source_id: u64, gain: f32, reply: ... }, MuteAudioSource { source_id: u64, muted: bool, reply: ... }. API: each carries the mixer-mutation payload + reply. Update Debug/Display and from_runtime_command.

- [src/runtime/handle.rs] Action: add — 4 public async submit methods: submit_add_audio_source(source: Box<dyn AsyncAudioSource + Send>) -> Result<u64, ReactorError>, submit_remove_audio_source(source_id: u64) -> Result<(), ReactorError>, submit_set_audio_source_gain(source_id: u64, gain: f32) -> Result<(), ReactorError>, submit_mute_audio_source(source_id: u64, muted: bool) -> Result<(), ReactorError>. Before → After: the unreachable!("use submit_add_audio_source instead") branch (handle.rs:73-75) becomes a real dispatch; all four follow the submit → DispatchCommand → reactor → oneshot-reply pattern.

- [src/runtime/reactor.rs] Action: add — reactor owns an Arc<AudioMixer> (default-call mixer) alongside client_state. DispatchCommand::AddAudioSource arm (reactor.rs:111-123) calls mixer.add_source(source) and replies Ok(source_id). New arms for RemoveAudioSource/SetAudioSourceGain/MuteAudioSource call mixer.remove_source/set_gain/mute and reply Ok/Err. Before → After: the BackendError stub is replaced with real mixer routing.

- [src/runtime/backend.rs] Action: modify — MockBackend gains observable conf_connect/conf_disconnect side effects (e.g., pub conf_connect_calls: Vec<(i32, i32)> and conf_disconnect_calls: Vec<(i32, i32)> recording (source, sink)). SipBackend trait signature unchanged (no implementor breakage). Before → After: tests can assert the from_runtime_command closure actually invoked backend.conf_connect/conf_disconnect.

- [src/runtime/audio_worker.rs] Action: add — #[cfg(test)] test hook for AudioMixer::next_source_id (e.g., fn set_next_source_id(&self, id: u64) behind #[cfg(test)]) so the u64::MAX wrap invariant is exercisable. No production behavior change.

- [src/runtime/audio_worker.rs] Action: verify — AudioWorkerInner::process_frame (audio_worker.rs:336-382) is directly invokable from the same-file #[cfg(test)] module; add process_frame tests with sources present asserting out_queue content.

- [src/runtime/mod.rs] Action: verify — pub use re-exports (AsyncAudioSource, AudioMixer, AudioWorkerTask, MockAsyncAudioSource) already present; add any newly public DispatchCommand variants if tests require crate-internal access.
- [src/api/asyncaudiosrc_adapter.rs] Action: verify — AsyncAudioSource, ErasedAudioSource, SyncAudioSource, SyncSourceAdapter already implemented (P5-2); no change required.
- [Cargo.toml] Action: verify — dashmap = "6", async-trait = "0.1", crossbeam-queue = "0.3" already present; no dependency change required.

- [tests/] Action: add — integration test file tests/runtime_audio_lifecycle.rs submitting ConfConnect/ConfDisconnect and the 4 audio-lifecycle commands through a live CoreReactor + MockBackend and asserting oneshot replies.
**Out of scope (items intentionally excluded, with justification):**
- Real PJSIP FFI conference-port integration (pjsua_conf_connect / pjsua_conf_disconnect) — deferred to P2-4; requires FFI binding, this ticket uses MockBackend only.
- Audio resampling, stereo/pair alignment, dynamic frame_duration — deferred to P1+ (AudioMixer is mono 8kHz 20ms i16).
- CPAL/microphone capture and real hardware audio I/O — deferred to P1-4.
- Slab-based source allocation for >32 sources — deferred to P1+ (documented future optimization).
- f32 sample-type migration of AsyncAudioSource — deferred to a future round (i16 is the current contract).
**Affected areas (components/systems impacted, even without direct modification):**
- src/runtime/command.rs — DispatchCommand gains up to 3 variants; Display/Debug/from_runtime_command matches must stay exhaustive.
- src/runtime/handle.rs — public API surface gains 4 submit methods; submit() match on DispatchCommand becomes total (no unreachable!()).
- src/runtime/reactor.rs — reactor loop gains mixer-backed dispatch arms; AddAudioSource stub replaced.
- src/runtime/backend.rs — MockBackend gains observable counters; SipBackend trait unchanged (no implementor breakage).
- src/runtime/audio_worker.rs — test hook for wrap invariant; no production logic change.

tickets.notes:
- [Implementation steps] 1) Add observable conf_connect/conf_disconnect invocation counters to MockBackend (backend.rs). 2) Add dedicated DispatchCommand variants RemoveAudioSource/SetAudioSourceGain/MuteAudioSource (command.rs) and update from_runtime_command/Debug/Display. 3) Add a reactor-owned Arc<AudioMixer>; wire the AddAudioSource arm to mixer.add_source and the three new arms to mixer ops (reactor.rs). 4) Add RuntimeHandle::submit_add_audio_source / submit_remove_audio_source / submit_set_audio_source_gain / submit_mute_audio_source (handle.rs). 5) Add a #[cfg(test)] next_source_id setter to AudioMixer (audio_worker.rs). 6) Add the O-001..O-006 unit + integration tests. 7) Run make test.
- [Risks] The reactor Execute closure only receives &mut dyn SipBackend, not the mixer — audio-lifecycle commands that mutate the mixer cannot be handled inside a plain Execute closure; they need dedicated DispatchCommand variants processed by the reactor loop (single-writer rule). DashMap iteration in process_frame must snapshot source_ids (already done) to avoid invalidation.
- [Caveats] The reactor mixer is a single default-call mixer for now; per-call routing of audio-lifecycle commands (call_id scoping) is a P2+ concern and requires adding a call_id field to the variants. Reply type remains Result<_, ReactorError> — SipError conversion happens at the public API boundary (SipClient).
- [Open items] Should the audio-lifecycle commands carry call_id for per-call routing? Current decision: no — a single reactor-owned default mixer is in scope; per-call routing is P2+. Should AddAudioSource resolve source_id internally or accept a caller-provided ID? Current decision: internal sequential allocation via AtomicU64.
- [Future improvements] Slab-based source allocation (P1+). Per-source priority mixing (P2+). AsyncAudioSource f32 migration. AudioWorker dynamic frame_duration adjustment. Per-call AudioMixer routing from the reactor.

tickets.invariants:
[Normal condition] RuntimeCommand has 18 distinct enum discriminants, each carrying a typed oneshot::Sender; reply channels are always created at construction and replaced by RuntimeHandle::submit()'s fresh channel (never reused). AudioMixer source_id starts at 0 and increments monotonically; per-source gain defaults to 1.0 and muted to false on add_source.
[Error invariant] oneshot::Sender is always resolved (send() called) in every code path of reactor dispatch — including the panic path, which replies Err(ReactorError::BackendError) before setting terminated. AudioMixer state is never partially modified: add_source fully inserts source+gain+mute or is a no-op; remove_source removes all three maps together.
[Internal state invariant] The reactor's AudioMixer is the single source of truth for the default-call audio sources; AudioWorkerTask holds its own Arc<AudioMixer> per call. RuntimeCommand reply channels are consumed exactly once by the reactor. process_frame snapshots source_ids before iteration so concurrent add/remove cannot corrupt iteration.
[Boundary invariant] u64 source_id wraps correctly from MAX to 0 (fetch_add wraps; the next available id after MAX is 0). Max 32 sources documented for slab optimization (future P1+). AudioWorker::process_frame must handle 0 sources (zero-filled silence) and 1 source (passthrough). gain clamped to [0.0, 2.0] on both bounds (negative clamps to 0.0, above 2.0 clamps to 2.0).
