The ticket's earlier "17 variants" count predates QueryState (P7-2) and must be corrected to 18.

2. DispatchCommand (command.rs:217-252) — 6 variants: Execute, AddAudioSource, GetAccountInfo, AddAccount, QueryState, Shutdown. RemoveAudioSource/SetAudioSourceGain/MuteAudioSource map to Execute closures that return a hardcoded Err(BackendError("audio source lifecycle not yet connected (P0-7)")) (command.rs:349-383). These closures only receive &mut dyn SipBackend, so they cannot mutate a mixer — they must become dedicated reactor-loop dispatch arms.

3. RuntimeHandle (handle.rs:24-140) — submit() has unreachable!("use submit_add_audio_source instead") for AddAudioSource (handle.rs:73-75) but NO submit_add_audio_source method exists anywhere in the crate (O-003). The four audio-lifecycle submit methods must be added.

4. Reactor (reactor.rs:55-220) — DispatchCommand::AddAudioSource arm (reactor.rs:111-123) is a stub replying Err(BackendError). The reactor owns client_state: ClientState (state.rs:42-52) which has NO AudioMixer field. The reactor must own an Arc<AudioMixer> to route audio-lifecycle commands.

5. Backend trait (backend.rs:16-98) — SipBackend already has conf_connect(&mut self, source: i32, sink: i32) and conf_disconnect (backend.rs:91-98). MockBackend.conf_connect/conf_disconnect (backend.rs:250-257) return Ok(()) with NO observable side effect — tests cannot verify the from_runtime_command closure actually invokes them (O-001).

AudioMixer (audio_worker.rs:130-224) — sources: DashMap<u64, Arc<tokio::sync::Mutex<Box<dyn AsyncAudioSource + Send>>>>, gains/mutes DashMaps, next_source_id: AtomicU64, out_queue/in_queue: crossbeam_queue::ArrayQueue<Vec<i16>>. add_source uses fetch_add(1) (audio_worker.rs:172-178) — the u64::MAX wrap is untestable without a test hook (O-005). set_gain clamps to [0.0, 2.0] (audio_worker.rs:193-202) — only the upper clamp is tested (O-006).

7. AudioWorkerTask/AudioWorkerInner (audio_worker.rs:242-383) — spawn uses tokio::task::spawn_blocking with Handle::current().block_on; run() loops process_frame + sleep(frame_duration). process_frame (audio_worker.rs:336-382) snapshots source_ids, calls next_chunk per source, mixes via mix_i16_frame, pushes to out_queue. No test exercises process_frame with sources present and asserts out_queue content (O-002).

8. asyncaudiosrc_adapter.rs — AsyncAudioSource (re-exported), ErasedAudioSource blanket impl, SyncAudioSource, SyncSourceAdapter all implemented (P5-2). MockAsyncAudioSource (audio_worker.rs:37-61) provides canned data.

tickets.title: Observability, Security & Platform Configuration

contracts.precondition: Observability needed for operations — the crate must provide tracing, metrics, and a capability matrix to consumers.
contracts.postcondition: Every public SipClient/SipAccountHandle method carries #[tracing::instrument]; MetricsRegistry initializes 8 default counters/gauges to zero under #[cfg(feature = "metrics")]; ClientCapabilities is advertised via a ClientInitialized event after SipClient::new() completes (O-002 emission + O-001 attribute presence + O-005 8-metric zero check).
contracts.invariant: Metrics are optional via the `metrics` feature flag — metrics types are structurally feature-gated (#[cfg(feature = "metrics")] precedes MetricsRegistry/MetricsCounter/MetricsGauge/MetricsLookupError, O-003); ClientCapabilities has no video fields (audio-only scope).

contracts.precondition: Security requirements known — passwords must never leak via logs/errors, Authorization headers must be redacted, platform differences documented.
contracts.postcondition: SecretString Display is [REDACTED] and Debug is SecretString([REDACTED]); RawSipMessage::redact_authorization() replaces password in Authorization headers; AuthCredentials.password is SecretString; module docs document Windows/MSVC, macOS frameworks, Linux libs (O-006 include_str!); SecretString zeroizes memory on drop under #[cfg(feature = "zeroize")] (O-004 Drop impl + test).
contracts.invariant: SecretString is used for all password fields — never plain String; zeroization happens on drop when the zeroize feature is active; TLS verify default is true (documented).

contracts.precondition: Usage needs documentation — consumers need a microphone source abstraction and complete usage examples.
contracts.postcondition: open_default_microphone_source(format: AudioFormat) -> Result<Box<dyn AsyncAudioSource>, SipError> exists behind #[cfg(feature = "cpal-input")] (O-007); spec-examples (client init, account register, make_call, audio_tap, TTS source) reference the public API types rather than being empty stubs (O-007).
contracts.invariant: Microphone is an optional feature — cpal-input is NOT in Cargo.toml default features; trait-based source injection works without the feature.

tickets.background:
[::INSPECTION_FLAGGED::]
This ticket has been flagged by the ABC Inspection Pipeline after completing the implementation lifecycle (make → plan → start → review → resolve). The actual source code was rigorously analyzed against three criteria:

  A — Contract Translation:   Are all Precondition/Postcondition/Invariant contracts accurately translated into test code?
  B — Violation Detection:    Can every contract violation be detected by an existing test assertion?
  C — Test Precision:         Are tests precise and unambiguous (no broad assertions, no missing edge cases)?

One or more ABC violations were confirmed (7 omissions: O-001..O-007). This ticket is hereby remanded for re-implementation. Every violation must be fully resolved, and every contract must be fulfilled in this final implementation round.

N0046 defines tracing spans for all public operations and the optional metrics feature. N0047 defines security (SecretString, Authorization redaction) and platform differences (Windows MSVC, macOS frameworks, Linux libs). N0050 defines the optional cpal-input feature and complete usage examples for client init, account management, calling, audio tap, and AI TTS.

### Goal
Add tracing instrumentation to all public operations, implement SecretString for credential safety, define ClientCapabilities as part of the initialization protocol, document platform-specific build requirements, provide comprehensive usage examples — and close all 7 ABC inspection gaps (O-001..O-007) confirmed in the prior implementation round.

### Purpose
Observability ensures debuggability of production SIP calls; SecretString prevents accidental credential leaks via log output (investigating an incident should never expose passwords); ClientCapabilities enables consumers to adapt their feature usage to what the runtime supports; platform documentation reduces build friction across three target OSes.

### Motivation
Without tracing, diagnosing call failures in production is guesswork. Without SecretString, any error-format! or Debug-impl on AuthCredentials leaks the password to logs. Without ClientCapabilities, consumers cannot determine at runtime whether ICE, SRTP, or a specific codec is available. The ABC inspection confirmed 7 testable behaviors that the prior implementation left untested or unimplemented: (O-001) no compile-time #[instrument] attribute-presence test; (O-002) SipClient::new never emits ClientInitialized; (O-003) metrics types not feature-gated; (O-004) no Drop zeroization for SecretString; (O-005) metrics zero-test covers only 4 of 8 defaults; (O-006) no include_str! platform-doc test; (O-007) open_default_microphone_source missing and spec-examples are empty stubs. These gaps block the first production deployment of siprs.

### Constraints
Must work with existing SipClient facade (P0-3) and EventBus (P0-5). SecretString must be zeroize-compatible but optional (behind zeroize feature). All types must be serde-compatible (behind serde feature) for WebSocket serialization (P4-4). tracing spans must not change public API signatures. cpal-input is optional and non-default. Metrics types must be structurally feature-gated (O-003). open_default_microphone_source defers real capture to the cpal crate (P8-4).
scope: **Scope of changes:**

- [src/config/observability_metrics.rs] Action: modify — add structural `#[cfg(feature = "metrics")]` gating. Detail: MetricsRegistry, MetricsCounter, MetricsGauge, MetricsLookupError are each preceded by `#[cfg(feature = "metrics")]` so the types are unavailable without the feature. Before: types compiled unconditionally (O-003); After: types feature-gated. API: unchanged when feature enabled, absent when disabled. Dep: none (cfg-if already in Cargo.toml).

- [src/config/observability_metrics.rs] Action: modify — extend `metrics_registry_starts_at_zero` test. Detail: assert all 8 default metrics are zero (audio_tap_overflows_total, dtmf_sent_total, dtmf_received_total, ice_failures_total, transport_reconnects_total, raw_sip_messages_total counters; active_calls, registered_accounts gauges) plus exact registry size. Before: 4 of 8 asserted (O-005); After: all 8 asserted. Dep: none.

- [src/security/security_platform_diffs.rs] Action: add — `impl Drop for SecretString` under `#[cfg(feature = "zeroize")]` calling `self.0.zeroize()`. Detail: guarantees heap-buffer zeroization at scope exit. Before: no Drop impl (O-004); After: Drop-triggered zeroization. API: none (Drop is not a method). Dep: zeroize (optional, already declared).

Detail: build a `SipEvent` with `EventMeta` + `ClientInitialized(caps)` and call `event_bus.publish(...)`. Before: ClientInitialized variant existed but never emitted (O-002); After: event emitted once after new() completes. API: none (method signature unchanged).

Before: only Cargo.toml string check (O-001); After: compile-time attribute presence enforced.

Detail: RFC §40 signature; body returns a documented `[::STUB::]` error until the cpal crate lands (P8-4). Before: function absent (O-007); After: signature contract enforced by C051-Pre type-check test.

- [examples/*.rs] Action: modify — spec-examples reference public API types (SipClient, ClientConfig, AccountConfig, SipAccountHandle, OutgoingCallRequest, AsyncAudioSource, AudioFormat) instead of empty `fn main() {}`. Detail: add O-007 source-inspection test asserting non-empty type references. Before: empty stubs (O-007); After: examples demonstrate intended usage. Dep: none (spec-examples feature gate retained).
- [src/config.rs] Action: verify — AuthCredentials.password is `crate::security::SecretString` (C048 invariant); `client_config_password_is_secret_string` test retained. No further change required.
- [Cargo.toml] Action: verify — features `metrics`, `zeroize`, `cpal-input`, `spec-examples` declared; `cpal-input` and `metrics` NOT in default features. No dep added in this ticket.
**Out of scope:**
- [PJSIP FFI binding updates] Excluded — P2-4 handles FFI layer, runtime codec/device enumeration, actual pj_status_t constants.
- [Full async AudioDevice enumeration] Excluded — AudioDeviceCaps struct defined; actual PJSIP device enumeration deferred to P2-4.
- [Real cpal microphone capture] Excluded — `open_default_microphone_source` body is a typed `[::STUB::]`; the `cpal` dependency is added in P8-4.
- [Video codec support] Excluded — audio-only scope maintained (C001 invariant); no video fields in ClientCapabilities.
- [Platform build scripts / build.rs cfg] Excluded — platform notes are documentation-only; actual build.rs implementation in P3-5.
- [tracing-subscriber dev-dependency] Excluded — span runtime capture deferred per testExceptions; O-001 source-inspection covers the compile-time contract.
**Affected areas:**

- [SipClient public API] Medium impact — method signatures unchanged; new ClientInitialized event emission is observable via EventBus; new `all_public_client_methods_are_instrumented` source-inspection test.
- [EventBus / ClientInitialized] Medium impact — ClientInitialized(ClientCapabilities) now actually published; consumers can subscribe and react to init completion.
- [AuthCredentials builder] Low impact — password field already SecretString; builders accept `Into<SecretString>` (String/&str/SecretString).
- [Metrics feature surface] Low impact — metrics types compile only under `--features metrics`; existing `cfg(feature = "metrics")` tests unchanged; CI matrix must run `--features metrics`.
- [Security posture] Positive impact — drop-zeroization (O-004) strengthens credential hygiene; platform-doc test (O-006) locks build documentation.

## Translatability improvements (Boy Scout Rule)

### 1. src/config/observability_metrics.rs — metrics feature-gating + test precision
**Current**: Metrics types compiled unconditionally; `metrics_types_not_available_without_feature` is an empty no-op (a lying test name). `metrics_registry_starts_at_zero` asserts only 4 of 8 metrics (under-specified).
**Target**: Add structural `#[cfg(feature = "metrics")]` on each metrics type so the source reads as "these types exist only under the metrics feature". Replace the no-op with `metrics_types_are_feature_gated` (source-inspection asserting the cfg attribute precedes each type). Extend `metrics_registry_starts_at_zero` to name all 8 metrics — the test then reads as a complete inventory.

### 2. src/security/security_platform_diffs.rs — drop-zeroization + doc enforcement
**Current**: `impl zeroize::Zeroize` exists but drop does not zeroize (a security gap the doc comment implies is covered: "the inner memory is zeroed on drop"). The doc comment lies.
**Target**: Add `#[cfg(feature = "zeroize")] impl Drop for SecretString` so the comment becomes true; add `secret_string_zeroized_on_drop` buffer-zero test; add `platform_docs_contain_os_notes` include_str! test so the OS-specific build notes are enforced rather than decorative.

### 3. src/client.rs — ClientInitialized emission + instrument enforcement
**Current**: `SipClient::new` returns a receiver but never publishes the initialization result; the `ClientInitialized` variant is dead code. `tracing_and_metrics_specified` asserts only that Cargo.toml contains the substring 'tracing' — it cannot detect removal of `#[instrument]`.
**Target**: Publish `ClientInitialized(ClientCapabilities::new())` after Initialize succeeds so the facade reads as "construct → initialize → advertise capabilities". Add `all_public_client_methods_are_instrumented` (source-inspection) so the tracing contract is provable, replacing the substring check as the primary guard.

### 4. src/api/asyncaudiosrc_adapter.rs — RFC §40 API contract
**Current**: The RFC-specified `open_default_microphone_source` does not exist; examples are empty `fn main() {}` stubs that demonstrate nothing.
**Target**: Add `open_default_microphone_source(format: AudioFormat) -> Result<Box<dyn AsyncAudioSource>, SipError>` behind `#[cfg(feature = "cpal-input")]` (typed STUB body pending cpal/P8-4) so the module reads as the audio-source entry point. Add `spec_examples_reference_public_api_types` so examples become documentation that references the real API.

### 5. Extract hardcoded feature strings into named constants
**Current**: Feature names are compared inline against string literals in tests (e.g., "cpal-input", "metrics") in client.rs and observability_metrics.rs.
**Target**: Define `const FEATURE_CPAL_INPUT: &str = "cpal-input"` and `const FEATURE_METRICS: &str = "metrics"` in a `features` constants module (or per-module consts) for test reuse — prevents drift if a feature is renamed.

contracts.precondition: PJSUA C library uses pj_pool_t for memory allocation. Callback parameters valid only within callback scope.
contracts.postcondition: pj_str_t always has Rust-owned backing (Vec<u8>). Native callback pointers not held beyond callback scope. pj_pool_t memory never embedded in Rust structs.
contracts.invariant: pj_str_t values outside FFI calls always point to Rust-owned memory. Original PJSUA ptr only used as source for immediate copy, never stored.

acceptanceCriteria: 【Happy path】Adding `pjsua-native` to the feature set with PJSIP headers available causes build.rs to run bindgen against wrapper.h and emit `pjsua_*` FFI declarations into OUT_DIR; `cargo build --features pjsua-native` succeeds and links.
【Happy path】build.rs resolves the PJSIP header root per RFC §28.1 search order (vendor/prebuilt/{target-triple}/include first, then vendor/pjsip source build) and passes wrapper.h to bindgen.
【Happy path】wrapper.h uncomments `#include <pjsua.h>`, `#include <pjmedia.h>`, and `#include <pjmedia-codec/opus.h>` when the `pjsua-native` feature is enabled.
【Happy path】The bindgen allowlist restricts generated declarations to the symbol subset siprs uses (pjsua_acc_id, pjsua_call_id, pj_str_t, pjsua_call_get_info, etc.), keeping compile times low.
【Error case】With the feature disabled (default), the crate compiles with no bindgen and no PJSIP installation using the stub aliases in src/ffi/bindings.rs — the default build must not fail.

【Error case】With the feature enabled but headers/libraries missing, build.rs fails with a user-friendly error that names the missing dependency and references the RFC §28 per-OS package list — not a raw clang/bindgen error.

【Edge case】The generated bindings and the stub aliases are mutually exclusive: exactly one compiles depending on the feature flag; `check-cfg` lists `pjsua-native` so `cargo check` emits no unexpected-cfg warning.
【Invariant】No `unsafe` appears outside the ffi/ module after the build change (C038); build.rs itself contains no unsafe.

tickets.notes:
- Stub markers resolved: build.rs:8 (covers build.rs:8,11), wrapper.h:6.
- Implementation steps: 1) add `pjsua-native = []` to Cargo.toml [features] and `pjsua-native` to lints.rust check-cfg (line 40); 2) add `[build-dependencies]` bindgen (pin a version, e.g. bindgen = "0.69"); 3) implement build.rs main() per RFC §28: detect the feature via CARGO_FEATURE_PJSUA_NATIVE, resolve the header root (vendor/prebuilt/{triple}/include → vendor/pjsip), run bindgen with the allowlist against wrapper.h, write to OUT_DIR; 4) uncomment the wrapper.h includes; 5) feature-gate src/ffi/bindings.rs stub aliases behind `#[cfg(not(feature = "pjsua-native"))]`.
- Related tickets: P3-2 (original FFI layer, contracts C038/C057), P8-18 (replace hand-coded PJSIP constants with bindgen output — consumes this ticket), P8-20 (wire real FFI call sites — consumes this ticket).
- Caveat: bindgen output varies by clang/bindgen version — the allowlist keeps the generated surface small and reviewable; pin the bindgen dependency in Cargo.toml. Verify with `make check-be` (default, stub path) and a feature-enabled build in a PJSIP-capable CI job.
tickets.invariants: 【C038】All unsafe code is isolated to the ffi/ module; no unsafe keyword appears in runtime/, client.rs, or config/ (compile-time enforced). 【C057】pj_str_t values outside FFI calls always point to Rust-owned memory (Vec<u8>); the original PJSUA pointer is used only as a source for immediate copy, never stored. 【Feature exclusivity】When `pjsua-native` is off, the crate builds with no external C library and no bindgen; when it is on, the bindgen-generated declarations replace the hand-written stubs exactly once — both are never compiled together. 【Build determinism】The bindgen allowlist is a fixed symbol set so generated output stays minimal and reviewable.
tickets.instrumentation:
- build.rs emits cargo:rerun-if-env-changed=CARGO_FEATURE_PJSUA_NATIVE and cargo:rerun-if-changed=wrapper.h so the script reruns when inputs change.
- build.rs prints which build path was taken (prebuilt / source-build / stub fallback) via println! so `cargo build -v` CI logs show the mode that produced the crate.
- When the feature is enabled but headers are missing, build.rs prints the RFC §28 package list to stderr with a `cargo:warning=` diagnostic so the failure reason is visible without a full build log.
tickets.investigation: build.rs:8-13 — `fn main()` is empty; lines 11-12 note 'feature and configure the wrapper.h header path once PJSIP is installed. The stub aliases in src/ffi/bindings.rs keep the crate compiling.' wrapper.h:6-10 — the three `#include` directives (`<pjsua.h>`, `<pjmedia.h>`, `<pjmedia-codec/opus.h>`) are commented out. Cargo.toml [features] (lines 15-37) declares no `pjsua-native` feature and there is no [build-dependencies] section, so `bindgen` is not available to build.rs; lints.rust check-cfg (line 40) lists only `cpal-input`. src/ffi/bindings.rs (lines 16-193) holds hand-written stub aliases (pjsua_acc_id, pjsua_call_id, pj_str_t, pjsua_call_info) and a stub pjsua_call_get_info (lines 124-133) that keep the crate compiling without a PJSIP install; the module header comment (lines 3-6) already promises bindgen output replaces it under `pjsua-native`. RFC §28.1-§28.4 specify the build.rs search order (prebuilt → source build → bindgen) and per-OS package requirements. A real implementation must: add the feature, add bindgen to [build-dependencies], implement header-root resolution + allowlist + OUT_DIR emission, uncomment wrapper.h, and feature-gate the stub aliases so bindgen output replaces them only when the feature is enabled.
tickets.boyScoutPlan:
- The `[::STUB::]` comments in build.rs and wrapper.h are deleted once the real build script and includes are in place (no leftover STUB debris).
- bindgen allowlist symbols move into a named const array (e.g. BINDGEN_ALLOWLIST: &[&str]) so the symbol list reads as a declaration, not inline strings.
- build.rs functions are named as verb phrases matching RFC §28.2 pseudo-code: prebuilt_available(), emit_link_directives(), generate_bindings() — the flow reads top-to-bottom as prose.
- Error messages from build.rs use the RFC §28 package-list names verbatim so users can act on them.
- src/ffi/bindings.rs keeps the named constants PJ_SUCCESS/PJ_EUNKNOWN (already present) for any retained stub code; no new magic numbers.

tickets.title: Wire spawn_dtmf_sent_timeout into the reactor SendDtmf handler and implement the two-phase DTMF-sent timeout once the reactor owns an EventBus

contracts.precondition: Call API supports DTMF — pjsua_call_dial_dtmf() can be called with valid native_call_id and digit string; AccountConfig::validate() rejects empty DtmfPolicy::send_methods or receive_methods
contracts.postcondition: DTMF specification defined — DtmfMethod enum has variants for Inband, SipInfo (Info), Rfc4733; DtmfReceivedInfo struct contains method:DtmfMethod, digit:char, duration_ms:Option<u16>, volume_dbm0:Option<i8>; data types implement Clone + Debug
contracts.invariant: 3 DTMF method categories: Inband (RFC 2833 in-band tone), SIP INFO (SipInfo in Info variant), RFC 4733 (out-of-band RTP event). DtmfPolicy always has at least one send_method and one receive_method — validated in AccountConfig::validate().

contracts.precondition: DTMF spec defined — DtmfMethod, DtmfReceivedInfo, DtmfPolicy types exist in the crate; DtmfSent event variant exists in SipEventPayload
contracts.postcondition: DtmfSentInfo and two-phase design — DtmfSentInfo { method, digit, status: Result<(), SentDtmfError>, pjsip_status } defined; send_dtmf() returns Ok(()) synchronously for command acceptance; DtmfSent event fires asynchronously on completion or timeout
contracts.invariant: 500ms default timeout (DEFAULT_DTMF_SENT_TIMEOUT_MS) for DtmfSent fallback when PJSIP callback unavailable; configurable via DtmfConfig::sent_timeout_ms

tickets.background:
[::INSPECTION_FLAGGED::]
This ticket has been flagged for rejection due to detection of implementation deficiencies, unresolved STUB markers, or other violations. It has been returned for re-implementation. A complete implementation free of all defects, STUB markers, and violations must be achieved in this final implementation round. Complete it this time.

Source ticket P5-2 (DTMF Specification, AsyncAudioSource & Incoming Call/Transfer) specified the DtmfSent two-phase design per contract C030: DtmfSentInfo separates synchronous command acceptance from asynchronous completion, and spawn_dtmf_sent_timeout implements the 500ms fallback timer. The function was left behind an #[allow(dead_code)] because the reactor did not yet own an EventBus at the time P5-2 landed. This work item resolves the marker by wiring spawn_dtmf_sent_timeout into the reactor SendDtmf dispatch path so the two-phase DtmfSent flow is actually exercised once the reactor owns an EventBus.
scope: src/api/m20_dtmfsent_twophase.rs (spawn_dtmf_sent_timeout — remove #[allow(dead_code)] once a reactor call site exists)
src/runtime/command.rs (RuntimeCommand::SendDtmf dispatch — invoke spawn_dtmf_sent_timeout after backend.send_dtmf succeeds)
src/runtime/reactor.rs (reactor ownership of an EventBus / default_event_bus so the timeout event has a publish target; route via dispatch_event)
Out of scope: real PJSIP send-complete callback wiring (P8-29 / pjsua-native FFI); unification of the two DtmfMethod enums (account_config_spec vs m20_dtmfsent_twophase).
Impact: DtmfSent events are now emitted from the reactor via the EventBus; send_dtmf() still returns Ok(()) on command acceptance and the completion/timeout arrives asynchronously.
testUnit: UT: [C030-Post] spawn_dtmf_sent_timeout publishes SipEventPayload::DtmfSent { Err(Timeout) } after the timeout elapses under tokio::time::pause (extend the existing test at src/api/m20_dtmfsent_twophase.rs:111).
UT: [C030-Inv] spawn_dtmf_sent_timeout falls back to DEFAULT_DTMF_SENT_TIMEOUT_MS when no explicit timeout_ms is supplied.
UT: [Normal] The SendDtmf dispatch spawns the timeout timer after a successful mock backend.send_dtmf, and does NOT spawn it when the backend returns Err.
UT: [Boundary] Aborting the returned JoinHandle before the timer fires suppresses the DtmfSent Timeout event (no publication).
UT: [Normal] The published DtmfSent event carries the correct call_id in EventMeta and the correct method/digit.
testIntegration: IT: [Two-phase flow] Submit RuntimeCommand::SendDtmf through the reactor with a mock backend that never fires completion; assert a DtmfSent Timeout event arrives on the EventBus after the configured timeout.
IT: [Cancellation] When a completion callback fires before the timer, assert no DtmfSent Timeout event is published (single publication).
IT: [EventBus routing] DtmfSent for a registered account_id is routed to the per-account bus; otherwise to the default bus.
testExceptions: The real PJSIP send-complete callback timing cannot be exercised without a live PJSIP stack (FFI linkage / pjsua-native). The 500ms fallback timer and its cancellation are fully unit-testable via tokio::time control.

Per-account vs default EventBus routing of DtmfSent depends on dispatch_event, which is gated behind P8-29 (NativeEvent dispatch wiring); routing is asserted at the unit level where the bus map is injectable.
acceptanceCriteria: 【Happy path】After backend.send_dtmf succeeds, the reactor SendDtmf handler spawns spawn_dtmf_sent_timeout so a DtmfSent { method, digit, status: Err(SentDtmfError::Timeout), pjsip_status: None } event is published to the EventBus when no PJSIP completion callback arrives within DEFAULT_DTMF_SENT_TIMEOUT_MS.
【Happy path】send_dtmf() still returns Ok(()) synchronously for command acceptance — the two-phase separation (C030) is preserved.
【Error case】When backend.send_dtmf returns Err, the handler does NOT spawn the timeout timer and propagates the error; no spurious DtmfSent Timeout event is published.
【Edge case】When the real completion callback fires before the timer, the retained JoinHandle is aborted so DtmfSent is published at most once per digit (never a duplicate Timeout).
【Edge case】The EventBus used as the publish target is the reactor-owned bus (per-account when the event account_id matches, otherwise the default bus), consistent with dispatch_event routing.

tickets.background:
[::INSPECTION_FLAGGED::]
This ticket has been flagged for rejection due to detection of implementation deficiencies, unresolved STUB markers, or other violations. It has been returned for re-implementation. A complete implementation free of all defects, STUB markers, and violations must be achieved in this final implementation round. Complete it this time.

Source ticket P4-2 (Audio Format, IN/OUT PairAligner, Resampler & Codec Policy) defined AccountConfig and its validation rules (C015/C052). SipAccountHandle::update_config was left as a no-op because no incremental update path existed. This work item resolves the marker by introducing an AccountConfigPatch type and a RuntimeCommand::UpdateAccount variant so account configuration can be changed at runtime and dispatched through the reactor.
scope: src/api/public_api_design.rs (update_config — accept AccountConfigPatch, submit RuntimeCommand::UpdateAccount, await the reply)
src/runtime/command.rs (add RuntimeCommand::UpdateAccount variant and dispatch to SipBackend::update_account)
src/runtime/backend.rs (SipBackend::update_account trait method; MockBackend impl)
src/runtime/state.rs (ClientState AccountEntry config update on success)
src/config/account_config_spec.rs (AccountConfigPatch type definition)
Out of scope: full AccountConfig schema migration; pjsua_acc_modify FFI call (P8-20 / P4+).
Impact: update_config is no longer a silent no-op; patches are validated and applied via the reactor.
testUnit: UT: [Normal] AccountConfigPatch construction, field access, and Default (no-op) derive.
UT: [C015] update_config with an invalid patch returns Err(SipError) before dispatch.
UT: [Normal] update_config submits UpdateAccount and returns Ok(()) on a successful mock reactor reply.
UT: [Error] update_config maps a reactor Err to a SipError (e.g. ConfigError).
UT: [Boundary] Applying a no-op patch leaves the ClientState account entry unchanged.
testIntegration: IT: [Reactor round-trip] update_config(patch) followed by accounts()/QueryState reflects the patched config in ClientState.
IT: [Dispatch] RuntimeCommand::UpdateAccount is serialized FIFO with other commands through the reactor channel.
testExceptions: The actual PJSUA account modification (pjsua_acc_modify) cannot be tested without live PJSIP linkage; the patch type, validation, and reactor dispatch are fully unit-testable.
The exact set of runtime-mutable fields is a product decision — the patch must only expose fields the backend can actually change.
acceptanceCriteria: 【Happy path】update_config(patch) submits RuntimeCommand::UpdateAccount and returns Ok(()) when the reactor applies the patch.
【Happy path】An AccountConfigPatch type exists exposing a runtime-mutable subset of AccountConfig (e.g. register_on_start, transport policy, codec policy), Send+Sync and Default (no-op patch).
【Error case】A patch that fails AccountConfig validation (C015/C052) returns Err(SipError) before dispatch — fail-fast.
【Error case】A reactor Err from UpdateAccount maps to a SipError (e.g. ConfigError) instead of silently succeeding.
【Edge case】An empty/no-op patch is accepted and returns Ok(()) without modifying reactor state.
The applied patch is reflected in the reactor ClientState account entry (subsequent accounts()/QueryState reflects it).

tickets.notes: Stub: src/api/public_api_design.rs:148. Adding a RuntimeCommand variant is a public command-enum change — update every match in src/runtime/command.rs (name(), to_dispatch, Debug) and any exhaustive matches elsewhere. Related: P3-1 (AccountConfig/validation), P4-2 (codec policy subset), P7 (config-change events).
tickets.invariants: C012 — API is Send+Sync. C015 — Validation rules enforced. C052 — All validation rules enumerated. New: update_config never silently drops a patch — a non-Ok reply is surfaced as an error.
tickets.instrumentation: log::trace! on update_config dispatch with the changed field set. log::warn! on patch validation failure.
tickets.investigation: src/api/public_api_design.rs:146-152 — update_config(&self, _patch: AccountConfig) -> Result<(), SipError> is a no-op that discards the patch and returns Ok(()). src/runtime/command.rs — RuntimeCommand has AddAccount/RemoveAccount/SetRegistration but no UpdateAccount variant; a new variant must be added and matched in name(), to_dispatch, and Debug (command.rs ~154-190). src/runtime/backend.rs — the SipBackend trait has add_account/remove_account but no update_account method. src/config/account_config_spec.rs:151 — AccountConfig is the full config; a runtime-mutable subset must be defined separately as AccountConfigPatch. Real implementation: define AccountConfigPatch, add RuntimeCommand::UpdateAccount { account_id, patch, reply }, add SipBackend::update_account, update the ClientState AccountEntry on success, and make update_config dispatch + await the reply.
tickets.boyScoutPlan: Replace the discard-pattern `_patch` parameter with a real typed patch. Reuse AccountConfig::validate rules (C015/C052) for the mutable subset so patch validation cannot diverge. Keep the RuntimeCommand match arms exhaustive when adding the new variant.

tickets.background:
[::INSPECTION_FLAGGED::]
This ticket has been flagged for rejection due to detection of implementation deficiencies, unresolved STUB markers, or other violations. It has been returned for re-implementation. A complete implementation free of all defects, STUB markers, and violations must be achieved in this final implementation round. Complete it this time.

Source ticket P4-2 (Audio Format, IN/OUT PairAligner, Resampler & Codec Policy) specified the codec policy but left runtime enumeration deferred. The marker at src/config/observability_metrics.rs:69 was left as a stub because the FFI-defined pjsua_codec_info types are not generated until bindgen runs under the pjsua-native feature. This work item resolves it by replacing the placeholder codec list and Codec type with runtime codec enumeration via the PJSIP codec API.
scope: - src/config/observability_metrics.rs:69,187 — replace the available_codecs: Vec<Codec> placeholder and the Codec struct with FFI-backed enumeration
- src/ffi/bindings.rs — consume the bindgen-generated pjsua_codec_info type once pjsua-native is enabled
- src/ffi/mod.rs — expose the codec-enumeration FFI surface (pjsua_enum_codecs path)
- Out of scope: PairAligner/resampler pipeline (C036/C037); codec policy/negotiation internals (C041/C042) beyond what enumeration feeds.
- Impact: ClientCapabilities.available_codecs, ClientCapabilities.opus_available, and every caller reading codec capability.
testUnit: UT: [Normal] maps a pjsua_codec_info fixture (id="opus", clock_rate=48000) to Codec { id, name, clock_rate }
UT: [Normal] opus_available is true when the enumerated list contains "opus" and false otherwise
UT: [Boundary] an empty enumeration yields an empty available_codecs and opus_available=false
UT: [Error] an enumeration FFI error returns an empty list with a logged diagnostic and no panic
testIntegration: IT: With pjsua-native enabled, ClientCapabilities::new() reflects the real codec set; with it disabled, available_codecs is empty.
testExceptions: Real codec enumeration requires a linked PJSIP library (pjsua_enum_codecs), so unit tests use a fixed pjsua_codec_info fixture — the live call is environment-dependent. Only the three Codec fields (id, name, clock_rate) are modelled and asserted; other pjsua_codec_info fields are out of scope.
acceptanceCriteria: 【Happy path】ClientCapabilities.available_codecs is populated from a real pjsua codec enumeration when pjsua-native is enabled, mapping each pjsua_codec_info entry to Codec { id, name, clock_rate }.
【Happy path】ClientCapabilities.opus_available reflects whether the enumerated codecs contain "opus".
【Error case】When enumeration fails (no PJSIP link, FFI error), available_codecs degrades to an empty list rather than panicking, and the failure is logged.
【Edge case】A one-to-one mapping test converts a fixed pjsua_codec_info fixture (id, name, clock_rate) to Codec.
【Edge case】Without pjsua-native, the fallback path still yields an empty available_codecs and the crate compiles without PJSIP.
tickets.relatedTicketIds: P5-2 (depends on: AudioMixer uses audio format types), P2-3 (depends on: event system uses AudioChunk), P7 (depends on: audio subscribe uses AudioChunkPair)
tickets.notes: Stub sites: src/config/observability_metrics.rs:69,187. Depends on P8-5 (bindgen generates pjsua_codec_info) and P8-16 (pjsua-native feature flag). Implementation: (1) add Codec::from_pjsua_codec_info; (2) add the FFI codec-enumeration function under pjsua-native; (3) call it when populating ClientCapabilities; (4) keep the empty-list fallback for the non-feature path. Related: P8-18 (PJSIP constants).
tickets.invariants: Codec auto mode must assign Opus=255 and PCMU=254 invariantly (C042). Codec policy only accepts PCMU and Opus (C041) — enumeration may report more codecs, but policy filtering still restricts to PCMU/Opus. Every enumerated Codec has a non-empty id and clock_rate > 0. available_codecs is derived from enumeration, never hand-maintained — no hardcoded codec list remains.
tickets.instrumentation: Add tracing::info! on enumeration success with the codec count, and tracing::warn! on enumeration failure. Consider a 'codecs.enumerated' counter metric.
tickets.investigation: src/config/observability_metrics.rs declares ClientCapabilities.available_codecs: Vec<Codec> at line 69, ClientCapabilities::new() initializes it to Vec::new(), and the Codec struct at lines 187-196 is { id: String, name: String, clock_rate: u32 } — a pure placeholder with no FFI backing (the marker covers :69 and :187). ffi/bindings.rs currently provides only stub type aliases (pjsua_acc_id = i32, pjsua_call_id = i32, pjsua_conf_port_id = i32, pjsua_transport_id = i32) and a minimal pjsua_call_info mirror — there is no pjsua_codec_info yet (that arrives with the P8-5 bindgen work). A real implementation must add a codec-enumeration FFI surface (pjsua_enum_codecs / pjsua_codec_info), map each entry into Codec, populate available_codecs and opus_available, and keep the non-pjsua-native path compiling with an empty list.
tickets.boyScoutPlan: Remove the placeholder comment above Codec once it has a real from_pjsua_codec_info conversion. Extract the mapping as a named conversion function so the enumeration loop reads as prose. Document the empty-list fallback in ClientCapabilities::new() instead of leaving it unexplained.

tickets.background:
[::INSPECTION_FLAGGED::]
This ticket has been flagged for rejection due to detection of implementation deficiencies, unresolved STUB markers, or other violations. It has been returned for re-implementation. A complete implementation free of all defects, STUB markers, and violations must be achieved in this final implementation round. Complete it this time.

Source ticket P4-2 (Audio Format, IN/OUT PairAligner, Resampler & Codec Policy) introduced PJSIP-native state mapping, but the PJSUA/PJSIP numeric constants were hand-copied from pjsua.h. These markers were left as stubs because the bindgen-generated constants from pjsua.h are not available until the pjsua-native feature enables FFI. This work item resolves them by replacing the hand-coded constants with the bindgen-generated constants.
scope: - src/error/error_design_siperror.rs:32 — replace hand-coded PJ_SUCCESS/PJ_ENOMEM/PJ_EINVALIDOP/PJ_EBUSY consts consumed by convert_pj_status
- src/error/m20_runtime_command_error.rs:32 — replace hand-coded PJ_SUCCESS/PJ_EINVALIDOP consumed by the M20 error converters
- src/state/m20_callstate_mapping.rs:59,70 — replace hand-coded pjsip_inv_state and pjsua_call_media_status modules
- src/ffi/bindings.rs — expose the bindgen-generated constants under pjsua-native; keep stub aliases otherwise
- Out of scope: SipErrorKind semantics; call-state conversion logic beyond the constant source.
- Impact: convert_pj_status, convert_call_state, convert_call_media_state, and every M20 native_error_with_status caller.
testUnit: UT: [Normal] convert_pj_status maps PJ_SUCCESS to None and PJ_EINVALIDOP to NativeError using the bindgen constants
UT: [Normal] convert_call_state maps pjsip_inv_state::CONFIRMED to CallConnected and DISCONNECTED to CallDisconnected
UT: [Normal] convert_call_media_state maps pjsua_call_media_status values (ACTIVE, LOCAL_HOLD, REMOTE_HOLD, ERROR) to CallMediaState
UT: [Boundary] pjsip_inv_state::NULL yields None (no event published)
UT: [Error] an unknown state value falls through to None without panicking
testIntegration: IT: A full build with pjsua-native enabled compiles, and the call/error mapping tests pass against the bindgen-generated constants.
testExceptions: The bindgen-generated constants only exist under pjsua-native with a real PJSIP install; unit tests assert behavior through the mapping functions, which is identical under both constant sources. The exact numeric values are owned by pjsua.h/bindgen — this ticket asserts mapping behavior, not the numeric values.
acceptanceCriteria: 【Happy path】With pjsua-native enabled, error_design_siperror.rs, m20_runtime_command_error.rs, and m20_callstate_mapping.rs reference the bindgen-generated constants (PJ_SUCCESS, PJ_EINVALIDOP, PJSUA_CALL_* / pjsua_call_media_status) with no hand-coded duplicate values.
【Happy path】convert_pj_status / convert_call_state / convert_call_media_state produce identical outputs to the previous hand-coded values for the same inputs (behavior regression preserved).
【Error case】A constant missing from the bindgen output causes a compile error — there is no silent fallback to a hardcoded value.
【Edge case】Without pjsua-native, the ffi::bindings stub aliases keep the crate compiling and the mapping functions still work against the stub constants.
tickets.relatedTicketIds: P5-2 (depends on: AudioMixer uses audio format types), P2-3 (depends on: event system uses AudioChunk), P7 (depends on: audio subscribe uses AudioChunkPair)
tickets.notes: Stub sites: src/error/error_design_siperror.rs:32, src/error/m20_runtime_command_error.rs:32, src/state/m20_callstate_mapping.rs:59,70. Depends on P8-5 (bindgen output) and P8-16 (pjsua-native feature). Implementation: (1) expose the bindgen constants from ffi::bindings under pjsua-native; (2) replace the local consts with ffi::bindings references; (3) keep stub aliases for the non-feature path; (4) keep the mapping tests green. Related: P8-17 (codec enumeration), P8-20 (FFI call sites).
tickets.invariants: No PJSIP/PJSUA numeric constant is hand-coded in src/error or src/state — every value comes from ffi::bindings (bindgen under pjsua-native, stub aliases otherwise). Codec auto mode must assign Opus=255 and PCMU=254 invariantly (C042). Codec policy only accepts PCMU and Opus (C041).
tickets.instrumentation: No new runtime metrics required. Add a compile-time assertion that the mapping functions still compile when the constant source switches to bindgen.
tickets.investigation: Three files hand-code PJSUA constants. error_design_siperror.rs:32 defines const PJ_SUCCESS: i32 = 0, PJ_ENOMEM: i32 = -2, PJ_EINVALIDOP: i32 = 150002, PJ_EBUSY, consumed by convert_pj_status (lines 300-306). m20_runtime_command_error.rs:32 defines PJ_SUCCESS = 0 and PJ_EINVALIDOP = 150002, consumed by convert_conf_disconnect_error and native_error_with_status (lines 40-50). m20_callstate_mapping.rs:59-70 defines pjsip_inv_state { NULL=0, CALLING=1, CONNECTING=2, CONFIRMED=3, DISCONNECTED=4 } and pjsua_call_media_status { NONE=0, ACTIVE=1, LOCAL_HOLD=2, REMOTE_HOLD=3, ERROR=4 }, used by convert_call_state and convert_call_media_state. ffi/bindings.rs currently carries stub aliases (PJ_SUCCESS=0, PJ_EUNKNOWN=-1, PJSUA_CALL_NULL..PJSUA_CALL_DISCONNECTED=0..6, PJSUA_REG_STATE_*) and will be replaced by bindgen output under pjsua-native. The real implementation must route the three files through ffi::bindings constants and delete the local duplicate const blocks.
tickets.boyScoutPlan: Delete the duplicated const blocks and route every reference through ffi::bindings so there is a single source of truth. Remove the 'hand-coded duplicates of pjsua.h' comments. Consolidate the PJ_SUCCESS/PJ_EINVALIDOP imports shared by error_design_siperror.rs and m20_runtime_command_error.rs onto one source.

Source ticket P4-2 (Audio Format, IN/OUT PairAligner, Resampler & Codec Policy) specified the audio pipeline, but the underlying PJSIP FFI calls were left canned or unimplemented. The markers at src/ffi/bindings.rs:123, src/runtime/backend.rs:287, and src/state/m20_native_event_conv.rs:110 were left as stubs because the pjsua-native feature and library linkage are not ready. This work item resolves them by replacing the canned/unimplemented FFI call sites with real bindgen-generated calls and obtaining actual media_status.
scope: - src/ffi/bindings.rs:123 — replace the canned pjsua_call_get_info stub with the real bindgen call; extend pjsua_call_info to the full bindgen struct (conf_slot + media_status)
- src/runtime/backend.rs:287 — implement PjsuaBackend methods against real PJSUA FFI instead of Err(BackendError("unimplemented"))
- src/state/m20_native_event_conv.rs:110 — call the real pjsua_call_get_info to obtain actual media_status instead of hardcoding 1
- Out of scope: build detection/feature flags (P8-16); bindgen generation (P8-5); callback registration (P8-21).
- Impact: CallMediaStateChanged event accuracy; PjsuaBackend call/registration/media operations.
testUnit: UT: [Normal] convert_call_media_state maps media_status values (0=NONE, 1=ACTIVE, 2/3=LOCAL/REMOTE_HOLD, 4=ERROR) to CallMediaState
UT: [Normal] a real pjsua_call_get_info result (fixture) sets both conf_slot and media_status on the info struct
UT: [Error] pjsua_call_get_info returning non-PJ_SUCCESS produces a BackendError carrying the status
UT: [Edge] an unknown/absent media_status maps to a safe default (CallMediaState::Error) rather than panicking
testIntegration: IT: An incoming call's media event flows callback → NativeEvent::CallMediaStateChanged → real pjsua_call_get_info → CallMediaState, without the hardcoded media_status=1.
IT: PjsuaBackend::hangup / make_call propagate real PJSUA return codes into ReactorError.
testExceptions: Real FFI calls require PJSIP library linkage (pjsua-native + linked lib); unit tests use a fixture/mock for pjsua_call_get_info because the real symbol is unavailable in the sandbox. End-to-end media_status accuracy depends on a live PJSIP call — the event-conversion path is unit-tested with fixture media_status values.
acceptanceCriteria: 【Happy path】Under pjsua-native, pjsua_call_get_info invokes the real FFI symbol and fills conf_slot and media_status from the actual pjsua_call_info struct.
【Happy path】NativeEvent::CallMediaStateChanged converts the real media_status from pjsua_call_get_info into CallMediaState (Active/Held/Error) — no hardcoded 1.
【Happy path】PjsuaBackend methods (make_call, answer_call, hangup, conf_connect, etc.) call real PJSUA functions and return their actual status.
【Error case】A non-success PJSUA status from a real FFI call maps to Err(ReactorError::BackendError) with the diagnostic preserved — never a canned success.
【Edge case】Without pjsua-native, the stub aliases remain so the crate compiles; the real-call path is feature-gated.
【Edge case】The canned-value tests in bindings.rs are replaced by tests asserting the real-call wiring (or are feature-gated).

Implementation: (1) replace the pjsua_call_get_info stub with the real call under pjsua-native; (2) extend pjsua_call_info with media_status; (3) wire m20_native_event_conv to read the real media_status; (4) implement the PjsuaBackend methods; (5) keep the non-feature stub path. Related: P8-18 (constants), P8-21 (callbacks).
tickets.invariants: The media_status reported for a call always comes from pjsua_call_get_info — never a hardcoded constant. Every PjsuaBackend method returns Err on a non-zero PJSUA status; a canned Ok(()) for an unexecuted FFI call is prohibited. Audio delivery keeps IN/OUT paired by timestamp (C031); codec policy remains PCMU and Opus only (C041); auto mode assigns Opus=255 and PCMU=254 (C042).
tickets.instrumentation: Add tracing::warn! on non-success PJSUA status at the FFI boundary. Expose a counter for CallMediaStateChanged events with their mapped media status.
tickets.investigation: ffi/bindings.rs:110-134 defines a minimal pjsua_call_info mirror containing only conf_slot and a stub pjsua_call_get_info that writes conf_slot = call_id and returns PJ_SUCCESS — canned values; its tests assert the canned behavior (conf_slot must match call_id). m20_native_event_conv.rs:104-113 handles NativeEvent::CallMediaStateChanged by calling convert_call_media_state(cid, 1) — media_status hardcoded to 1 (ACTIVE) because the real pjsua_call_get_info is not wired. runtime/backend.rs:287+ defines PjsuaBackend (derives Default) whose SipBackend methods (set_registration, make_call, answer_call, hangup, send_dtmf, configure_codecs, transfer_call, shutdown, conf_connect, conf_disconnect) all return Err(ReactorError::BackendError("... not yet implemented (P4-2)")). A real implementation must gate these on pjsua-native, invoke the bindgen FFI symbols, propagate status codes, and obtain actual media_status for CallMediaStateChanged.

Replace the per-method Err("... not yet implemented (P4-2)") boilerplate in PjsuaBackend with real calls, deleting the stub strings.

tickets.background:
[::INSPECTION_FLAGGED::]
This ticket has been flagged for rejection due to detection of implementation deficiencies, unresolved STUB markers, or other violations. It has been returned for re-implementation. A complete implementation free of all defects, STUB markers, and violations must be achieved in this final implementation round. Complete it this time.

Source ticket P4-2 (Audio Format, IN/OUT PairAligner, Resampler & Codec Policy) specified the audio/media pipeline; the PJSIP → Rust event bridge in src/ffi was left as no-ops. The markers at src/ffi/callback.rs:16 and src/ffi/mod.rs:27 were left as stubs because PJSIP is not yet linked. This work item resolves them by registering all PJSIP callbacks via pjsua_config.cb and enqueuing NativeEvents through the reactor channel.
scope: - src/ffi/callback.rs:16,30,51,74,91,97 — implement on_incoming_call, on_reg_state, on_call_state, on_call_media_state, on_reg_started, on_call_redirected, on_dtmf_digit, on_call_transfer_status as NativeEvent producers
- src/ffi/mod.rs:27 — wire the callback module and expose a register_callbacks entry point that fills pjsua_config.cb

- src/state/m20_native_event_conv.rs — consume the newly produced NativeEvent variants, including the currently-deferred P1/P2 variants (CallTsxStateChanged, CallRedirected, CallTransferStatus, CallReplaced, NatDetected)
- The reactor event channel — the lock-free queue / MPSC that NativeEvents are enqueued onto
- Out of scope: real FFI call sites (P8-20); build detection/linkage (P8-16).
- Impact: every event-driven path (incoming call, registration, call state, media, DTMF, transfer).
testUnit: UT: [Normal] on_incoming_call copies acc_id/call_id into a CallStateChanged NativeEvent without retaining rdata pointers
UT: [Normal] on_reg_state maps (acc_id, is_registering, code) into RegistrationStateChanged carrying the native status code
UT: [Normal] on_call_media_state produces NativeEvent::CallMediaStateChanged
UT: [Boundary] a queue-full enqueue returns a drop signal and increments a loss counter (no block)
UT: [Error] null rdata / reason pointers are handled without dereferencing null, and the event is still enqueued with an empty reason
testIntegration: IT: register_callbacks fills pjsua_config.cb with all callback pointers, and the reactor round-trips a NativeEvent → SipEventPayload for an incoming call.
IT: dtmf_digit and call_redirected events propagate to SipEventPayload without the current deferred-None behavior.
testExceptions: Live PJSIP callback invocation requires a linked PJSIP and a running account/call; unit tests invoke the extern "C" functions directly with synthetic args. The exact pjsua_config.cb field names are bindgen-dependent — the registration helper is asserted for the set of callback pointers, not the C layout.
acceptanceCriteria: 【Happy path】Each PJSIP callback is registered into pjsua_config.cb and, when invoked, enqueues a NativeEvent (on_incoming_call → CallStateChanged, on_reg_state → RegistrationStateChanged, on_call_media_state → CallMediaStateChanged, on_dtmf_digit → DtmfDigit, on_reg_started → RegistrationStarted, on_call_redirected → CallRedirected, on_call_transfer_status → CallTransferStatus).

【Happy path】The enqueue uses only the permitted operations — copy params into a pre-allocated NativeEvent and push on a lock-free queue / MPSC — with no locks, allocation, .await, or PJSUA re-entry (design constraint in callback.rs:6-14).
【Error case】When the queue is full, the enqueue is loss-tolerant (event dropped, counter incremented) — it never blocks the PJSIP real-time thread.

【Edge case】The P1/P2 NativeEvent variants that currently return None in convert_native_event_to_payload (CallTsxStateChanged, CallRedirected, CallTransferStatus, CallReplaced, NatDetected) are now produced by their callbacks and either converted or explicitly deferred with a documented reason.
【Edge case】The stub markers are removed only after the callbacks enqueue real events and the reactor round-trip tests pass.

tickets.notes: Stub sites: src/ffi/callback.rs:16,30,51,74,91,97; src/ffi/mod.rs:27. Depends on P8-16 (pjsua-native / linkage) and the reactor channel. Implementation: (1) add register_callbacks(pjsua_config, channel); (2) implement each callback to enqueue a NativeEvent; (3) use a pre-allocated lock-free queue / MPSC per the design constraints; (4) update convert_native_event_to_payload for the newly produced variants; (5) keep the no-op stub path behind !pjsua-native. Related: P8-20 (FFI call sites), P8-13 (real CallId).
tickets.invariants: Callbacks never allocate, lock, await, or call back into PJSUA (design constraint from callback.rs:6-14). NativeEvent enqueue is loss-tolerant: a full queue drops the event and increments a counter, never blocking. Audio delivery keeps IN/OUT paired by timestamp (C031); codec policy remains PCMU and Opus only (C041); auto mode assigns Opus=255 and PCMU=254 (C042).
tickets.instrumentation: Add a monotonic counter for enqueued NativeEvents and a separate counter for dropped events on queue-full. tracing::debug! on callback entry with call_id/acc_id only (no payload copy).
tickets.investigation: ffi/callback.rs declares #[no_mangle] unsafe extern "C" callbacks — on_incoming_call (:16), on_reg_state (:30), on_call_state (:51), on_call_media_state (:74), plus on_reg_started / on_call_redirected / on_dtmf_digit / on_call_transfer_status (covers :91,97 per the marker) — each currently discards its arguments (let _ = (...)): pure no-ops. The design-constraint comment (callback.rs:6-14) mandates copying event params into a pre-allocated NativeEvent and enqueueing on a lock-free queue or MPSC channel. ffi/mod.rs:27 documents the callback module; there is no register_callbacks entry point yet. m20_native_event_conv.rs declares the NativeEvent variants (RegistrationStateChanged, RegistrationStarted, CallStateChanged, CallMediaStateChanged, DtmfDigit, plus P1/P2 TransportStateChanged, IceTransportError, CallTsxStateChanged, CallRedirected, CallTransferStatus, CallReplaced, NatDetected) but convert_native_event_to_payload returns None for the P1/P2 variants. The real implementation must (1) register the callbacks in pjsua_config.cb, (2) enqueue NativeEvents via a lock-free / MPSC channel, (3) let the reactor drain and convert, and (4) decide P1/P2 conversion or document deferral.
tickets.boyScoutPlan: Remove the let _ = (...) no-op bodies and replace them with a shared enqueue_native_event helper used by every callback (single source of truth for the lock-free enqueue). Delete the stale doc comments claiming the callbacks are no-ops. Ensure the channel is pre-allocated at registration time to honor the no-allocation rule.

Source ticket P4-2 specified the foundational audio primitives: AudioFormat/AudioChunkPair (model/audio_format_chunkpair.rs), PairAligner (model/audio_aligner.rs), ResamplePipeline (model/audio_resampler.rs), and NegotiatedCodec/CodecSelectionPolicy (config/codec_policy_fallback.rs). The audio/ module was commented out in src/lib.rs:64-66 because those format types were not yet stable. This work item uncomments the audio/ module and implements higher-level audio orchestration that composes the model/ primitives into a usable pipeline.
scope: - src/lib.rs - uncomment `pub mod audio;` (line 66) and remove the P8-23 stub at line 64
- src/audio/ (new) - higher-level audio orchestration module: mod.rs plus orchestration submodules
- src/model/audio_format_chunkpair.rs - reuse AudioFormat, AudioChunk, AudioChunkPair, SampleRate, BitDepth, ChannelLayout (read-only)
- src/model/audio_aligner.rs - reuse PairAligner/TimedFrame
- src/model/audio_resampler.rs - reuse ResamplePipeline, interleave_in_out
- src/config/codec_policy_fallback.rs - reuse NegotiatedCodec, CodecSelectionPolicy
- Out of scope: FFI audio capture/playback (P8-26 / P3-2 FFI), AudioMixer/process_frame internals (P3-2), cpal device I/O (P8-7).
- Impact: new audio/ module compiled and linked; lib.rs module graph gains the audio submodule.
testUnit: UT: [C031] AudioFormat all 64 valid combinations construct; invalid frame_ms returns Err.
UT: [C036] PairAligner within-tolerance pairing returns (in,out); over-tolerance drops the earlier frame and zero-pads.
UT: [C037] ResamplePipeline 48kHz->16kHz resample yields correct output dimensions; stereo L=IN, R=OUT.
UT: [C041] CodecSelectionPolicy::PreferOpusFallbackPcmu resolves Opus first, falls back to PCMU.
UT: [C042] Auto-mode codec id assignment: Opus=255, PCMU=254, others=0.
UT: [Normal] Orchestration module re-exports exist (compile-time).
UT: [Edge] Empty AudioChunk::I16 flows through the pipeline.
UT: [Error] Invalid AudioFormat is rejected by the orchestration entry point with AudioFormatError.
testIntegration: IT: [Pipeline] Feed a stereo 48kHz frame through the audio/ orchestration API end-to-end (align -> resample -> policy) and verify the OUT buffer length and channel mapping.
IT: [Module-graph] cargo check succeeds with `pub mod audio;` uncommented and all re-exports resolving.
testExceptions: Actual rubato resampling fidelity/performance requires the rubato native crate, which is verified by dependency build, not unit assertions.
FFI capture/playback (RustMediaPort get_frame/put_frame) is out of scope; the orchestration layer is tested with in-memory AudioChunk buffers.
acceptanceCriteria: 【Happy path】src/audio/ compiles with `pub mod audio;` uncommented; the module re-exports the orchestration API and composes AudioFormat, AudioChunkPair, PairAligner, ResamplePipeline, and CodecSelectionPolicy.

【Happy path】A full IN/OUT pipeline run (align -> resample -> codec policy) on a valid 48kHz stereo frame produces output matching the source invariants (stereo L=IN, R=OUT; IN/OUT paired by timestamp).
【Happy path】The orchestration layer propagates zero-padding from PairAligner when a pair exceeds tolerance, without panicking.
【Error case】Orchestration with an invalid AudioFormat (e.g., frame_ms outside {10,20,40,60}) returns a typed error (AudioFormatError); no partial/inconsistent AudioFormat is constructed.
【Error case】Codec policy fallback with no mutually supported codec returns an error (e.g., MediaNegotiationFailed), never panics.
【Edge case】AudioChunk::I16 with an empty Vec<i16> flows through the orchestration pipeline (valid edge state, len=0).

tickets.title: DTMF Specification, AsyncAudioSource & Incoming Call/Transfer

contracts.precondition: Call API supports DTMF — pjsua_call_dial_dtmf() can be called with valid native_call_id and digit string; AccountConfig::validate() rejects empty DtmfPolicy::send_methods or receive_methods
contracts.postcondition: DTMF specification defined — DtmfMethod enum has variants for Inband, SipInfo (Info), Rfc4733; DtmfReceivedInfo struct contains method:DtmfMethod, digit:char, duration_ms:Option<u16>, volume_dbm0:Option<i8>; data types implement Clone + Debug
contracts.invariant: 3 DTMF method categories: Inband (RFC 2833 in-band tone), SIP INFO (SipInfo in Info variant), RFC 4733 (out-of-band RTP event). DtmfPolicy always has at least one send_method and one receive_method — validated in AccountConfig::validate().

contracts.precondition: DTMF spec defined — DtmfMethod, DtmfReceivedInfo, DtmfPolicy types exist in the crate; DtmfSent event variant exists in SipEventPayload
contracts.postcondition: DtmfSentInfo and two-phase design — DtmfSentInfo { method, digit, status: Result<(), SentDtmfError>, pjsip_status } defined; send_dtmf() returns Ok(()) synchronously for command acceptance; DtmfSent event fires asynchronously on completion or timeout
contracts.invariant: 500ms default timeout (DEFAULT_DTMF_SENT_TIMEOUT_MS) for DtmfSent fallback when PJSIP callback unavailable; configurable via DtmfConfig::sent_timeout_ms

contracts.precondition: Audio subscribe uses sources — AudioMixer stores Box<dyn AsyncAudioSource+Send>; AsyncAudioSource trait defined with async fn next_chunk(&mut self, buf: &mut [i16]) -> usize
contracts.postcondition: AsyncAudioSource trait with RPITIT — async fn next_chunk in trait definition (currently #[async_trait] desugaring). ErasedAudioSource blanket impl auto-derived for all T: AsyncAudioSource + Send. SyncAudioSource trait and SyncSourceAdapter<T: SyncAudioSource + Send> provided for synchronous sources.
contracts.invariant: ErasedAudioSource auto-derived for every AsyncAudioSource implementor — blanket impl <T: AsyncAudioSource + Send> ErasedAudioSource for T must compile. SyncSourceAdapter<T: SyncAudioSource + Send> must implement AsyncAudioSource + Send.

contracts.precondition: Call API defined — IncomingCallInfo, ReferRequest, TransferInfo event types exist in SipEventPayload; CallEntry state machine creates entries on incoming INVITE
contracts.postcondition: IncomingCall struct { from_uri, to_uri, display_name, headers, offered_codecs, has_early_media } defined; optional auto-reject timer configurable in account config; ReferRequest { refer_to, referred_by, replaces? } creation from SIP REFER; blind transfer NOTIFY → TransferCompleted event
contracts.invariant: Blind transfer (REFER without Replaces header) is first-class — ReferRequest::replaces is Option; transfer completion always emits TransferCompleted event via NOTIFY subscription state

tickets.background:
[::INSPECTION_FLAGGED::]
This ticket has been flagged by the ABC Inspection Pipeline after completing the implementation lifecycle (make → plan → start → review → resolve). The actual source code was rigorously analyzed against three criteria:

  A — Contract Translation:   Are all Precondition/Postcondition/Invariant contracts accurately translated into test code?
  B — Violation Detection:    Can every contract violation be detected by an existing test assertion?
  C — Test Precision:         Are tests precise and unambiguous (no broad assertions, no missing edge cases)?

One or more ABC violations were confirmed. This ticket is hereby remanded for re-implementation. Every violation must be fully resolved, and every contract must be fulfilled in this final implementation round. Complete it this time.

- 【Goal】Define and implement the DTMF specification (DtmfMethod, DtmfReceivedInfo with the method:DtmfMethod field and contract-correct Option<u16>/Option<i8> field types), the AsyncAudioSource adapter types (ErasedAudioSource, SyncAudioSource, SyncSourceAdapter<T>), and the IncomingCall / REFER-transfer types (IncomingCall, IncomingCallConfig, ReferRequest.replaces, TransferInfo) per RFC nodes N0028 / N0032 / N0048. Close the 4 ABC inspection omissions (O-001..O-004) and resolve the TS-003 orphan-ticket crime in src/config/versioning_policy.rs so the ticket survives a full make → plan → start → review → resolve cycle this time.
- 【Purpose】Provide type-safe DTMF signalling primitives for SIP call control (send + receive with DtmfPolicy validation). Enable downstream crates to implement custom async audio sources for AudioMixer via the SyncAudioSource → SyncSourceAdapter bridge and the ErasedAudioSource dynamic-dispatch wrapper. Expose incoming call metadata (from_uri, to_uri, display_name, headers, offered_codecs, has_early_media) and REFER-based transfer capabilities (ReferRequest.replaces, TransferCompleted) to application code as typed SipEventPayload variants.
- 【Motivation】The ABC Inspection Pipeline remanded P8-4 with one critical omission (O-001: ReferRequest.replaces missing and zero tests construct ReferRequest/TransferInfo, so the C049 invariant and acceptance criteria are unenforced), one major (O-002: DtmfReceivedInfo.duration_ms widened to Option<u64> and volume_dbm0 to Option<i32> vs the contract Option<u16>/Option<i8>, and no None/0/MAX edge tests), and two minor (O-003: no SipEventPayload::DtmfSent construction test; O-004: no 65536-sample SyncAudioSource boundary test). The versioning_policy.rs STUB (TS-003) is an orphaned ticket reference that must be resolved this round. Every contract (C029/C030/C033/C049) must be translated into precise test assertions so that removing any contract behavior fails a test.
- 【Constraints】MSRV 1.95 — RPITIT is stable but the existing AsyncAudioSource uses #[async_trait] for Box<dyn> compatibility in AudioMixer; the ErasedAudioSource blanket impl provides the dynamic-dispatch path without refactoring existing implementors. Do NOT add new crate dependencies — all required derives (Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq) are std. Keep the canonical 4-variant DtmfMethod (Rfc2833, Rfc4733, Info, Inband) from account_config_spec.rs; leave the separate 2-variant DtmfMethod in m20_dtmfsent_twophase.rs intact to avoid breaking DtmfSentInfo consumers (unification is an open item, not a forced change). Maintain backward compatibility with existing DtmfReceivedInfo consumers (m20_native_event_conv.rs constructs with None/None, so field-type narrowing is compatible). ReferRequest gains the additive replaces: Option<String> field; all struct-literal construction sites must add it.
scope: Changes (path): src/api/event_model_payload_bus.rs (MODIFY) — narrow DtmfReceivedInfo.duration_ms to Option<u16> and volume_dbm0 to Option<i8>; add ReferRequest.replaces: Option<String>; add payload-construction and edge/boundary tests. src/api/asyncaudiosrc_adapter.rs (MODIFY) — add the 65536-sample SyncAudioSource/SyncSourceAdapter boundary test; update the open_default_microphone_source STUB marker. src/config/versioning_policy.rs (MODIFY) — implement VersionPolicy per N0006 §4.1 and remove the TS-003 STUB marker. src/state/m20_native_event_conv.rs (VERIFY) — DtmfReceivedInfo construction still compiles after type narrowing.

Changes (action): 1) Change DtmfReceivedInfo field types to the contract types. 2) Add ReferRequest.replaces field. 3) Add the missing event-payload construction tests and boundary tests. 4) Implement VersionPolicy (semver phase classification, CHANGELOG requirement, 1.0+ MAJOR/MINOR/PATCH semantics) with a #[cfg(test)] module. 5) Re-scope the microphone-source STUB to MUST RESOLVE with the cpal-dependency constraint reason.

Changes (detail): DtmfReceivedInfo { method: DtmfMethod, digit: char, duration_ms: Option<u16>, volume_dbm0: Option<i8> } (was Option<u64>/Option<i32>). ReferRequest { call_id: CallId, refer_to: String, referred_by: Option<String>, replaces: Option<String> }. VersionPolicy type in src/config/versioning_policy.rs implementing the N0006 §4.1 rules (0.x CHANGELOG-based breaking changes; 1.0+ MAJOR = breaking / MINOR = additive / PATCH = bugfix; security-fix PATCH exception). New tests: payload_dtmf_sent, payload_refer_received, payload_transfer_completed, dtmf_received_info_none_edge, dtmf_received_info_duration_boundary, dtmf_received_info_volume_boundary, refer_request_blind, refer_request_full, transfer_info_fields, sync_source_adapter_65536_buffer, version_policy_0x_and_10x.

Changes (before/after): BEFORE — DtmfReceivedInfo.duration_ms: Option<u64>, volume_dbm0: Option<i32>; ReferRequest { call_id, refer_to, referred_by }; versioning_policy.rs holds only a doc comment + STUB; no DtmfSent/ReferReceived/TransferCompleted payload tests. AFTER — duration_ms: Option<u16>, volume_dbm0: Option<i8>; ReferRequest gains replaces: Option<String>; VersionPolicy implemented with tests and the STUB marker removed; payload_* tests assert each event variant; the 65536-sample buffer boundary is covered.

Changes (API): DtmfReceivedInfo field types narrow (Option<u64> → Option<u16>, Option<i32> → Option<i8>) — a type-level change affecting struct-literal construction sites (only m20_native_event_conv.rs today, None-compatible). ReferRequest gains the additive replaces: Option<String> field. VersionPolicy is a new public type in the config domain. No changes to the AsyncAudioSource / ErasedAudioSource / SyncAudioSource / SyncSourceAdapter signatures (already present from P5-2/P0-6).
Changes (schema): None — pure Rust API types; no serialization, DB, or wire-format changes. DtmfConfig::sent_timeout_ms and IncomingCallConfig already exist (P7-2 / P5-2) and are untouched.

Changes (config): No AccountConfig or ClientConfig changes required for the P8-4 core scope. versioning_policy.rs is a standalone config-domain module (N0006) implemented independently of account/client config to avoid entanglement.

Changes (dep): No new crate dependencies. All derives (Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq) are std. VersionPolicy uses only std. The microphone source stays behind the cpal-input feature gate because adding the cpal crate is prohibited by the ticket constraint.

Non-change (item): PJSIP FFI callback wiring (on_dtmf_digit / on_incoming_call / on_refer) and the Reactor event dispatch — separate P5-3 ticket. RPITIT refactoring of the existing #[async_trait] AsyncAudioSource — deferred. Attended transfer end-to-end (REFER with Replaces targeting a live call) — depends on the multi-call state machine, P5-3+. Unification of the 2-variant DtmfMethod with the 4-variant canonical — open item, not forced.

Non-change (why): The P8-4 scope is the pure type definitions + test assertions that close the ABC gaps. FFI wiring needs a live PJSIP stack; RPITIT refactor risks the working AudioMixer integration; attended transfer needs multi-call semantics; DtmfMethod unification would break DtmfSentInfo consumers (P7-2 tests). Each is a separate, larger change better owned by a dedicated ticket.

Impact (component): src/api/event_model_payload_bus.rs — event payload structs (DtmfReceivedInfo, ReferRequest) + SipEventPayload variants. src/config/versioning_policy.rs — new VersionPolicy type (additive). src/api/asyncaudiosrc_adapter.rs — test-only change + STUB re-scope. src/state/m20_native_event_conv.rs — DtmfReceivedInfo construction (None-compatible). runtime/audio_worker consumers — ErasedAudioSource blanket impl adds an impl boundary with zero migration cost.

Impact (nature): API surface expansion (additive: replaces field, VersionPolicy) + field-type narrowing (minor breaking for DtmfReceivedInfo literal constructors). Existing Default implementations and None-construction paths remain compatible. No behavioral change to event dispatch.

Impact (response): Downstream crates constructing DtmfReceivedInfo must pass Option<u16>/Option<i8> values (u64/i32 literals beyond the range fail to compile — intended, enforces the boundary invariant). ReferRequest constructors must add replaces: Option<String>. VersionPolicy is additive with no consumer impact.

tickets.boyScoutPlan:
Translatability improvement plan (Boy Scout Rule — leave code cleaner than found):
- Function names as verb phrases: DtmfPolicy::is_send_allowed / is_receive_allowed already read as verbs — keep. VersionPolicy methods must be verbs: classify_change(), requires_changelog(), current_phase() — never generic names like process() or check().
- Variable names as domain concepts: DtmfReceivedInfo fields already use SIP domain terms (method, digit, duration_ms, volume_dbm0). ReferRequest.replaces is the domain term for the Replaces header — no generic option. VersionPolicy must name the semver concepts (phase, change_kind, changelog) not raw strings.
- One function one responsibility: VersionPolicy::classify_change answers only "what kind of change" — CHANGELOG gating is a separate method requires_changelog(). Do not merge classification with release automation.
- Hardcoded values as named constants: DEFAULT_AUTO_REJECT_TIMEOUT_MS (incoming_call_refer.rs:36) and DEFAULT_DTMF_SENT_TIMEOUT_MS (m20_dtmfsent_twophase.rs:64) already exist — keep. Any new versioning thresholds become named constants in versioning_policy.rs.
- No error swallowing: AccountConfig::validate errors propagate via ?. spawn_dtmf_sent_timeout publishes errors on the EventBus instead of log-and-continue. VersionPolicy returns typed errors for invalid classifications.
- Proactive cleanups in touched files: update the stale [::STUB::] P0-1 reference in versioning_policy.rs (resolved by implementation); re-scope the microphone STUB to MUST RESOLVE with the cpal constraint reason instead of leaving a misleading P8-4 reference that would later read as a completed-ticket staleness crime; in event_model_payload_bus.rs, align the DtmfReceivedInfo doc comment with the narrowed Option<u16>/Option<i8> types and add the replaces field doc to ReferRequest.

Any future addition of video types would fail the compile-time invariant tests defined in testUnit. This is NOT an architectural defect — the RFC deliberately scopes to audio-only, and the type system enforces this at compile time. Exception: SipClient::new returning Result is a type-level invariant, cannot test as individual runtime assertion — Reason: The function signature SipClient::new(config: ClientConfig) -> Result<(Self, Receiver<SipEvent>), SipError> is enforced by the Rust compiler at compile time — every caller must handle both Ok and Err. The Err branch IS tested in testUnit for invalid config. Alternative verification: compile_fail tests in testUnit cover the error path at the type level. This is NOT an architectural defect — returning Result from fallible operations is idiomatic Rust design.

Exception: All public async fn signatures returning Result<T, SipError> cannot test individually at runtime — Reason: This architectural invariant is enforced by the Rust compiler and verified by compile-time tests in testUnit. Runtime testing of each method's specific error return path requires downstream tickets (P0-4 for SipError variants, P0-5 for event types, P0-6 for FFI integration). This ticket establishes the convention and verifies it at compile time. This is not a defect — this is a deliberate design choice for the facade layer.

**Exception entry — CoreReactor::spawn is the single reactor-thread factory**
- [Item] The invariant "exactly one reactor thread exists per SipClient, created only via `CoreReactor::spawn`" **cannot test** as a single runtime assertion: other code could spawn additional threads, and the reactor thread terminates on shutdown, so a liveness check alone cannot assert exclusivity.
- [Reason] This is a crate-wide *structural* property, not a single-function behavior. A runtime test can observe the reactor it spawns (`JoinHandle`, `is_terminated`) but cannot observe threads created elsewhere. This is **not testable** as one assertion, yet it is NOT an architectural defect: the thread *factory* is fully testable (O-004 type assertion + `"siprs-reactor"` thread name), and only the exclusivity of the factory is a source-review property. Stating it is "not a defect" because the testable part is fully covered by testUnit.
- [Alternative verification] (1) O-004 closure: `let _: std::thread::JoinHandle<()> = join;` in `reactor_spawn_creates_thread` proves `spawn` uses `std::thread`. (2) `make stubs` / source review enforces that `thread::Builder`/`thread::spawn` appear only in `src/runtime/reactor.rs`. (3) Integration tests join the `JoinHandle` and assert `is_terminated()` to prove the reactor thread lifecycle.
acceptanceCriteria: [Happy path] SipClient::new is called with a valid ClientConfig — returns Ok(SipClient) with initialized CoreReactor. All five module declarations (client, config, account, call, transport) are active in lib.rs. SipClient::shutdown() terminates cleanly. The compile-time invariant tests pass (no video types, all APIs return Result, SipClient is Send+Sync).
[Error case] SipClient::new is called with empty sip_proxy_host — returns Err(SipError::InvalidConfig("sip_proxy_host must not be empty")). CoreReactor is NOT spawned. No orphaned resources.

[Edge case] SipClient::shutdown() is called twice — first call succeeds (returns Ok(())), second call is a no-op (also returns Ok(()), verifying C044: Shutdown is idempotent). Calling any method after shutdown returns Err(SipError::Shutdown).

**[Happy path] — Crate identity complete; all invariant tests green**
- `make test` passes: 647+ unit, 37+ integration, doc-tests — all green, zero warnings.
- `SipClient::new(valid ClientConfig)` returns `Ok((SipClient, broadcast::Receiver<SipEvent>))`; `client.is_terminated() == false`; `client.handle()` exposes a live `RuntimeHandle`.
- `SipClient::shutdown()` returns `Ok(())` and terminates the reactor within 5s.
- `src/lib.rs` declares all RFC §6 modules as `pub mod` (client, config, account, call, transport, event, error, runtime, api, state, ffi, security, build, tests, model).
- All four ABC closures pass: O-001 `assert_sync::<SipClient>()`, O-002 `manifest.contains("metrics")`, O-003 `features_independently_selectable`, O-004 `let _: std::thread::JoinHandle<()> = join;`.

**[Error case] — Invalid configuration rejected; no orphaned resources**
- `SipClient::new` with empty `sip_proxy_host` returns `Err(SipError)` with `kind == SipErrorKind::InvalidConfig` and message containing "empty".
- `sip_proxy_port(0)` and `user_agent` > 256 bytes are likewise rejected by `ClientConfig::validate()`.
- On construction failure the reactor is NOT spawned: no `siprs-reactor` thread leaks, no command-channel resources remain, and no half-constructed `SipClient` is observable (the `Err` path returns before `Self` is built).

**[Edge case] — Idempotent shutdown and boundary values**
- `shutdown()` called twice: both return `Ok(())`; the second is a no-op (C044 invariant).
- `sip_proxy_port(65535)` (max `u16`) accepted; `0` rejected; 256-byte `user_agent` accepted; 257-byte rejected.
- `subscribe_raw_sip()` returns `None` when raw SIP is disabled, `Some(receiver)` when enabled — the Option boundary is exercised both ways.
- Feature boundary: `metrics`, `cpal-input`, `zeroize` are each selectable without being in `default = [...]`; `tls` and `srtp` are independently selectable (C003 invariant).
